entries.title: Flower startup and recovery presentation
entries.description: Keep navigation and drafts available while the single readiness owner prepares, stops or restores Flower.
entries.summary: Env App/Desktop project one owner's readiness and typed Stop/Retry while retaining navigation and drafts. Close failure requires restart; unknown or contradictory facts are non-retryable contract failures. No surface adds an availability controller. First content admits the workspace; later refresh/reconnect retains mounted conversation state.

entries.title: Flower persistent-index startup acceptance
entries.description: Record isolated Floret v7.52.0 and complete product activation measurements on the 710 MB conversation fixture.
entries.summary:
On the isolated 710,344,704-byte database with 219 threads, complete Redeven
construction plus activation reached a nearest-rank P95 of **9.429 seconds** over
20 sequential process runs. Published Floret v7.52.0 retained at most **261.052 MiB**
of GC-live heap; the entire product retained at most **295.018 MiB**. Both fixture
acceptance targets (P95 <=10 seconds and Floret idle heap <=350 MiB) passed.
These are dataset-specific measurements, not universal startup guarantees.

entries.title: Flower conversation switch performance qualification
entries.description: Reproduce point-read scaling, bounded read recovery and actual sidebar presentation with synthetic data.
entries.summary:
Published Floret v7.87.3 owns windows, bounded item-text reads, View and Summary. Redeven owns
bounded reads and presentation through the [sidebar](../ui/flower-thread-sidebar.md)
and [Desktop bridge](../desktop/desktop-runtime-bridge.md). Local qualification
targets >=70% lower short-detail P95, warm synchronous P95 <8 ms, and feedback
before commit. Fixtures never continue real user tasks.

entries.title: Flower conversation selection and detail reads
entries.description: Present navigation feedback before committing content and coordinate bounded canonical detail reads.
entries.summary:
Flower acknowledges navigation before transcript work. One coordinator serves
navigation, command confirmation and reference preflight. ThreadCache owns
selection and detail; the loader owns bounded ephemeral demand.
Readiness controls reveal; elapsed time controls feedback only.

entries.title: Control-plane capacity qualification
entries.description: Measure ten thousand enrolled Runtime control sessions with real authority, recovery, and signed Gateway requests.
entries.summary: Control-plane capacity qualification measures ten thousand enrolled Runtime sessions through real Nginx/TLS, MySQL, and canonical authority decisions. The harness uses production heartbeats, signed Gateway observations, and credential recovery. A full acceptance result combines client latency and recovery counts with independent server CPU, RSS, database, queue, and challenge-backlog measurements.

entries.title: Tessiven DSL versioning
entries.description: Select exact frozen DSL schemas and migrate supported documents without rewriting history.
entries.summary:
The Runtime owns Tessiven DSL schema selection and explicit forward migrations.
New documents use `apiVersion: redeven.io/tessiven/v1.1.0`. Supported legacy
`redeven.io/tessiven/v1` and `v1.0.0` remain readable through the reviewed
`v1 -> v1.0.0 -> v1.1.0` chain. Each edge updates only the version scalar;
new group packing rules are opt-in and older documents retain automatic layout. Reads project current structured data while preserving historical YAML,
digest and revision identity. Authorized edits save a new current snapshot.
Unknown versions, invalid source/target documents or migration failures leave
stored data intact; users need a compatible Runtime or a valid repair.

entries.title: Tessiven stable canvas presentation
entries.description: Render validated canvas data through an independently frozen client display contract.
entries.summary:
The Runtime interprets the current Tessiven DSL and projects a frozen,
data-only `redeven.io/tessiven-presentation/v1` display model. Native clients
render that model using bundled code. A DSL release does not by itself change
the display format or require a client release. Historical YAML, its digest,
revision identity, write validation and operation authority stay unchanged.
An unsupported source retains verified source for viewing and export but does
not invent topology. Integrity failure returns an error without an exportable
source. No response supplies executable renderer code.

entries.title: Tessiven canvas contract
entries.description: Store immutable service canvases in one Runtime-owned library.
entries.summary:
Tessiven is the Runtime-owned library of immutable service canvases. Each
canvas stores a complete `redeven.io/tessiven/v1.1.0` YAML document and every save
creates a new version. The Runtime is the single owner of canvas data; the
Desktop Welcome surface and the local Env App render that same library. A
failed validation or version conflict leaves the last saved document intact.

entries.title: Native Runtime bridge
entries.description: SSH placement for native clients without Desktop management or Runtime startup authority.
entries.summary: `redeven native-bridge --state-root PATH` attaches a native client to the already running Runtime selected by that state root. The owner-only management socket is the attachment authority. The command carries `redeven-native-runtime-h2/1` over stdio and exposes only the fixed `native-runtime` CONNECT surface. Missing, inaccessible, stopped, or incompatible runtimes fail without installation, startup, address fallback, or Desktop credentials. Disconnecting releases this client's bridge and sessions, never the Runtime process.

entries.title: Flower working files and deliverables
entries.description: Thread-owned intermediate files, canonical delivery references, authorized downloads and safe cleanup.
entries.summary:
Flower keeps intermediate files under the Runtime's application state and final
files at the user's destination. Redeven owns filesystem policy, bytes and UI;
published Floret owns tool results and conversation identities. No artifact
index, duplicated transcript, new Floret API or domain migration is introduced.

entries.title: Flower browser source ownership
entries.description: Admit browser targets for Flower while preserving native identity and private control boundaries.
entries.summary:
- Authority: ComputerUseRuntime authorizes target selection and control; its browser source Host owns admitted CDP and extension adapters.
- Outcome: Flower can discover, connect to, automate, observe, take over and return control of managed or explicitly selected browser tabs.
- Invariants: discovery never grants input; each admitted page has one debugger and ordered input path; private opener ancestry remains hidden across CDP and extension inventories.
- Failure boundary: source loss retires only affected target bindings. Unknown input outcomes are never replayed, and a failed source Host cannot silently create replacement authority.

entries.title: Flower browser Linux preparation
entries.description: Prepare a separate persistent Linux browser application for Flower connection.
entries.summary:
- Authority: Runtime owns installation discovery and Native Messaging registration; Host Applications owns the prepared application and its graphical lifecycle.
- Outcome: Flower's connection guide can prepare a separate persistent Linux Chrome or Chromium profile without launching it or granting a browser target.
- Invariants: clients submit only an installation ID, never paths or launch arguments; personal profiles and existing website data remain untouched.
- Failure boundary: unsupported platforms, absent installations and unsafe profile directories fail before launch. Preparation cannot claim a successful connection.

entries.title: Database schema migration ownership
entries.description: Redeven automatically migrates product databases at startup while upstream-owned stores remain opaque.
entries.summary:
- Authority: each repository migrates the schemas it owns; Redeven owns product databases, while Floret and ReDevPlugin own their internal stores.
- Outcome: each Redeven product store opens through an exact versioned schema contract before the dependent service accepts requests.
- Invariants: released migration lineages are contiguous, atomic, verified, and data-preserving; existing-file preflight reads the complete SQLite main-plus-WAL view, while future, drifted, wrong-kind, and unsupported inputs fail without changing database files or sidecars.
- Failure boundary: a failed migration stops the affected service with the previous supported database intact; Redeven never patches an upstream database or silently replaces an incompatible product database.

entries.title: AI readiness and service generation lifecycle
entries.description: Keep Code App available while a process-local controller serializes AI startup, retry, and request-scoped service generations.
entries.summary: Floret owns durable Agent/Store facts; Redeven's single process-local readiness controller owns AI construction, retry, publication, request leases, drain and close. Non-AI surfaces remain usable through startup/migration/recovery. Requests use one generation. Unavailable startup returns sanitized typed state without publishing a partial service, repairing Store data or creating durable Agent state.

entries.title: Runtime startup presentation
entries.description: redeven run startup output is structured events rendered by rich, plain, or machine presentation modes.
entries.summary: `redeven run` startup is modeled as a lifecycle event stream. Human terminal output and public machine events are renderers over the same state snapshot, while a separate private Desktop report carries machine-only attach data and stable failure codes needed to open or recover the local Env App safely.

entries.title: Observation and target action events
entries.description: Publish computer and browser action progress through the canonical Flower workspace stream while keeping media ephemeral and target-scoped.
entries.summary: Target actions are ordinary Flower tool observations. The workspace stream remains the only lifecycle and replay channel; screenshot descriptors are canonical keyframes, while short-lived live frames are target-scoped media and may be dropped without changing thread state.

entries.title: Local UI surface
entries.description: Local UI serves browser entrypoints, access-gated APIs, direct sessions, Env App proxying, codespaces, and port forwards.
entries.summary: Redeven Local UI is the Runtime-owned client endpoint. Desktop and browsers can connect concurrently using independent access sessions. Public HTTP/WS or HTTPS/WSS shares one configured port; authenticated Desktop bridge traffic remains on its separate numeric-loopback listener and isolated `flowersec-private-loopback/1` profile. The versioned SQLite authority store is the sole issuer-side source for one-shot Flowersec authorization and browser spend state across all transports. [Local UI network exposure](../security/local-ui-network-exposure.md) owns protocol choice, scope, password, certificate, and migration rules.

entries.title: Env App session event transport
entries.description: Observe Env App events through the current authenticated session without consuming browser HTTP connection slots.
entries.summary: Floe Webapp owns one HTTP proxy runtime per connected Env App session. All built-in browser event subscriptions and the ReDevPlugin host request adapter use that runtime's logical streams. They cannot occupy native HTTP/1.1 connection slots, choose another upstream or identity, or create a second transport. Session replacement and teardown cancel old observations. Each feature retains its existing recovery policy; stopping observation never cancels background business work.

entries.title: Activity navigation restoration
entries.description: Restore one locally saved Activity target before startup work and recover unavailable dynamic pages without stealing navigation.
entries.summary:
Redeven owns exactly one versioned Activity navigation record. It selects the
saved target before the first page mounts, commits valid navigation immediately,
and remembers a unique recency order of built-in pages. Floe persists layout
sizes and collapse state but does not read or write the active tab. Invalid
dynamic targets fall back to the latest available built-in page, or Terminal.
A transient directory failure preserves the original saved target for a future
startup or explicit retry; a late restoration never replaces user navigation.

entries.title: Env App resource snapshots
entries.description: Restore authorized local presentation snapshots while refreshing Host Applications, Containers, Web Services, and Codespaces.
entries.summary:
The published Floe resource cache owns disposable snapshot restoration, request
coalescing, response fencing, persistence, and capacity eviction. Redeven owns
identity confirmation and explicit presentation projections. Host Applications,
Containers, Web Services, and Codespaces show their most recent successful inventory while
fetching current facts. Refresh changes only the existing refresh icon during
normal operation. Cached facts never authorize an operation. A permission denial
or locked access clears the affected presentation; ordinary connectivity failure
retains it with the existing error and retry affordance.

entries.title: Env App page loading continuity
entries.description: Apply one initial-loading and refresh policy across Activity pages and Workbench widgets.
entries.summary: One product presentation registry declares initial loading and reload eligibility for every built-in Activity page and Workbench widget. Modules load inside their own surface, preserving existing successful content. Data services own readiness; access/authentication changes override retention, and loading never grants permission.

entries.title: Env App document reload presentation
entries.description: Bridge document reload before modules execute and hand off once to the selected authorized inventory.
entries.summary:
Published Floe owns the anonymous geometry placeholder spanning a full document
reload. Redeven's Shell owns its handoff to the selected Activity inventory.
Reload must not paint an empty root, reveal a differently shaped list skeleton,
or replace restored content with another loading state. Geometry is never
resource data or authorization. Explicit access denial, navigation, an actionable
error, or changed authentication ends the placeholder instead of hiding recovery.
Unavailable presentation storage must not prevent normal startup.

entries.title: Web Services interface
entries.description: Read current service facts, open services, and resolve exceptions in compact Activity and Workbench surfaces.
entries.summary:
The shared Web Services interface presents the service identity, current backend status, available action, and supporting facts in that order. Activity and Workbench use the same collection and management drawer. Content must remain readable and actionable at narrow surface widths, with long translations and enlarged text. Historical failures cannot replace observed state. Failed checks preserve previously loaded facts with a visible explanation; unavailable actions retain an actionable inspection path within existing permissions.

Local inventory continuity follows [Env App resource snapshots](../ui/env-resource-cache.md); presentation restoration grants no lifecycle or route authority.

entries.title: Web Service browser sessions
entries.description: Address-first Web Service opening, ephemeral forward lifecycle, and isolated Desktop browsing.
entries.summary: Web Services accepts ports or HTTP(S) deep links to the current Environment's loopback and opens them through authorized forwarding. Other targets fail before session/window creation. Registry-owned `access_mode` selects secure `unified_proxy` or HTTP-only Desktop `desktop_loopback`; heuristics and failures cannot override it. Stale windows, mismatched routes, invalid modes and expired temporary forwards fail closed.

entries.title: Managed host application preparation
entries.description: Compatible installed components, independent user-directed updates, incremental transfer and same-window first-use preparation.
entries.summary: Published Floe Native Apps owns Linux component acquisition, verification, staging, self-check and activation. Redeven owns authorized routes, private placement, localized progress and pending app opening. Preparation needs no container, VM, package manager or admin password. Runtime upgrades remain independent; compatible installed components survive optional-update failure/cancellation. Activate only after verification and graphical qualification.

entries.title: Human remote desktop sessions
entries.description: Share the host's current graphical desktop with an authenticated viewer, exclusive remote input, and bounded media.
entries.summary:
Redeven owns remote desktop authorization, ephemeral sessions, window placement,
configuration and audit. Published `floe-native-apps` owns current-desktop
selection, OS authorization, native input, capture, codecs, bounded playback and
Linux component acquisition and the privileged physical-desktop service.
A desktop session shares the existing signed-in macOS or Linux desktop. It never
creates an application-private desktop, changes system security policy or grants
access to a lower-permission user. Disconnect releases remote input and media;
host applications and unsaved work survive. Platform unavailability revokes
input and requires a fresh active frame before recovery.

entries.title: Administrator-authorized remote desktop deployment over SSH
entries.description: Install and manage the Linux physical-desktop service from Env App without target-side graphical consent.
entries.summary: Desktop owns SSH authorization and UI-operation lifetime; published Floe Native Apps owns privileged preparation; Runtime owns product authorization, service authentication and audit. Every SSH connection runs ensure, including active older-policy services, and authenticates the actual Runtime before opening. Unknown records remain unchanged. Cancellation reports observed rollback; verified completion may win the race but still suppresses automatic viewer opening.

entries.title: Persistent remote desktop sharing approval
entries.description: Restore approved desktop sharing without conflating saved OS authorization, active sessions, or Runtime startup.
entries.summary: Redeven owns sharing preference/reset; published Floe Native Apps owns OS authorization and private recovery credentials. Logged-in Runtime defaults to reusing first approval, attempting recovery before new consent. Saved credentials are opportunities, never proof of OS admission, and never reach viewers, URLs or audits. This optional user Portal chain is separate from [SSH system-service deployment](remote-desktop-ssh-deployment.md).

entries.title: Remote desktop connection launcher
entries.description: Identify the target host, explain connection readiness and open its desktop through one concise, localized flow.
entries.summary: Env App owns one remote desktop flow in Host Applications/Workbench: identify the host, show readiness and one primary action, then continue authorization in place. [Session policy](remote-desktop.md) enforces platform/permission limits. Failure retains recovery; dismissal before creation finishes releases that session. An opened viewer has an independent lifetime.

entries.title: Flowersec transport for graphical windows
entries.description: Bind every remote desktop and host application data channel to one resource-scoped native Flowersec session in direct and tunnel modes.
entries.summary:
Flowersec owns encryption, carrier selection, multiplexing, proxy framing and
backpressure for remote desktop and host application windows. Redeven owns the
resource, user authorization and route mapping. All graphical data, including
state, attachment tickets, input, clipboard, audio, pixels and explicit disconnect,
uses the published native session proxy. Static program bootstrap and acquisition
remain on the authenticated browser entry. Missing authority fails closed; no
viewer backend may silently open a raw graphical HTTP or WebSocket connection.

entries.title: Graphical window native transport qualification
entries.description: Assess published Flowersec direct and tunnel coverage, Linux application and desktop behavior, and the remaining unlocked macOS qualification.
entries.summary:
The [graphical transport contract](../architecture/graphical-window-transport.md)
passes native direct, real encrypted tunnel, resource-authority and Linux live
checks with published dependencies. Active macOS capture and the Electron
fullscreen portion remain blocked by the host lock screen. Locked-host refusal
passes, but does not qualify an unlocked desktop. These functional checks do not
replace the separate [performance measurement contract](remote-desktop-validation.md).

entries.title: Remote desktop viewer interaction
entries.description: Operate the remote desktop toolbar, input modes and ended-session recovery consistently in browsers and Desktop.
entries.summary:
The Redeven viewer owns product controls and local feedback over published Floe
input and native playback. The [remote desktop session contract](remote-desktop.md)
owns authorization, capture generations and native authority. Only current painted
control permits input. Separate-cursor control frames enable immediate client
pointer movement independently of later frame arrival; embedded-cursor frames
hide the local pointer. Local controls remain usable during recovery. Disconnect
stops local input and playback immediately, then confirms server removal or offers
an explicit retry. It never presents a frozen desktop as a live connection.

entries.title: Remote desktop media and input scheduling
entries.description: Preserve bounded pixel ownership, cursor presentation and ordered input/video while reducing capture and playback work.
entries.summary: Published native components own capture, encoding and playback; Redeven consumes them. [Session authority](remote-desktop.md) owns authorization/generations. Media work is bounded and cursors follow painted pixels. Input admission does not prove host delivery. Capture/input failure retires authority; delayed work cannot overwrite or authorize a successor.

entries.title: Wayland cursor and scheduling optimization evidence
entries.description: Assess separate cursor ownership, ordered nonblocking input and damage-aware capture without confusing synthetic results with desktop latency.
entries.summary:
This record owns evidence for the Wayland cursor and scheduling changes in
`floe-native-apps` v0.22.12. The [session contract](../architecture/remote-desktop.md)
owns authorization and generation boundaries; the
[viewer contract](../architecture/remote-desktop-viewer.md) owns pointer presentation.
A separate-cursor frame must contain cursor-free pixels, while view-only capture
retains the host pointer. Input replies must not block capture or authority
callbacks, and damage information cannot hide changes after a sequence gap.
Distribution and browser evidence does not establish actual GNOME desktop latency.
The user explicitly waived performance thresholds for the weak `udesk24` VM on
2026-10-05. Functional regressions remain required; hardware availability is not
performance evidence.

entries.title: Wayland legacy MemFd capture compatibility
entries.description: Verify the fix for immediate post-authorization capture failure with older GNOME PipeWire producers.
entries.summary:
This record owns the reproduction and acceptance evidence for the Wayland MemFd
compatibility repair. The [media contract](../architecture/remote-desktop-media.md)
owns buffer lifetime, cursor ownership and damage handling. An authorized readable
system-memory frame must work when an older producer omits the MAPPABLE flag;
invalid bounds must fail without reading outside the backing file. A native
capture failure still suspends the generation. Synthetic compatibility evidence
cannot certify an actual GNOME session or physical latency.

entries.title: Wayland capture pool optimization evidence
entries.description: Verify bounded pixel reuse and measure the released capture implementation on the udesk24 VM.
entries.summary:
This record owns acceptance evidence for the capture pool implementation in
`floe-native-apps` v0.22.14. The [media contract](../architecture/remote-desktop-media.md)
owns pixel lifetime, cursor presentation and scheduling. Native copies must
preserve supported formats, clean comparison pixels and the final changed frame;
shutdown must interrupt exhausted-pool waits. Installed tests and controlled
latency measurements cannot certify physical input response or the user's
running GNOME session. Weak-VM performance remains observational.

entries.title: Current-desktop acceptance method
entries.description: Qualify remote desktop contracts, office interaction and actual painted performance without substituting synthetic checks.
entries.summary:
This guide defines acceptance for the [desktop contract](../architecture/remote-desktop.md).
Use published dependencies with `GOWORK=off`, preserve failed measurements and
resolve unmet thresholds for the agreed performance hosts before declaring
remote-desktop acceptance. Source integration does not substitute for this
qualification. A connected picture, native input
admission or a synthetic fixture does not certify real desktop performance.
The [acceptance record](remote-desktop-results.md) owns measured results and
remaining qualification.

entries.title: Current-desktop qualification results
entries.description: Assess published macOS and X11 performance, functional-only Wayland validation and local delivery limits.
entries.summary:
The agreed host scope passes the tested [desktop contract](../architecture/remote-desktop.md).
Published v0.22.6 passes macOS/X11 performance, office interaction and ten-minute
input/queue checks. The user designated `udesk24` for functional validation only;
its [Wayland failures](remote-desktop-wayland-results.md) remain outside that scope.
Preserve the [measurement boundaries](remote-desktop-validation.md) and failures;
passing retries do not establish causes. The [reconnect record](remote-desktop-recovery-results.md)
qualifies v0.22.7 sound, Mac hotplug, locked reconnect and Wayland mode recovery.
Integration does not establish release acceptance, passing Wayland performance
or hardware encoding.

entries.title: Remote desktop latency and NVIDIA encoding
entries.description: Assess the controlled RTX 4090 D desktop latency comparison and the remaining capture and transport limits.
entries.summary:
The controlled physical-seat and X11 comparisons qualify their tested local
configurations. The v0.22.29 physical-seat candidate reduced host-local input
receipt latency and CPU use; the v0.22.10 X11 candidate reduced client-window
response latency with working NVIDIA encoding and one local host-shaped cursor.

Session authority remains owned by the
[desktop contract](../architecture/remote-desktop.md). These measurements establish
the tested configuration, not physical input-to-photon latency, universal GPU
performance, zero-copy capture or WAN behavior. Capture/encoder failures still
revoke media authority and require fresh current-generation paint.

entries.title: Remote desktop drag latency
entries.description: Assess raw-pointer dispatch using repeated native drag and client-window observations over the production Desktop SSH placement bridge.
entries.summary:
The 2026-10-04 X11 qualification observes lower continuous window-drag latency
with published Floe Webapp v0.81.6 over the production Desktop SSH/HTTP2 placement
bridge. The [viewer contract](../architecture/remote-desktop-viewer.md) owns input
and painted-frame authority; the published pointer controller owns raw motion,
button ordering and cancellation. A failed decoder still requires a fresh
generation and paint. This record establishes one tested configuration, not
physical input-to-photon latency or parity with NoMachine.

entries.title: Physical desktop responsiveness and local input
entries.description: Assess physical-seat input and DRM capture on orange and udesk26, distinguishing host feedback from client presentation.
entries.summary:
Native v0.22.33 provides idle capture wakeup; published Floe controllers own
bounded pointer submission and local text mode. The
[media contract](../architecture/remote-desktop-media.md) owns privileged
authority; the [viewer contract](../architecture/remote-desktop-viewer.md) owns
input modes. Locks remain physical-only; generation and mode changes revoke
input. This record qualifies document contents, DRM feedback and encoded-frame
arrival separately. The udesk26 path passes functional qualification. The
[orange AFBC record](remote-desktop-orange-afbc-results.md) owns the later
Wayland import repair and native lock/unlock qualification. Native qualification
does not establish complete Viewer or performance acceptance.

entries.title: Orange AFBC capture qualification
entries.description: Verify the bounded legacy Rockchip scanout import repair and distinguish native qualification from deployed Viewer acceptance.
entries.summary:
The native converter owns physical scanout format normalization; Redeven
consumes its release without a second capture implementation. Orange's active
1920x1080 Wayland scanout is decodable through its installed EGL stack once
the exact legacy AFBC component convention is respected. Real pixel and native
lock/unlock tests pass on orange; udesk26 passes the corresponding regression.
Input authority remains with the privileged service and a fresh painted
generation. Native results do not qualify browser/network latency, physical
photons or an installed product update. Unsupported layouts fail explicitly.

entries.title: Physical-device remote desktop Viewer qualification
entries.description: Assess deployed udesk26 Viewer behavior and bounded recovery timing while preserving IME, cursor and comparison limits.
entries.summary:
Env App owns permanent SSH desktop deployment; the privileged native service
owns physical-seat input and lock authority. This run consumes native
`v0.22.34` and qualifies real udesk26 picture, mouse, keyboard, assisted Unicode
commit, physical unlock, window switching, disconnect and Electron fullscreen.
Ordinary input stays disabled while locked or disconnected. Ten injected
control-channel interruptions recover to a new Viewer paint confirmation.
The [Orange follow-up](remote-desktop-orange-viewer-results.md) owns recovered
connection and Runtime update evidence; its Env App service update and Viewer
acceptance remain pending. Real IME composition, matching cursor feedback,
command RTT and RustDesk/NoMachine parity remain unqualified.

entries.title: Orange remote desktop Viewer follow-up
entries.description: Record published native deployment, real Viewer recovery and the measured RustDesk acceptance boundary.
entries.summary:
Orange runs published native `v0.22.37` through Env App update and executable
admission; all thirteen release qualification jobs pass. Real Viewer checks pass
Unicode paste, physical lock, wrong-password rejection, unlock, successor input
and scoped media recovery. Mac local Pinyin is deferred; host Pinyin remains
unvalidated. Two paired rounds improve matched latency tails and motion FPS,
but missing idle responses and failed SSH carrier recovery prevent RustDesk
parity. A third RustDesk half has severe tails and disconnects. Comparison moves
to udesk26 after measured Orange LAN loss; complete quality and resource
evidence is still required.

entries.title: Physical desktop RustDesk comparison
entries.description: Apply paired presentation, detail, compatibility and resource criteria before accepting RustDesk parity.
entries.summary:
The primary qualification task owns acceptance. Full RustDesk parity and
repeatable restoration of historical performance remain unaccepted. Published
native v0.22.48 with negotiated six-frame delivery averages 46.21 FPS against
RustDesk 32.54 FPS in three retained motion rounds. Candidate pooled P95 is
310.60 ms against 207.59 ms, with nine versus three gaps over 250 ms. Candidate
round three reaches 53.04 FPS/P95 150.20 ms with no long gaps, but the adverse
first round cannot be replaced. Keep current security, authorization, confirmed
paint, ordering and recovery safeguards. The [C05 result](remote-desktop-lan-c05-results.md) owns current
results and open cases; the [decision ledger](remote-desktop-lan-experiment-ledger.md)
records adopted, rejected and unresolved experiments.

entries.title: LAN desktop experiment decision ledger
entries.description: Consult historical winners, rejected hypotheses and retry conditions before another LAN performance experiment.
entries.summary:
The LAN record shows a measured deficit without establishing its cause or full
RustDesk parity. The published v0.22.48 six-frame path reached 53.04 FPS in one
round, but did not restore three-round stability. C01-C03 hypotheses were
rejected; C04 supports optional Linux six-frame delivery as a throughput
diagnostic only. C05 owns current paired results and remaining limits.

entries.title: Published LAN C05 outcomes and unresolved boundaries
entries.description: Inspect every retained v48 paired result, source-loss failure and resource/detail limit before another controlled experiment.
entries.summary:
The primary qualification task owns C05 outcomes. The released six-frame path
restores the ability to exceed 51 FPS while retaining later fixes, but does not
restore the historical three-round stability or qualify complete RustDesk parity.
All complete adverse trials count. Source-input loss invalidates ordinal latency
association; missing presentation with all source inputs remains a valid failure.
The [comparison contract](remote-desktop-rustdesk-comparison-results.md) owns
acceptance and [C05 preparation](remote-desktop-lan-published-c05.md) owns immutable
identities, controls, release checks and compatibility. Retry only a named fixture
repair or a new discriminating hypothesis, after consulting the decision ledger.

entries.title: Published six-frame LAN qualification C05
entries.description: Verify the released optional frame window against RustDesk and retain preparation failures separately from performance evidence.
entries.summary:
The primary qualification task owns C05. The optional six-frame implementation
must use a published native module and preserve four-frame legacy/macOS behavior,
confirmed paint, generation/order fences and finite admission. C04 establishes a
diagnostic throughput benefit, not released recovery or full RustDesk parity.
The [comparison contract](remote-desktop-rustdesk-comparison-results.md) owns
acceptance. A failed release gate or invalid fixture stops qualification; retain
its evidence and repair the named failure before retrying.

entries.title: Remote desktop platform reacceptance
entries.description: Recheck actual GDM, GNOME lock, Portal and macOS behavior and trace the published Portal damage repair.
entries.summary:
This record owns the 2026-10-17 UTC platform reacceptance evidence. The
[session](../architecture/remote-desktop.md) and
[media](../architecture/remote-desktop-media.md) contracts own authorization,
generation and pixel safety. Acceptance requires captured pixels and native input
receipts, preserving existing sessions and Runtime processes. Viewer/helper evidence stays distinct; failures remain visible.

entries.title: Desktop reconnect qualification results
entries.description: Verify published desktop transport, locked reconnect, physical Mac hotplug and Wayland display recovery with fresh-paint authority.
entries.summary:
Published `floe-native-apps` v0.22.7 passes Linux X11 and macOS product reconnect:
the running audio device survives replacement, new samples reach its AudioWorklet,
and input waits for current paint. Mac physical hotplug, locked replacement and
Wayland mode changes also pass fresh-paint recovery. These results do not certify
[Wayland performance](remote-desktop-wayland-results.md); `udesk24` is designated
for functional validation only. The [session contract](../architecture/remote-desktop.md)
owns normative behavior; the [overall record](remote-desktop-results.md) owns
performance and delivery boundaries.

entries.title: Wayland desktop qualification results
entries.description: Assess real GNOME Wayland office behavior and retained capture failures before and after authorized virtual graphics provisioning.
entries.summary:
The real `udesk24` GNOME 46 Wayland desktop passes the tested office workflow
and display-mode recovery with published `floe-native-apps` v0.22.7. The user
designated this host for functional validation only on 2026-10-02; its graphics
performance does not block delivery. It still fails the
[performance contract](remote-desktop-validation.md): current 1080p/1440p
scrolling reaches 27.46/23.46 FPS despite authorized virtual graphics provisioning.
Preserve the failures; X11 or synthetic results cannot replace Wayland evidence.
The [overall record](remote-desktop-results.md) owns delivery and the other hosts.

entries.title: Host application catalog and owned native sessions
entries.description: Browse Linux and macOS host applications and open owned, reconnectable graphical sessions through existing authorized windows.
entries.summary:
Redeven owns application discovery, authorization and independent client sharing
leases. Applications run as the host OS user without a container or virtual
machine. Opening an application always admits or resumes sharing for the current
client; closing that client's viewer releases only its lease and preserves the
application. The last lease ends the route and transport without stopping the process;
ordinary quit and confirmed force quit are separate explicit actions. Sharing
routes are ephemeral. Surviving Linux instances require verified recovery, while
macOS uses native OS inventory. Missing capabilities and failed capture remain
visible and never imply that an application exited.

entries.title: Cross-platform host application behavior
entries.description: Compare aligned user operations and operating-system limits for macOS and Linux host applications.
entries.summary:
Host Applications separates viewing, sharing, window closure and process exit on
both platforms. Ordinary actions preserve unsaved work and respect app cancellation.
Only an independently confirmed Force quit may bypass saving. The backend owns
process evidence, and the interface names the actual supported operation. OS
session, display and service policies remain authoritative; unavailable recovery
must not silently relaunch an unrelated or replacement process.

entries.title: Linux application instances and independent sharing
entries.description: Preserve owned Linux graphical applications across viewer and Runtime lifetimes, with verified recovery and explicit process termination.
entries.summary: Redeven owns Linux instances, authorization and ephemeral shares; Floe Native Apps owns GIO/process observation. Applications outlive viewers and window count. Closing a share or Runtime never requests termination. Recovery requires original user/private state plus matching kernel process generation and endpoint; persisted PID alone never permits signaling. Reboot, display destruction or external cgroup cleanup can end dependent apps.

entries.title: Client input for host applications
entries.description: Own composition once on the client, bind confirmed text and keys to painted application windows, and recover without replay.
entries.summary: Published Floe remote-input owns viewer keyboard/composition. Clients own input method/preedit/candidates; hosts deliver confirmed Unicode/keys to the painted window. Each operation has one output owner. Binding loss cancels composition/releases keys; reconnect never replays. Unsupported old protocols require save/quit/reopen without automatic process termination. Flower, terminals and editors keep their own input.

entries.title: Pointer gestures for host applications
entries.description: Scroll, click and drag remote applications through one client gesture owner while retaining browser pinch zoom and local controls.
entries.summary:
Published Floe remote-pointer owns content pointer events in Linux native/Xpra and macOS
viewers. Touch swipes scroll; taps click; long presses provide drag or right click.
A gesture stays bound to one painted window instance and connection generation.
Cancellation drops queued movement and scroll and releases only its own buttons.
Keyboard composition stays with [remote-input](host-application-input.md). Missing
pointer capability requires saving, quitting and reopening the application; closing
only its viewer does not upgrade or terminate the application process.

entries.title: Host application display and window layout
entries.description: Keep Xpra layout, native window state, pixel density and cursor coordinates consistent across viewport and quality changes.
entries.summary: Published Floe Native Apps owns Linux display configuration, constraints and cursor coordinates. Redeven declares layout/quality; Desktop owns actual maximize/minimize. Remote receipts cannot create resize loops, and unchanged configuration preserves canvases without commands. Old display backends retain logical density with explicit high-resolution limits; apps never auto-restart.

entries.title: Native Linux host application picture streams
entries.description: Negotiate efficient native pictures and compose bounded regions without changing input authority, application geometry or process identity.
entries.summary:
Published Floe Native Apps owns native capture, region encoding and browser
composition. Redeven maps picture preferences and displays measured statistics.
Only successfully composed pixels authorize input and acknowledgement. Quality
changes preserve application and connection identity. Incompatible or malformed
frames require explicit recovery; surviving legacy sessions remain viewable.
The [display contract](host-application-display.md) owns application geometry.

entries.title: Host application viewer resources and layered upgrades
entries.description: Prepare current immutable viewer snapshots while retaining application and backend lifetimes, and authorize their content-addressed resources.
entries.summary: Published Floe Native Apps owns immutable `PreparedViewer` documents/assets, digests and capabilities. Redeven pins one snapshot per authorized Xpra share. Compatible surviving apps reconnect after viewer/Runtime updates without PID/content changes. Preparation failure offers retry, never historical resources. Backends and loaded modules retain process lifetimes without hot swaps.

entries.title: Host application viewer state and recovery
entries.description: Present authoritative application state, first pixels, recovery without conflating viewer closure with application termination.
entries.summary: Runtime/native events own application facts; Redeven bootstrap owns viewer presentation. Show pixels only after decoding. Transport/access loss never proves exit, and reconnect preserves process identity without launching. Confirmed last-window/app closure dismisses an established viewer; an already-loaded terminal document remains readable. [Application authorization](host-applications.md) and [titlebar](../desktop/host-application-titlebar.md) retain their owners.

entries.title: Host application platforms and initialization
entries.description: Capability-based Linux initialization, dependency diagnostics, distribution evidence, and native macOS requirements.
entries.summary:
Published Floe Native Apps owns Linux graphics, package planning and scoped host
service adaptation. Redeven owns the authorized catalog, instance and viewer.
New applications normally receive a private Wayland/Xwayland environment; an
explicit upstream X11-only contract can select Xpra before execution. A launch
never retries with another backend. Native applications need no full desktop or
physical monitor. Snap and Flatpak additionally require their installed runtimes
and necessary host services. Missing capabilities remain explicit failures.

entries.title: macOS application picture quality and delivery
entries.description: Retina window pixels, live picture controls, hardware video and bounded authenticated frame delivery.
entries.summary:
Redeven's native application capture helper owns image resolution and encoding;
the viewer owns picture preferences and measured display statistics. Application
identity, permissions and input retain the [native session contract](macos-host-applications.md).
A frame can acknowledge delivery only after decoding for the current capture
generation. Quality changes and reconnects preserve the application process.
Hardware or browser video unavailability selects the explicit image transport;
the quality panel reports the transport actually producing frames. A real capture
failure retains the session's existing reconnect boundary.

entries.title: Native macOS host applications
entries.description: Real application discovery, direct local launch, owned remote window capture and human input on macOS.
entries.summary: Redeven discovers installed macOS bundles and opens real apps as the Runtime user. Trusted Desktop Local routes launch directly; remote routes capture the selected app's actual windows, including existing single-instance processes. [Application authorization](host-applications.md) gates every operation/stream. Missing graphical login or permissions blocks capture; disconnect preserves the app and reconnect binds the same process.

entries.title: macOS application window lifecycle
entries.description: Preserve shared applications through uncertain window inventories and end viewers only on confirmed native closure.
entries.summary:
Redeven's native helper owns macOS application-window lifetime. Its registry binds
exact AX windows to the selected process instance; capture surfaces do not define
window lifetime. Only confirmed destruction can start the last-window grace.
Uncertain inventory, unavailable capture and transport loss retain the session and
its recovery entrypoint while revoking stale input. Runtime preserves the helper's
explicit end reason; the shared viewer owns whether an established page can close.

entries.title: macOS application menu scope
entries.description: Export native application commands without the system Apple menu and validate every executable handle against the live menu.
entries.summary:
The macOS helper owns the menu exposed by a single-application viewer. It omits
the entire system Apple subtree and identified cross-application visibility
commands before issuing handles. Application titles remain literal native text.
Only an enabled leaf from the current snapshot, still under its allowed live
ancestry, can execute. Rejected or stale actions produce the existing localized
operation error and preserve the application and capture. Menu inspection happens
on explicit menu requests and actions, never on the launch or first-frame path.

entries.title: macOS application capture process ownership
entries.description: Share one native capture process while preserving independent application channels, frame credit and lifecycle.
entries.summary:
The host application Manager owns one lazily started Swift helper for its Runtime
lifetime. All catalog requests, human-operated application sessions and
[remote desktop sessions](remote-desktop.md) use that process. Suspending one application must not interrupt another application's
capture. Application identity, viewer authorization, input, frame credit and
cleanup remain independent. A helper crash fails its current sharing sessions
without quitting native applications; a later explicit open may start a new
helper. The [native application contract](macos-host-applications.md) owns OS
permissions and process/window validation.

entries.title: macOS application management and graceful quit
entries.description: Live OS application inventory, generation-bound quit and independent sharing detachment.
entries.summary:
Redeven owns the Host Applications management UI and authenticated native actions.
The OS owns process liveness, and the application owns saving or cancelling quit.
Running applications remain manageable without a sharing session. An explicit
quit validates the original process generations; it never force-kills an app,
retargets a replacement process, or treats command acceptance as proof of exit.
An unavailable or stale target returns an actionable error and preserves sharing.
The [native session contract](macos-host-applications.md) owns capture, input and
physical viewer closure.

entries.title: Prepare Linux hosts for native applications
entries.description: Prepare the default combined backend and identify the explicit system Xpra installation boundary.
entries.summary:
New Linux applications use the managed combined Wayland/Xwayland component from
published Floe Native Apps. The application library provides its preparation and
recovery flow; Desktop can transfer verified archives to an offline host. Native
applications need no full desktop or physical monitor. Snap and Flatpak additionally
need their installed package runtimes and required host services. Missing services
produce explicit recovery guidance; Redeven never installs system packages or
changes security policy automatically.

The [platform contract](../architecture/host-application-platforms.md) owns package,
service and isolation requirements; [preparation](../architecture/host-application-preparation.md)
owns acquisition and recovery. Refresh the library after administrative changes.

entries.title: Host application distribution validation
entries.description: Installed-stack evidence, architecture limits and repeatable native application acceptance.
entries.summary:
This record distinguishes installed-stack evidence from host policy certification.
Its distribution and pointer records describe retained historical Xpra versions.
The [desktop and package validation record](host-application-desktop-validation.md)
owns current combined-backend, sandbox package and product integration evidence.
The Runtime capability and isolation contract is owned by
[host application platforms](../architecture/host-application-platforms.md).
A passing userspace check proves the tested Xpra/GIO/runtime combination only;
missing subscriptions, CPU translation and untested host policy remain explicit.
Administrators retain the [setup route](host-application-setup.md) for their host.

entries.title: Host application picture performance
entries.description: Measure native host application bandwidth, presented frames, input latency and bounded decoding with repeatable browser workloads.
entries.summary:
The [display contract](../architecture/host-application-display.md) owns picture
behavior. Floe Native Apps owns capture, encoding and region decoding; Redeven owns
forwarding, picture choices and acceptance. Measure pixels and bytes, not limits.
Failed budgets retain their raw result and block the associated claim. Documents
do not certify video, WAN, physical displays or universal remote-desktop parity.

entries.title: Host application input validation
entries.description: Verify actual toolkit text delivery, click focus and surviving application instances without substituting simulated IME evidence.
entries.summary:
This guide qualifies the [client input contract](../architecture/host-application-input.md)
through actual application receipts and saved bytes. Published upstream qualification
owns native input adapters and prepared Xpra event ownership. Redeven verifies its
viewer, authenticated transport, launch and recovery adapters. Sending a request or
focusing a DOM element is insufficient. Existing applications retain their backend
and loaded resources. Real system candidate selection and physical mobile acceptance
remain separate; simulated events must never be reported as those checks.

entries.title: Linux desktop and package compatibility validation
entries.description: Assess released native backend evidence separately from Redeven viewer, package, recovery and deployment acceptance.
entries.summary:
The [platform contract](../architecture/host-application-platforms.md) is qualified
by real processes, windows, native input receipts and saved files. Floe Native Apps
owns reusable graphics/package/service evidence; Redeven owns product launch,
sharing, rendering and recovery evidence. Each claim retains its source/component
identity. Prototype results do not substitute for exact-release qualification.
Missing capabilities remain explicit failures, and no result certifies arbitrary
applications, physical GPUs or every desktop version.

entries.title: Host application platform validation
entries.description: Assess the tested Linux userspace and native macOS application matrix with explicit hardware and policy limits.
entries.summary:
Host application platform acceptance records real installed-stack and native
session evidence under the [platform contract](../architecture/host-application-platforms.md).
The matrix identifies exactly which userspace, Runtime, CPU and display combinations
were exercised. Container or translated-CPU results cannot certify host boot,
kernel, security policy or native hardware behavior. Missing permissions, unavailable
subscriptions and untested environments remain unqualified; they never become
successful simulated acceptance.

entries.title: Host application cursor acceptance
entries.description: Distinguish published cursor geometry, native click receipts and physical pointer evidence.
entries.summary:
The [viewer contract](../architecture/host-application-viewer.md) owns cursor
geometry; published `floe-native-apps` owns its implementation. Acceptance checks
decoded images and application click receipts separately from the operating
system's displayed pointer. A CSS declaration or ordinary page screenshot cannot
qualify physical pointer appearance. Unavailable devices remain unpassed.

entries.title: Host application lifecycle acceptance
entries.description: Scenario-based evidence for native application sharing and explicit recovery boundaries.
entries.summary:
This matrix records observable lifecycle acceptance for Host Applications. The
[shared authorization contract](../architecture/host-applications.md) and
[macOS window lifecycle owner](../architecture/macos-application-window-lifecycle.md) remain normative.
A live process, an available window, a decoded frame and an authenticated viewer
are separate facts. Only explicit closure evidence ends the physical viewer.
A missing or inaccessible surface must preserve the app and provide an accurate
recovery path; it must never silently select an unrelated process or inject stale
input. This matrix is not a certification of every installed application.

See the [cross-platform behavior contract](../architecture/host-application-behavior.md)
for aligned operations and unavoidable OS differences.

entries.title: Portable native Runtime binaries
entries.description: GNU static Runtime builds, native Floeterm, musl execution and LGPL source/relink distribution.
entries.summary:
The shared Runtime builder owns native terminal linkage for Runtime and Gateway.
Linux artifacts run on glibc and musl systems without a host dynamic loader;
Darwin artifacts require a matching Apple builder. Missing native tools fail
preflight. Linux releases must include matching source and relink materials for
the statically linked LGPL library, and publication fails when that kit is absent.

entries.title: Desktop loopback Web Service access
entries.description: Give one HTTP Web Service an isolated numeric-loopback browser Origin without bypassing its protected Runtime route.
entries.summary: Desktop-only `desktop_loopback` gives one Environment session/forward a random `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` origin while every request follows its protected Runtime route. It never connects directly, changes interfaces, modifies applications or falls back to unified proxy. Closing the owning window/Environment removes the gateway and authority.

entries.title: Web Service system-browser authorization
entries.description: Hand Desktop-private Web Services to a system browser without exposing the bridge credential or creating a public fallback.
entries.summary: Runtime alone admits system-browser access to Desktop-private `unified_proxy` services. Desktop requests a short-lived single-use entry for an exact forward/path; Runtime redeems it into a Host-only session on `pf-<forward_id>.localhost:<bridge_port>`. Bridge credentials stay out of browsers and browser credentials out of services. Failure opens no URL; `desktop_loopback` is excluded.

entries.title: Managed Web Service opening
entries.description: Prepare the current verified launch entrance and recover authentication without implicit lifecycle changes.
entries.summary:
- Authority: the released template package owns entrance declarations and parsing; Runtime owns launch verification, preparation and private persistence; Desktop owns navigation results; Env App owns factual presentation.
- Outcome: Host, Container and Compose hand a verified current entrance to the existing protected Forward route, including an already-running instance after an upgrade.
- Invariants: opening never restarts, upgrades, reinstalls or modifies application data; one public preparation path owns results; HTTP 401 proves response availability, not authenticated access.
- Failure boundary: unverified ownership, launch changes, unavailable output and unsafe URLs fail with retryable or explicit recovery explanations. A preparation failure never stops a healthy application.

entries.title: Managed Web Service Templates
entries.description: Consume one signed-off versioned service catalog whose release is a recommendation, not a user-version restriction.
entries.summary: The released `redeven-service-templates` module owns built-in identity, specifications, releases, localization, icons and service-specific notices. Redeven embeds a reproducible digest-verified offline bundle. Recommendations set defaults, never constrain source choices or replace installed releases. Malformed, missing, mismatched or future content blocks startup without local-definition fallback.

entries.title: Redeven Service Template format compatibility
entries.description: Read branded and historical template documents through the released upstream data adapter without rewriting source files.
entries.summary:
- Authority: the released `redeven-service-templates/template` package owns schemas, historical data adapters, and current types. Runtime owns authorization and execution.
- Outcome: formally supported old template directories remain usable after a Redeven upgrade, with their original filenames, bytes, modes, digest, and source commit intact.
- Invariants: compatibility operates in memory, feeds one current executor, never persists an adapted execution definition, and never installs, upgrades, or restarts a service by itself.
- Failure boundary: invalid historical shapes, ambiguous entrypoints, incorrect identity, and future formats fail explicitly without altering files. Unsupported formats require a compatible release or author correction.

entries.title: GitHub service template sources
entries.description: Import and manually review original GitHub template directories through Desktop transfer or direct Runtime acquisition.
entries.summary:
- Authority: upstream owns acquisition and format validation; Redeven owns authenticated import, user review, and the active-directory pointer.
- Outcome: public/private GitHub templates import through Desktop transfer or direct Runtime download without an installed `git` executable.
- Invariants: no background source checks, automatic source updates, dependency installation, script execution, application upgrade, or restart occurs during source import/review. Credentials remain request-scoped.
- Failure boundary: validation or confirmation failure keeps the active source. One missing, corrupt, or unsupported source blocks only that template and its associated operations; there is no old-definition fallback.

entries.title: Independent Host service lifecycle
entries.description: Preserve running applications across management restarts and recover only verified process ownership.
entries.summary:
- Authority: the application owns its business execution; Redeven owns authorized lifecycle actions, native process identity, launch records, and opening validation.
- Outcome: Desktop or Runtime exit, restart, or upgrade leaves a launched service's PID and launch generation unchanged.
- Invariants: no new binary, resident supervisor, application-specific driver branch, process-output pipe to Runtime, or ownership inferred from PID alone.
- Recovery boundary: absent, mismatched, and uninspectable resources are distinct. Only confirmed absence permits eligible automatic startup; opening failure never stops a running application.

entries.title: Managed Web Services
entries.description: Operate generic Host, Container, and Compose services from the current verified external template definitions.
entries.summary: Redeven owns service instances, bindings, resources, operations and protected forwards; verified external templates define behavior. One generic engine handles Host, Container and Compose installation, lifecycle, recovery and uninstall. Registry state and exact resource identity are authoritative. Invalid catalog, release, ownership, permission or health facts fail closed without adopting unknown resources.

entries.title: Web Service management recovery
entries.description: Keep service facts, user goals, resource cleanup, and management archives actionable across failures and Runtime restarts.
entries.summary:
- Authority: the Registry owns management records and lifecycle transactions; the Manager observes resources and determines actions; the Renderer presents that decision.
- Outcome: every service explains its current situation, the last operation's result, and an available next step in Activity and Workbench.
- Invariants: historical failures never determine current resource state; unavailable inspection never means absence; destructive effects require fresh ownership and explicit cleanup choices.
- Failure boundary: an administrator with a working Registry can detach even when the engine is offline. Detachment preserves resources and never claims that business processes stopped.

entries.title: Service resource ownership
entries.description: Allocate isolated instance resources and verify exact ownership before reuse or deletion without moving legacy application data.
entries.summary:
- Authority: the Registry records resource allocations and identities; engine and filesystem inspection establish current facts.
- Outcome: separate instances, including installations in separate Runtime state directories, receive independent default data and workspace resources.
- Invariants: names alone never confer ownership; stopped containers count as references; external resources and unverified legacy assets cannot become implicitly deletable.
- Failure boundary: inspection or identity uncertainty preserves resources and directs users to the management review. No running data is moved or copied during upgrade.

entries.title: Managed Service operation progress
entries.description: Persist and stream bounded, redacted lifecycle command output while preserving stable, user-controlled progress presentation.
entries.summary:
- Authority: a Manager-owned Reporter publishes each active operation; the Registry owns durable history.
- Outcome: users can inspect bounded lifecycle output in a focused drawer view and keep a brief completion visible while list and stream refreshes preserve the expanded operation.
- Invariants: safe command templates, pre-persistence redaction, one operation ID for disclosure, readable terminal feedback, and no Runtime identity derived from output.
- Failure boundary: persistence, streaming, capture, and validation failures never expose raw output, secrets, credentials, sensitive URL queries, private paths, or control characters.

entries.title: Managed Service release discovery and updates
entries.description: Discover exact npm and OCI releases directly from configured sources, require explicit selection, and update with rollback.
entries.summary: Configured npm/OCI registries own release metadata; Redeven validates candidates, installed identity, updates and rollback. Users explicitly select compatible releases without a Redeven version service. Discovery never installs; recommendations are defaults only. Expiring opaque IDs are revalidated at execution. Failure preserves healthy service and last-success summaries without implicit installation.

entries.title: Managed Service version interaction
entries.description: Select and verify a version in one drawer, confirm only changed notices, and stop or submit without losing context.
entries.summary: Redeven owns version selection; Manager owns exact update-plan admission. Users select and submit in one drawer. Preparation executes nothing, only changed required notices need confirmation, and selection/browsing survives preparation or admission failure. Accepted operations retain their existing controller after drawer closure; source failures stay actionable in place.

entries.title: Managed Service Instance Configuration
entries.description: Resolve the current template and instance overrides into one validated Runtime specification with journaled stopped-state reconfiguration.
entries.summary: The verified current template owns Runtime baseline; Redeven owns overrides, exact release, digest, Resource Plans, secrets, journals and rebuilds. Renderer owns an unsaved draft. One resolver combines baseline and differences. Runtime apply requires stopped state, current revision, exact plan and risk checks; invalid input fails before commit and failed rebuild restores prior state or reports rollback failure.

entries.title: Runtime Service snapshot
entries.description: Runtime identity, independent compatibility, access readiness, workload inventory, and optional Gateway supervision.
entries.summary: The Runtime Service snapshot is a typed boundary between Runtime, Desktop, Local UI, and optional Gateway supervision. Runtime protocol/version, compatibility epoch, capabilities, service readiness, and workload identity are explicit facts. Gateway is optional for Runtime startup and ordinary access; its absence only closes Redeven-managed lifecycle actions.

entries.title: Runtime session permission gates
entries.description: Redeven validates session metadata and clamps granted permissions before opening runtime sessions.
entries.summary: Before any runtime session is accepted, Redeven validates `session_meta`, rejects unsupported app/channel combinations, intersects the control-plane grant with the local permission policy, and then applies extra app-specific gates for Code App and Port Forward. Read permission grants the existing system-monitor snapshot, including process names, users, and resource usage. Process termination remains independently protected by execute permission.

entries.title: Runtime system monitoring
entries.description: Sample environment resources once and report network totals and rates from non-loopback interfaces.
entries.summary: The Monitor service owns environment CPU, memory, network, and process sampling. Its cached snapshot is the authority for both the Monitoring page and Workbench. Network byte totals and rates exclude every interface marked as loopback by the operating system and share one filtered counter source. A failed network sample never enters rate history or falls back to all-interface totals; later valid background samples recover automatically while other resource sampling continues.

entries.title: Runtime transport dependencies
entries.description: Runtime transport uses Flowersec sessions while terminal lifecycle is delegated to Floeterm managers.
entries.summary: Redeven runtime builds control and data sessions on the Transport v3 artifact and the current Flowersec lease, connection-controller, session, RPC, and byte-stream primitives, while terminal lifecycle is delegated to Floeterm. Each Env App owns one protocol provider and current Flowersec session; RPC and independent live streams share it. Placement HTTP/2 is a separate SSH stdio boundary and does not change Flowersec wire or public SDK contracts.

entries.title: Runtime artifact spend and control pool
entries.description: Persist, spend, replenish, and revoke opaque Flowersec control artifacts without replay or authority duplication.
entries.summary: Remote control and data artifacts are opaque, single-spend capabilities. Redeven binds each Lease to one digest-global tombstone, persists idempotent bootstrap and top-up request identities, and rejects stale, duplicate, malformed, expired, or cross-environment responses before a connection can consume them. Pool replenishment and relink are terminal state transitions, never silent fallback.

entries.title: Runtime terminal lifecycle
entries.description: Delegate PTY, native terminal state, live streams, semantic history, and warmup to the released Floeterm manager.
entries.summary: Floeterm terminal-go owns each PTY, native Ghostty VT, geometry, controller epoch, input encoding, semantic history, clear/reset, and atomic Presentation. Redeven maps permissions, session metadata, and Activity/Workbench placement around that actor; browser views consume bounded semantic streams and never become a second terminal state machine.

entries.title: Product RPC request encoding
entries.description: Redeven codecs construct JSON requests that preserve optional filesystem operation semantics before Flowersec dispatch.
entries.summary:
Redeven request codecs own product JSON construction; published Flowersec owns
transport validation and dispatch. File creation accepts empty content and
omitted encoding. Absent optional fields must be omitted, while explicit false
and empty content retain their meanings. Invalid request objects fail before
dispatch and require a codec correction, not transport retries or relaxed
validation.

entries.title: Git workspace inventory lifecycle
entries.description: Bound Git workspace capture, immutable revisions, resource admission, mutation coordination, and destructive linked-worktree removal.
entries.summary: Git workspace queries produce bounded immutable process-local snapshots; paged/path reads bind exact revisions. Git and Files mutations share repository/topology coordination and invalidate affected snapshots before and after effects. Display state never authorizes mutation. Oversized, stale, malformed or exhausted requests return small typed errors while the Flowersec session remains usable.

entries.title: Env App upstream web dependencies
entries.description: Env App composes published floe-webapp, FloeBrowser, Floeterm, and Flowersec packages.
entries.summary:
Env App adapts published floe-webapp UI/runtime and protocol, FloeBrowser projection, Floeterm terminal-web, and Flowersec artifact helpers into the Redeven shell.

Pins are Floe Webapp Boot, Core, and Protocol v0.86.63 (Env App Core v0.86.63), FloeBrowser v0.1.28, Floeterm terminal-web v0.19.2, and Flowersec Core v5.11.1. Floeterm supplies semantic Presentation and session exports.

[Page asset recovery](../ui/page-asset-recovery.md) uses Floe's document asset monitor and per-view error boundary for deployment and lazy imports.

entries.title: Env App terminal and surface composition
entries.description: Compose published Floeterm semantic terminal APIs and Floe surface lifecycles without duplicating renderer or navigation state.
entries.summary: Env App keeps terminal and Activity/Workbench surfaces thin over published Floeterm and Floe components. A mounted view owns only its semantic projection and local interaction state; Floeterm owns PTY facts and Floe owns shell, selection, KeepAlive, focus, and layer mechanics. Lazy loading and recovery preserve those ownership boundaries while keeping existing surfaces mounted and interactive where policy allows.

entries.title: Env App connection and recovery
entries.description: Compose published Floe and Flowersec artifact sources, Service Worker control, and reconnect recovery without a product retry loop.
entries.summary: Env App uses Floe's published artifact-source and connection-controller contracts for public HTTPS, explicit HTTP, remote controlplane, and Desktop-private loopback paths. It binds each source to the current origin and environment, requires exact Service Worker control, and projects Flowersec diagnostics into one immutable recovery snapshot without replaying requests or inventing retry policy.

entries.title: Whole-window status surfaces
entries.description: Present environment recovery, access gates, and standalone Desktop availability without applying glass to movable content.
entries.summary: Floe owns the shared whole-window layout, static artwork, retry geometry and progress shimmer. Redeven maps real connection, access and Desktop states to those published primitives. Recovery and access gates use an opaque neutral theme background even when the underlying workspace remains mounted and inert; no second disconnect notice may show through. Floating windows, Workbench widgets and draggable content never receive this material. Failure retains the existing recovery owner and explicit actions; appearance never grants access or starts another recovery loop.

entries.title: Env App page asset recovery
entries.description: Recover stale or interrupted page modules after Runtime connectivity returns.
entries.summary:
Floe owns document asset comparison and per-view error isolation. Redeven owns
the authenticated Env App entry route, secure-connection trigger, localized
presentation, and explicit reload action. A connected Runtime does not prove
that an already loaded browser document can still fetch its page modules.
Changed builds and failed module loads must expose recovery rather than an
endless loading placeholder. Detection never reloads over unsaved work.
Recovery notices stay inside the active mode's content area, below the unchanged
shell header and native window controls.

entries.title: ReDevPlugin host integration boundary
entries.description: Redeven consumes ReDevPlugin as a published platform and keeps only host policy, placement, source admission, localized presentation projection, and business adapters.
entries.summary: Redeven consumes the coordinated published ReDevPlugin Go, npm, Rust and machine-contract artifacts without forking platform mechanics. It owns session mapping, source policy/review, placement, product runtime builds and business adapters. Missing/unverifiable identity, lifecycle, interaction, package or runtime contracts fail closed without local compatibility or sibling-source fallback.

entries.title: ReDevPlugin Redeven adapters
entries.description: Keep Redeven-specific host modules, external package policy, and surface projection separate from ReDevPlugin platform mechanics.
entries.summary: Redeven owns only the adapters that bind authenticated product sessions, source policy, business capabilities, and Activity or Workbench placement to released ReDevPlugin contracts. ReDevPlugin remains the authority for host protocol, package trust, runtime execution, and platform state. Adapter failures stop at the product boundary and never create copied platform state or implicit grants.

entries.title: Plugin platform integration
entries.description: Redeven mounts released ReDevPlugin v3 and adds authenticated host modules, market-backed official releases, external-source policy, localized plugin presentation, product placement, and business adapters.
entries.summary: Redeven mounts released ReDevPlugin through one Go Host, HTTP namespace, Env App client and surface scope. Published Process Supervisor runs a verified product-built Linux/Darwin runtime. Redeven adds authenticated sessions, source policy, placement and business adapters; upstream owns package, state, protocol, trust and execution. Missing or unproven identities fail closed.

entries.title: Plugin process sessions
entries.description: ReDevPlugin owns opaque external-process sessions, bounded binary streams, and cleanup; Redeven only supplies authenticated owner, secret, policy, audit, and diagnostic adapters.
entries.summary:
ReDevPlugin Process Broker is the single platform owner for local processes
requested by plugins. Redeven supplies the authenticated user and environment
scope, permission decision, minimal environment, secret resolver, state root,
audit sink, and diagnostic sink; it does not expose a second process protocol.
The observable outcome is an opaque session handle and bounded binary stdin,
stdout, and stderr operations. The failure boundary is explicit: process
output may be lost after a bounded buffer overflows, and Host shutdown,
disable, uninstall, revocation, or owner teardown terminates owned processes.

entries.title: Plugin background entries
entries.description: ReDevPlugin starts and recovers one headless background entry per plugin instance and environment without creating a Redeven visual surface.
entries.summary:
Background entries are a generic ReDevPlugin lifecycle mechanism, not a
Codex-specific hidden page. A plugin declares `runtime_start` or `on_demand`;
the platform starts one headless worker per plugin instance and environment,
keeps it independent from visible Activity or Workbench surfaces, and exposes
only lifecycle outcomes. The platform stops it on disable, uninstall,
revocation, and Host close. Plugin business protocol state is not owned or
recovered by Redeven.

entries.title: Plugin package and runtime lifecycle
entries.description: Qualify released plugin package sources, installation, runtime admission, and cache ownership through ReDevPlugin.
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin owns package trust, inspection, installation, runtime readiness, release cache, and durable lifecycle. Redeven supplies authenticated source policy, review presentation, and localized outcomes. Every source follows inspect, explicit confirmation, and released Host installation; unverified bytes, stale trust, missing runtime identity, or uncertain mutation outcomes fail closed.

entries.title: Plugin surface recovery and permissions
entries.description: Keep Env App plugin inventory, installation observation, permission finalization, and reconnect recovery on one released client scope.
entries.summary: Env App owns one authenticated plugin client, one shared scope, and one installation observer. ReDevPlugin remains the authority for inventory, Executions, Events, permissions, revocation, and runtime recovery. Closing or reconnecting a panel preserves the exact request identity and authoritative outcome; a product refresh never becomes a second mutation or recovery lifecycle.

entries.title: Plugin market consumption
