sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
[Flower Goals](flower-goals.md) use the optional published Goal controller. Ordinary executable items retain strict identity.

## Incremental observation and public projection
Floret supplies optional `ThreadFactsSource`, `ThreadWindowSource` and canonical body readers. The published module `v7.87.4` includes bounded item-text reads, lazy hidden-field preparation, prepared-thread startup reuse and single-mutation title summaries. Title extraction uses at most 16 KiB of the existing canonical array prefix without detail preparation or new index writes. Blank-module adoption opens released-writer fixtures and verifies historical continuation and restart. Floret alone owns text cadence, versions, append buffers, Activity reduction and canonical reads.

Root detail, child detail and command receipts use the bounded window projection. The accepted window includes its canonical Summary in the same baseline; there is no separate preparation window or independently sampled read watermark. POST history selects an authorized page and, when an observer is supplied, installs its reading interest on the same ordered Floret subscription. POST history-item expands one canonical item by its published body locators: frozen live extent, manifest parts or hash-verified field chunks. Every read refreshes endpoint, namespace and user authorization. The client never supplies raw entry locators as authority. Historical zero-byte Activity sources are synthesized only by Floret on explicit expansion; Redeven must not duplicate those defaults.

Workspace updates carry facts only; unchanged sidebar-visible facts preserve cache identity at text-stream cadence. Each observer has exactly two cancellable reading slots, for the conversation and optional child panel. Computer assistance outside the selected interval uses server-only canonical evidence, which is not included in the bounded response. See [live delivery](../ui/flower-live-timeline.md) and [qualification](../operations/flower-thread-switch-qualification.md).

No database schema or migration changes are part of this optimization.

## Model output and presentation
[tool_result_encoding.go](../../internal/ai/tool_result_encoding.go) owns the single final result encoder: execution facts, tool content policy, final JSON, then Text and an independent Decoder.UseNumber Structured snapshot. Activity independently projects valid source data; its display truncation never changes model output. Floret applies the engine-owned uncertain-effect warning outside the tool payload budget, preserving complete JSON diagnostics in the next provider request and through restart/retry.

Its `request_key` remains the send idempotency identity used only to settle the short-lived browser outbox; the two values are not interchangeable.

Flower ask_user exposes only write and select_or_write. The latter always presents fixed choices with a separate custom-text answer, even when write_label is omitted. Floret owns normalization of historical select requests; Redeven does not add a second compatibility path. Ordinary InputRequired selection remains a separate contract.

The obsolete logged max_tool_calls declaration is removed because it never enforced a limit.

User and model updates enter Floret's shared journal writer with request identity and expected version. An existing unfinished Goal remains authoritative across continuation and context restoration.

Stop cancels execution and reflection; deletion only cancels future Goal checks.

Selecting or entering /goal opens an in-composer command chip.

Each popup opening confirms detail through the existing read coordinator before showing canonical text.

A failed binding leaves the draft available for retry; no cross-thread target validation is relaxed and no attachment is uploaded twice.

sections.title: Contract

## Mechanism
A Flower-generated plugin flow is a sequence of approved product actions over released ReDevPlugin APIs.

A plugin-generation handler may run already-approved local steps and call released ReDevPlugin adapters, but it must not perform its own approval wait, bypass Floret dispatch, mutate Flower activity rows directly, or convert plugin audit rows into Flower timeline state.

If a generated plugin needs a platform capability that does not exist in released ReDevPlugin, the requirement is recorded upstream instead of hidden behind a Redeven-local helper.

frontmatter.title: Flower storage ownership and migrations

concepts.summary:
- Authority: Floret owns canonical Agent data and its physical and logical formats; Redeven owns product facts, read state and uploaded resources.
- Outcome: supported existing data upgrades automatically and remains usable for new conversations.
- Invariants: stable database kinds, contiguous transactional migrations, immutable historical decoders, public Floret APIs and one service generation.
- Failure boundary: unknown formats, future versions, drift or failed validation block Flower without resetting data or disabling the core Runtime.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Storage owners
Redeven consumes the exact published Floret version in go.mod with `GOWORK=off`.

Floret owns bounded startup recognition and background per-thread migration. Each validated dependency closure publishes atomically; retained sources retire only after complete verification. The oldest v2-v5 snapshots reserve historical identities through a resumable scan before new-thread admission. Segmented stores admit new threads immediately. Redeven uses public status, thread preparation and per-thread media contracts and never decodes upstream records.

Published Floret v7.87.0 removes hidden Activity field preparation from ordinary startup, retains summary metadata on large activity admission, batches explicit locator writes and skips same-value SQLite upserts. Its recent manifest cache is bounded, memory-only and owned upstream. No new host indexes, full-text indexes or duplicate conversation storage are introduced. First disclosure may still prepare the selected complete activity once; this is not a claim of field-granular cold preparation.

Cancellation, shutdown and execution-context settlement resolve canonical control records through Floret. The host keeps the original Stop request and does not read or reconstruct upstream conversation bodies to settle it.

A read-state failure cannot become a core Runtime constructor failure or a synthetic read record.

## Readonly checks and owner transactions
`sqliteutil` owns WAL-aware readonly preflight, integrity checks and complete SQLite snapshots for product and read-state owners. Inspection never creates missing data or runs a migration.

Required upgrade snapshots precede Floret space maintenance and all migrations, as specified by the [backup and recovery contract](flower-backup-and-recovery.md).

## Frozen historical queue conversion
The migration-only `pendinginputlegacy` package owns the complete interpretation of historical queue bytes: session identity, options, context shapes, default values, resource metadata and normalization limits.

The v4-to-v5 product transaction imports canonical pending inputs through Floret's public idempotent import API, records necessary product authority and removes retired source tables before commit. The upgrade operation contains only target build, original snapshot identity and completion; owner versions and canonical records remain the progress authority.

## Resource and authorization retention
Product upload references retain resources for every canonical thread that contains them, including ordinary forks, nested forks and restored inputs.

After activation, product recovery pages settings, retains each thread's complete descriptors and promotes eligible admitted input. Failures retain the cleanup gate while independent threads recover. Tool-media collection keeps its complete global inventory, write gate and idle constraint.

Bounded keyset maintenance and compaction stop and drain with their owning generation.

concepts.summary:
Flower keeps intermediate files under the Runtime's application state and final
files at the user's destination. Redeven owns filesystem policy, bytes and UI;
published Floret owns tool results and conversation identities. No artifact
index, duplicated transcript, new Floret API or domain migration is introduced.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Placement

    <StateDir>/task-files/<ThreadID>/scratch
    <StateDir>/task-files/<ThreadID>/staging

Scratch retains helper scripts, intermediate data, screenshots and diagnostics
across turns. Staging is optional unfinished work. Admission and dynamic provider
preparation include the same absolute paths in the existing managed execution-
environment snapshot. The system prompt applies this rule even when intermediates
are retained for follow-up or a skill suggests project-relative temporary files.

Terminal child environments receive FLOWER_SCRATCH_DIR and FLOWER_STAGING_DIR.
There is no private FLOWER_OUTPUT_DIR. Project cwd, HOME, package caches and OS
temporary variables retain their existing semantics. Long thread paths are not
used as TMPDIR: Unix socket paths and CLI expectations must continue working.
OS temporary files retain OS lifecycle; persistent intermediates use scratch.

Final files go directly to the requested destination or established project
output location, otherwise the selected project/worktree. A temporary command
cwd does not change that destination. Users need no extra export step. Ordinary
project source, tests and conventional build outputs keep their existing paths.
Prompts cannot sandbox arbitrary shell or external-tool effects; no filename
heuristic silently reroutes project writes.

The task scope is a current-policy snapshot with one private writable root.
Sibling thread roots remain denied, including symlink aliases. Adding scratch
never expands normal project permissions. Fork uses a new writable scratch root; historical references never grant
access to an ancestor's working files.

## Fork continuity

Fork remains one action, without a working-file selector or technical warning.
Both current and historical conversation cuts inherit independent copies of the
source's current scratch/staging files. Conversation history stops at the selected
canonical item; working files are not historical filesystem snapshots. Project
files and final destinations remain shared and are never copied or redirected.

Preparation excludes new source filesystem admissions and cleanup, waits for
admitted operations with caller cancellation, and refuses unreaped background
processes. Copying uses rooted operations, bounded buffers, executable helper
preservation, source identity/size/time checks and a final tree validation. Only a
complete private staging tree is renamed into the new ThreadID directory.
Unsupported file types and external links fail without following them. No hard
links or writable parent aliases are created.

Product settings are published only after files are ready. Failed preparation is
not a visible/admitted product thread; replaying the same canonical Fork request
finishes preparation. An already admitted fork is never recopied, including after
its work files have been edited or explicitly cleaned. A small file-source marker
supports interrupted publication and dynamic context; it is not an artifact or
conversation ledger. Cleanup preserves the marker, while thread deletion removes
it with the private root. Unpublished copies are removed on failure and replaced
on retry after a process interruption.

The current execution-environment context tells the model to inspect inherited
files, map old scratch/staging paths by their relative suffix into its own root,
and repair hardcoded helper paths before execution. This applies to nested forks
without rewriting history or file contents. The model handles these details
internally; users are not asked to choose directory or snapshot behavior. Cleanup
or deletion of an ancestor cannot remove a descendant's independent files.

## Delivery and discovery

The file.present tool verifies a regular file outside application state, hashes
bytes with cancellation, checks file identity/size/modification consistency, and
returns its path, title, MIME, size, SHA-256, modification time, endpoint and
canonical thread/turn/run identities. It never moves, uploads or deletes the
file. A failed canonical result cannot remove an already-written user file.

The Files panel queries successful canonical file.present results through the
public authorized Floret query/read boundary. It pages 50 results, bounds each
record to 32 KiB, and preserves original provenance through Fork and restart.
There is no startup filesystem crawl or second durable delivery ledger. Read
permissions are checked again; canonical references are not authorization.

Available means the current file is accessible with unchanged size/modification
metadata. Changed, missing and unavailable states describe current observations;
listing does not rehash large files or assert byte-for-byte historical identity.
The stored hash describes delivery-time bytes. Final files remain user-owned and
mutable; no invisible version copies are created.

The shared desktop/mobile Files dialog shows final results first and expandable
working files second. Existing preview and directory actions retain their host
routing and HTML isolation. Hosts without those callbacks use the shared image,
PDF and text preview and a read-only directory listing. Source Runtime and actual
saved path stay visible.
Downloads use the existing native/browser save destinations and reauthorize each
256 KiB source chunk. Size/modification version drift or inconsistent offsets
abort the destination. Desktop routes admit only exact thread endpoints and
validated query keys. Downloads do not publish files or change their original
location. Browser Blob fallback retains its existing browser-memory behavior.

## Cleanup

The panel lists at most 200 working files and inspects at most 10,000 entries;
truncation and lower-bound totals are visible. Manual cleanup requires RWX and
an explicit confirmation. It removes only owned scratch/staging, with rooted
filesystem operations. Active/queued turns, pending interactions, admitted tool
work and unreaped terminal processes prevent cleanup. In-process admission
counts and the existing canonical view are sufficient; no durable cleanup ledger
or lease exists.

Thread deletion settles canonical work and terminates its owned terminal
processes before removing its private tree. Normal deletion refuses live work;
force deletion uses the existing explicit cancellation semantics. Final files
are never in cleanup scope. Archival has no automatic file deletion. No TTL is
enabled. Project-local application state is disclosed in the panel.

Legacy files scattered in a project remain untouched: names such as tmp or
task-evidence do not prove ownership. The existing file browser permits explicit
user inspection/deletion; this change does not guess legacy ownership or relocate
historical paths. Complete terminal-log retention and immutable file snapshots
remain separate capabilities and are not claimed here.

frontmatter.title: Flower canonical thread queries

concepts.summary:
Flower exposes two read-only tools for finding another readable conversation
and reading its content: `threads.query` and `threads.read`. The tool contract
is intentionally smaller than Floret's published general query API.
`threads.aggregate` is not registered or dispatched.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Find, browse, read

- `threads.query` defaults to `object: threads`, listing recently updated
  conversations first. Optional `title` is one literal, case-insensitive title
  fragment. Optional `thread_id` selects one exact conversation.
- To browse `messages` or `tool_calls`, provide one `thread_id`. Records are
  chronological; there are no model-controlled sort keys or detailed filters.
- `limit` defaults to 50, with a maximum of 200. Continue with `next_cursor` and
  unchanged input. Pass a record's `ref` to `threads.read` for complete content,
  following its cursor until no continuation remains.
- Nested `filter`, message-body matching, argument/result matching, keywords,
  phrases, time/role/tool/status predicates, grouping and aggregation are not
  accepted by the tool schema or handler. Unsupported inputs fail explicitly.
- Reasoning, secrets and private provider state remain excluded. Tool arguments
  and confirmed results are available only through authorized content reads.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
## Authorization owner

Authenticated session authority supplies read permission, user, endpoint and
namespace identity. Redeven reconstructs the readable scope for every page and
read. Tool parameters and returned references never grant authority. Changed
scope invalidates frozen cursors; a new query starts under current permission.
The adapter uses published Floret public APIs and never reads Floret SQL or
reconstructs canonical records.

## Historical results and presentation

Saved query/read results remain previewable after restart and after their
original refs expire. The historical aggregate result renderer remains solely
for immutable already-saved tool exchanges; it cannot dispatch aggregation.
Private query contents are not added to Activity snapshots. The intent label
and explicitly opened, bounded result preview remain the presentation boundary.

## Storage and execution

The canonical owner stores source locators and metadata. Flower requires no
full-text index and schedules no startup or background indexing. Metadata-only
browsing requests one thread's ordered records; canonical full content is read
only as needed. Floret's retired optional indexing declarations are not a
product capability. The engine's published query API may retain compatibility
filters without exposing those filters to Flower's model tools.

frontmatter.title: Flower MCP runtime

concepts.summary:
Redeven owns administrator-managed MCP configuration and a thin product adapter
over the released official Model Context Protocol Go SDK. The SDK owns stdio
and Streamable HTTP protocol sessions. Floret owns invocation identity,
approval, one-shot effect authorization, history, and recovery through the
[typed thread runtime](floret-thread-runtime.md). MCP must not introduce another
execution queue, lifecycle projection, or retry authority. A lost call outcome
is terminal and cannot be replayed. Invalid persisted configuration fails closed
without changing the original bytes.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Configuration and protocol
Configuration lives at `<stateDir>/ai/mcp.json`, with schema version 2, one monotonic configuration revision, and server revisions for optimistic edits. Persistence failure leaves the in-memory catalog unchanged.

Catalog limits are 32 servers, 128 tools per server, 32 KiB per schema, and 4 MiB total persisted configuration.

## Presentation icons
Save and explicit Check read `serverInfo.icons` from the existing SDK initialize result. Connection-preserving disabled edits retain icons; changed connection settings clear stale discovery.

Rejected sources receive the generated identity described in [the shared UI contract](../ui/flower-extensions.md#entry-icons).

## Execution and dependencies
Enabled, previously discovered tools join the dynamic tool surface before the existing permission filter. Their identity binds the exact server configuration and tool schema, so a changed or disabled configuration cannot execute through an old invocation name.

Enabled, checked configuration satisfies the catalog indicator; it does not promise current network reachability or bypass approval.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
MCP tools are conservatively mutating and open-world regardless of server annotation claims. An MCP handler cannot run directly without that proof.

Server tool errors and known connection failures remain distinct from an unknown execution outcome.

Redeven passes model output capability as Floret ModelMaxOutputTokens, and only an explicit per-request limit as MaxOutputTokens. It never maps capability to a fixed output reservation.

The comparison logs are /tmp/redeven-budget-desktop-failures-focused.log and /tmp/redeven-budget-desktop-main-baseline.log.

## Mechanism
Model reasoning capability, stream fields, history replay, and immutable thread settings are governed by [model reasoning capabilities and transport](model-reasoning-runtime.md).

Unsupported transports reject non-empty state before HTTP.

Hosted-turn diagnostics record the selected wire mode, and Floret lifecycle audit events carry batch index, batch size, event type, and observation time so operators can distinguish model serialization, provider single-call output, approval wait, dispatch, and completion without feeding diagnostics back into scheduling.

[Flower prompt and rule sources](flower-prompt-and-rule-sources.md) owns task, interaction, recovery, complete rule reading, and runtime-context admission policy.

## Related provider history
Provider-visible history, render lineage, and unavailable-tool continuity are owned by [Model provider surface and history](model-provider-surface-and-history.md).

## Related context usage
Usage accounting, context pressure, compaction, token budgets, and capacity failures are owned by [Model context usage and compaction](model-context-usage-and-compaction.md).

## Evidence and projection
Lifecycle evidence may retain frozen trigger candidates, pressure and validated replacement. Floret installs complete actor-owned context before publishing its version. Changed context bypasses text cadence; equal snapshots coalesce text in bounded queues. Redeven neither accumulates usage nor reconstructs lifecycle facts, invents budgets or infers capacity from weights.

## Timeline
One row between short separators uses a compact surface-owned tooltip without expansion or reflow. Success shows only canonical message counts as ≈ {before} → {after} tokens, never provider-request estimates. Localize missing-count, running and cancelled explanations. Wrap original errors without clipping; localize the fallback only when absent.

The tooltip follows the active surface and global theme outside chat. Prefer above, or below near the top boundary. Delay pointer-exit dismissal for hovering/selection. Escape, Tab, blur and outside clicks dismiss it; the visibility owner closes it on process collapse. Retain keyboard/touch access and independent retry.

sections.body:
## Native web-search observation
OpenAI Responses hosted search requests include `web_search_call.action.sources` so returned source URLs can reach the canonical Activity. Qwen requests keep their existing tool shape.

## Provider surface and history
Flower's provider prefix has one owner. Published Floret v7.37.0 keeps one append-only canonical history and keys each render lineage by the complete provider request surface: provider, model, reasoning, System Prompt, local and hosted tools, adapter, context policy, and provider-state compatibility.

Flower reads persisted Activity first and otherwise uses a neutral label and renderer without exposing arguments or unknown JSON.

## Provider rendering and estimation
Published Floret v7.26.0 owns `EstimateRenderedRequest` for local Responses, Chat Completions, Gemini signatures, Moonshot, and Anthropic. Verified model mappings select official vocabularies; unknown models use an explicit multilingual BPE proxy. These remain estimates because server rendering can differ; Redeven adds no network preflight or calibration ledger.

## Native request measurement
Published Floret v7.79.0 owns [native request measurement](model-request-measurement.md), frozen-prefix pressure and schema 28. Redeven maps protocol facts without a second pressure policy or measurement store.

## Provider request recovery
[Model request recovery](model-request-recovery.md) defines Engine-owned retry budgets, physical-request deadlines, attempt diagnostics and current-view feedback. Neither creates a second history owner.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Capability and transport
OpenAI-compatible Chat reasoning is capability-driven. Redeven reads only response fields named by that result, emits their fragments as reasoning without trimming provider whitespace, and never treats reasoning-only output as assistant body text.

Budget-only and fixed-thinking models never acquire synthetic effort names or a toggle merely because another model supports one.

## Default selection
Default asks for the model's own reasoning behavior. Thread creation, Thread
edits, and every Turn canonicalize it once, in
`config.CanonicalAIReasoningSelection`: on a model without verified reasoning
controls a budget-free Default is the omitted selection and is neither stored
nor sent. Default with a budget, Off, On, and named efforts remain explicit
intent and are rejected for such a model; personal memory keeps no reasoning
choice for it. Clients may send Default without knowing the model's capability
and must not drop or rewrite it themselves.

## Settings ownership
Thread model, reasoning and permission settings are Redeven product state. Execution authority records admission permission for historical attribution only, never as live tool authorization. The configured `current_model_id` initializes future threads only.

## Automatic titles
Published Floret v7.26.0 owns title reasoning and output limits. They never change the thread's saved reasoning choice or the main response policy.

The [live timeline contract](../ui/flower-live-timeline.md) owns canonical title status, persistence, and workspace-summary presentation.

sections.body:
Runtime/Desktop epoch 68 and model-source RPC v4 preserve Floret's effective request reuse policy. Adapters cannot broaden it.

Full input always owns estimates and fingerprints.

## Responses continuation configuration
`config.AIProvider.EffectiveResponsesContinuation` is the sole provider-level decision. Complete canonical input remains available when the ID is omitted.

No gateway-specific retry or alternative history owner is introduced.

## Cache usage presentation
The existing context tooltip shows the latest completed request and cumulative session cache hit rates. Recent counters project Floret's canonical confirmed usage directly and clear with its existing model/compaction boundaries. Historical cumulative usage is neither rewritten nor backfilled.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
HTTP and WebSocket use one Responses event consumer and send at most one generation per attempt. Unsupported upgrade, recoverable connection failure, interrupted streams, missing completion and precise pre-output stale continuation return to the Engine's existing budget and backoff.

There is no persistent transport history or second retry owner.

OpenAI request settings, continuation state, and input prefixes use SHA-256 only
as equality fingerprints for in-memory reuse decisions. These digests do not
store or verify user passwords and grant no authentication authority. Credential
rotation separately invalidates the live connection before another request.

concepts.title: OKF bundle lifecycle
concepts.description: Redeven builds a deterministic embedded OKF bundle from source Markdown concepts.

frontmatter.description: Redeven builds a deterministic embedded OKF bundle from source Markdown concepts.
frontmatter.title: OKF bundle lifecycle

concepts.summary: Redeven builds its embedded OKF bundle from curated source files under the top-level `okf/` authoring root, verifies deterministic dist outputs under `okf/dist/`, and embeds the resulting bundle into the binary used by Runtime and AI features for local retrieval.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
`build_assets.sh` invokes `build_okf_bundle.sh`, which runs `cmd/okf-bundle` against explicit source and dist roots. The builder emits the bundle, manifest and checksum deterministically. Summary and section bodies are embedded as structured data; Evidence remains in its source file but is omitted from ordinary concept opening unless requested. `okf/dist/*` is generated from source and is never an authoring surface.

## Quality gates
Report mode exposes layout, indexing, summary, evidence, duplication, lifecycle and budget issues without blocking cleanup. Strict mode fails structural and source-integrity violations, overdue reviews, and source totals above the hard cap. Final integration runs strict content quality after source integrity and before verifying the generated bundle.

## Source budget
Count Unicode characters in every source Markdown file under `okf/`, including the index and log, after CRLF-to-LF normalization; exclude `okf/dist/`. The report shows total, remaining capacity and index/concept/log usage. Exceeding 900,000 warns; strict quality accepts exactly 1,000,000 and fails above it. A per-concept `quality_exception` cannot waive this hard cap.

## Review and log lifecycle
Every concept declares `lifecycle` and `reviewed_at`: review contracts every 180 days, active measurements and operational evidence every 90 days, and retained history every 365 days. Retained history also needs a concise `retention_reason`. Report mode warns and strict mode fails on invalid or overdue metadata; expiry prompts review and never deletes a document automatically. Keep `log.md` to compact summaries from the last 30 days after durable knowledge moves into its concept.

## Index and retention
Keep categories and concept links in the index; the parser derives each retrieval summary from the concept's `# Summary`. Prefer an existing concept, preserve only decision-relevant historical conclusions and counterevidence, and remove obsolete detail from the current tree so Git history remains the recovery path.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The bundle remains auditable only while OKF Markdown concepts are the sole authoring surface, source and lifecycle budgets are enforced through the shared parser, and `okf/dist/*` stays a generated verification artifact set rather than hand-edited truth. A `quality_exception` may document a justified per-concept length exception, but it never waives the source cap or other quality checks.

frontmatter.title: OKF tool suite

concepts.summary: Redeven exposes the embedded OKF bundle through read-only `okf.index`, `okf.search`, and `okf.open` builtin tools. Redeven projects bounded safe results into Floret v7.26.0 structured Activity rows, and the shared Flower surface expands those rows without reading raw OKF result JSON.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
Runtime OKF code loads the embedded bundle once, indexes root directory sections, scores structured summaries and sections in memory, and opens a concept summary or one selected section by id or path. Internal ids, paths, and unfiltered result objects never enter that display contract. OKF activity labels and operation values come from `ToolPresentationSpec`, so the Floret projection does not own a separate OKF display vocabulary.

## Tool workflow
`okf.index` browses `okf/index.md` as a structured directory and returns summaries plus section counts. `okf.search` returns a bounded short candidate list with query-aware snippets and the best matching section id/title; title and Summary matches outrank section body matches.

Models should follow `okf.index -> okf.search -> okf.open Summary -> okf.open section` and must not rely on snippets for detailed contracts.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The tools return scoped Redeven repository knowledge and do not mutate OKF source or dist artifacts. They must not be used for current news, recent public events, market or pricing facts, third-party documentation, external facts, or general web facts. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
[Task-file placement](flower-task-files.md) supplies thread scratch/staging through
child-only environment variables while preserving project cwd and OS temporary
path conventions. Cleanup waits for owned terminal processes to be reaped.

PTYs use Floret execution/effect identities. `terminal.exec` waits 5 seconds when `yield_ms` is omitted or zero; positive values cap at 30 seconds. Yield returns a running process ID without stopping the command.

On macOS/Linux, one exit worker observes command exit without reaping, kills its process group, retires numeric signaling, verifies no live members within 2 seconds, then reaps and drains output. The unreaped root pins its PID through cleanup. Child cleanup preserves shell exit codes; only confirmed Stop termination means cancellation. Stop, input failure, the 30-minute limit and Service shutdown share this worker. Unconfirmed cleanup reports a runtime error and retains workload admission. Settlement stops the watchdog.

Long-lived commands stay foreground under the yielded process ID. Backgrounding and `nohup` cannot transfer ownership; escaping the PTY group/session is unsupported. Independent services need a managed lifecycle; previews use the managed browser. Names, CPU use and age never establish ownership.

`terminal.read` observes output after the caller's sequence for up to 60 seconds, returning early on output/exit. An expired observation retains process ID and cursor and reports `wait_expired`/`wait_ms`; `timed_out` means command timeout. Continue with the same ID and returned `last_seq`, without sleeps or command restarts.

Normal expiry uses Floret `BoundedWait`; Floret measures handler time and owns repeat protection. Immediate, failed, canceled and early reads gain no exemption, nor do neighboring repeated effects. No extra retry counter, clock, wake or durable ledger exists.

Reads are read-only effects: cancellation preserves process and cursor, then confirms the canceled result after observation returns. Execution/input retain shell-effect uncertainty rules. `terminal.write` bounds stdin; `terminal.terminate` kills the owned group and waits for reap/output drain. Thread Stop policy governs cleanup.

Read results contain incremental output, status, cursor, wait and exit facts. Command, cwd and timing remain in canonical Activity without repeated model echoes.

Browser payloads exclude local working paths, stdin, authorization proofs, and effect internals.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: No authority barriers, admission receipts, recovery handles or projection-cursor waits exist. Reads never retry settlement. Open-detail polling refreshes bytes, never canonical status or provider dispatch.

frontmatter.title: Tessiven Runtime discovery and operations

concepts.summary:
The Runtime-owned Tessiven product service is the authority for UI and Flower
Runtime discovery and dispatch. It composes the existing Desktop connection
registry, authenticated Gateway catalogs, Runtime business resource executors,
and Desktop lifecycle coordinator. Discovery observes registered paths without
starting a process or acquiring a business session. A reference identifies one
path; it grants no permission. Lost source authority, changed path generations,
replaced identities, and revoked permissions stop dispatch. A lost mutation
response reports an uncertain canonical tool outcome. The model first inspects
the original operation or current state before deciding what work remains; the
original invocation never replays automatically.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Official surface
- `tessiven.runtimes` / `GET /_redeven_proxy/api/tessiven/runtimes` returns   independent source availability and exact target paths. - `tessiven.runtime.inspect` / `POST .../runtimes/inspect` reads status,   bounded public diagnostics, or the original Desktop operation. - `tessiven.runtime.action` / `POST .../runtimes/actions` requests connection   or one supported `start`, `stop`, `restart`, or `update` process operation. - `tessiven.inspect/action` retain the canonical canvas version, bound instance,   and resource identity checks for Managed Services and containers.

No sibling module, replacement SDK, or product lifecycle queue is introduced.

## Source authority and discovery
Desktop registers its Tessiven host through owner-authenticated private Runtime control. Web Service, CodeSpace, nested frame, unrelated-origin and worker requests cannot declare a native source;

Ambiguous references fail closed.

## Connection and business access
Explicit connect reuses saved configuration and existing connection leases.

It cannot carry claimed permission flags, an arbitrary URL, another Runtime reference, or a process-lifecycle action.

Member removal and replacement retire the transport; no local or alternate route is substituted.

## Native lifecycle handoff
Process actions use saved direct Desktop placements and the existing [Desktop lifecycle owner](../desktop/desktop-runtime-process-lifecycle.md). The model cannot choose a download URL or release version; the existing release selector owns updates and post-operation verification.

Unknown connection outcomes require checking the selected connection in its native owner rather than retrying.

sections.title: Boundaries

The Connected environments panel and Runtime node entry use this same service. The Runtime Dialog is part of the loaded Tessiven page; opening it must not suspend the page or show its navigation loading placeholder.

Gateway v6 application access, Tessiven DSL, and persistent database lineages retain their current shapes.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Default Flower tools omit write_todos; historical Todo results remain readable. The Floret-native goal tool has independent control ownership; see [Flower Goals](flower-goals.md).

## Mechanism
The registry includes readonly file/search helpers, standard mutation, patch, terminal, web search, OKF, interaction, skill, subagent, MCP, and Floret-native tools. Structured detail uses Floret's bounded typed rows; operation, status, repeated names, and raw tool fields never create an expand affordance.

The resolver validates MIME, size, and digest through the target-owned media store; it never stores image bytes in durable tool state.

## File editing

Redeven owns Flower patch execution. Local edits use the filesystem registry;
patch and move paths must resolve inside cwd. Relative and absolute paths are
accepted. Symlinks and new-file ancestors resolve before approval; execution
rechecks approved canonical targets. Readonly roots reject writes. Target-routed
tools retain target-owned policy.

Use file.edit for unique literal replacements, file.write for complete files,
and apply_patch for multi-chunk/file changes. Its strict JSON input argument and
declared routing fields have no patch or input_format aliases. Model names never
imply endpoint support for freeform grammar.

Chunks search original content forward, honoring anchors, EOF and numeric ranges.
Only order failures allow reordering: every chunk needs one exact, non-overlapping
match, without anchors, ranges, EOF markers or pure additions. Sorted chunks use
the same matcher and write plan. Forward patches, recorded arguments and rejection
classifications remain unchanged. Ambiguity names the blocking chunk and requests
unique context. The provider still requests source order.

Pure additions append. Untouched lines retain their endings; insertions use the
first ending (LF for empty files), and nonempty updates retain a final newline.
Exact matching precedes whitespace and punctuation normalization. Explicit Add
and Move may replace regular files. Use one operation per canonical path.

Diagnostics distinguish order, overlap, anchor, EOF, repeated/missing context and
duplicate paths, with chunk, patch-body line, search boundary, exact source line
when available, and a remedy. They never select writes. Floret validates JSON.

Plans validate before writing and recheck source/destination snapshots per commit.
Validation errors confirm no writes; commit errors report completed operations
and uncertain effects, never permission to replay. Replacement is atomic per
file, not per patch. Success retains confirmed paths/counts; canonical Activity
retains before/after diffs and format metadata.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- Independently detect one service per engine without scanning/fallback. Each discovery has a two-second total budget shared by its commands; the concurrent engines cannot consume each other's budget. Reuse the selected endpoint inventory when binding health probes. [Resource readiness](container-resources-capability.md) remains independently bounded.
- Docker Desktop ownership comes from the selected local `desktop-linux`/`desktop-windows` context or an exact endpoint-address alias of it. An installed Desktop plugin does not claim another local engine or remote context. Validate management using `docker desktop version --format json`, then read engine health from the bound endpoint. Never run the slow `desktop status` command during discovery.
- Once the active context establishes Desktop ownership, management/health errors retain its service ID, implementation, configuration sources, and supported lifecycle actions. Report missing CLI, permission, timeout, and unknown failures explicitly; they never establish a stopped state. The API and UI allow Start only when stopped and Stop/Restart only when running. Configuration save-and-restart requires known running/stopped state before any write; plain save remains available. Resolve Podman Machine ownership before probing its remote health.
- Start/stop/restart use typed service actions. Lifecycle commands share a two-minute budget across their steps, independent of the ten-second query timeout and two-second discovery budget. Parent cancellation/deadlines still apply. On macOS, Start opens the official application with LaunchServices (`/usr/bin/open -g -b com.docker.docker`), then polls the reviewed local endpoint with bounded read-only probes until ready. Restart first stops Desktop under the same deadline. Other Desktop platforms and Stop retain the official CLI. Launch acceptance alone never establishes success; final state is reloaded before success. Never invoke sudo/pkexec/polkit, prompt for elevation, alter groups or socket permissions. Keep operation locked until fresh authoritative final state.
- Read-gated `GET /_redeven_proxy/api/container-resources/services` exposes access mode/source IDs; one source failure cannot hide another. Contiguous migrations map legacy state to `engine` and `client_proxy` to `docker_cli`.
- Service actions and configuration changes use one confirmation: preflight first, then show the service name, localized risks and supplied impact counts, with an explicit Start/Stop/Restart/Save action. Never require retyping the service name or another review step. The client binds the displayed name to the request; the server still validates identity, permissions and request/plan hashes. Cancel creates no operation; duplicate submission stays locked. Hashes and raw backend prose are never rendered; operation history resolves service names and localizes public errors.
- One Container services Settings action carries warnings. Refresh retains cards, animates only its indicator and reports inline errors. A known Desktop with uncertain health retains its Start control, disabled with state guidance; successful revalidation enables the same control. Service cards show action-specific pending state, elapsed time, localized recovery guidance, status revalidation, cancellation and secondary operation history without opening a drawer automatically. Unmeasured service work has no percentage bar. Operation completion through either SSE or fallback polling reloads authoritative service and runtime facts.
- Cards prioritize observed service health. Active operations retain feedback and action locks. Terminal start/restart failures leave the card when running is observed; stop failures leave when stopped is observed. Unknown health and configuration failures retain actionable feedback. Completed/canceled records remain in secondary history. This changes presentation only: running does not prove a previous restart succeeded. History retains its original outcome, localized error and duration alongside separately labeled current service status; it never renders an empty error panel or a historical duration as current progress.

frontmatter.title: Native container operation observation

concepts.summary:
Every native Containers mutation has one durable Redeven operation identity and
one resource-local lock. Submission, cancellation, progress events, restart
recovery, and terminal reconciliation flow through `containerresource`.
Inventory refreshes and UI observation never become a second lifecycle owner.
Lost submissions, stale plans, runtime restarts, and unavailable engines are
reported explicitly and are never hidden behind automatic replay.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Admission and serialization
The operation key contains engine, opaque endpoint ID, resource kind, and canonical identity.

Reusing a request ID with different hashes produces an idempotency conflict instead of a second operation.

## Execution, cancellation, and events
The service owns an operation context from queued state through reconciliation. Cancellation is an explicit API action; closing Activity, Workbench, an inspector, an event stream, or the browser never implies cancellation.

Terminal errors use a small public taxonomy for storage, registry availability, rate limiting, not-found, and access denial; the drawer maps known codes to localized guidance alongside the durable timeline. Unknown codes use a localized generic failure; codes and backend messages remain diagnostic evidence, not visible UI copy. Timeout guidance acknowledges that host work may still be in progress. Desktop service cards direct users to its native application for setup/startup recovery and expose status revalidation. Service history shows state transitions without generic execution stages or a synthetic percentage bar.

## Authoritative terminal observation
After engine execution returns, the service reloads the exact endpoint-bound resource or relevant bounded inventory.

The operation is never replayed, regardless of whether the resource appears present or absent.

## UI observation
Inventory requests and streams are fenced by source runtime, endpoint, resource view, and request generation. A superseded response cannot replace current data.

Mobile and desktop expose the same state and cancellation authority. Service lifecycle feedback stays on its card; history is secondary. Polling terminal transitions refresh authoritative service/runtime facts even when the event stream was lost. The portaled operation drawer owns its responsive container; narrow drawers stack history and details without horizontal overflow.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: - The database is operation evidence, not a mutation queue or replay journal. - UI inventory and SSE consumers observe service authority; they do not own   lifecycle state or reconciliation. - A runtime restart converts active work to interrupted after read-only   observation; it never assumes success or retries the command. - The full native container ownership contract is defined in   [Native container resources](container-resources-capability.md).

concepts.summary:
- Authority: each repository migrates the schemas it owns; Redeven owns product databases, while Floret and ReDevPlugin own their internal stores.
- Outcome: each Redeven product store opens through an exact versioned schema contract before the dependent service accepts requests.
- Invariants: released migration lineages are contiguous, atomic, verified, and data-preserving; existing-file preflight reads the complete SQLite main-plus-WAL view, while future, drifted, wrong-kind, and unsupported inputs fail without changing database files or sidecars.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Redeven-owned stores
Each SQLite store declares a stable database kind, current version, supported minimum version, ordered `n -> n+1` migrations, an existing-schema validator, and a final exact verifier.

Migration and verification failure rolls back.

Host identity upgrades use their own private journal and native verification after Registry migration; no live-engine guess or database reset substitutes for resource ownership.

## Upstream-owned stores
Floret owns canonical thread storage and its schema lifecycle through the published Runtime APIs.

Cross-database atomicity is never assumed or simulated by copying upstream lifecycle state into Redeven tables.

concepts.summary: Floe Webapp owns one HTTP proxy runtime per connected Env App session. All built-in browser event subscriptions and the ReDevPlugin host request adapter use that runtime's logical streams. They cannot occupy native HTTP/1.1 connection slots, choose another upstream or identity, or create a second transport. Session replacement and teardown cancel old observations. Each feature retains its existing recovery policy; stopping observation never cancels background business work.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## One session and one request path
Product subscriptions call the Shell-bound session event reader. Floe Webapp's acquisition lifecycle opens a logical HTTP stream on the current Flowersec session and parses SSE with its shared bounded parser.

Session multiplexing removes those event requests from the browser HTTP pool; changing request priority alone cannot do so.

## Authority and resource lifetime
Local session issuance declares only Env App API and plugin API paths plus the plugin CSRF and expected-management-revision headers. Remote issuers must declare the same plugin request authority and upload cap in their signed scope.

Product code must not reset a successful response while its bytes are still being consumed.

## Observation and recovery
Flower maintains one workspace stream; thread selection never reconnects it.

Its transport and cancellation regression coverage remain intact.

sections.body: An observer cannot choose another upstream, session identity or native HTTP transport. Ending an observation does not cancel the feature's background business operation.

concepts.title: Cross-platform host application behavior
concepts.description: Compare aligned user operations and operating-system limits for macOS and Linux host applications.

frontmatter.description: Compare aligned user operations and operating-system limits for macOS and Linux host applications.
frontmatter.title: Cross-platform host application behavior

concepts.summary:
Host Applications separates viewing, sharing, window closure and process exit on
both platforms. Ordinary actions preserve unsaved work and respect app cancellation.
Only an independently confirmed Force quit may bypass saving. The backend owns
process evidence, and the interface names the actual supported operation. OS
session, display and service policies remain authoritative; unavailable recovery
must not silently relaunch an unrelated or replacement process.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
| Operation | macOS | Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Close outer Desktop window / browser popup | Release this client lease; app survives | Same |
| Network loss, reload, second viewer | Reconnect same live app; stale input is revoked | Same |
| Release this client lease | End this capture/route; other clients and app survive | End this proxy/route; other clients and app survive |
| No window for more than 40 seconds | Waiting, with native menu/reopen | Waiting, reconnect same process without relaunch |
| Close last window | Viewer closes; app decides whether its process exits | Same |
| Cancel normal close/quit | Preserve application and save dialog | Same; ordinary control is Close all windows |
| Explicit Force quit in library | Confirm loss warning; exact AppKit instance | Confirm loss warning; exact owned backend and descendants |
| Orderly Runtime shutdown or process exit | Native app remains discoverable | Private display survives; new Runtime verifies/reconnects it |
| Running list | Regular apps in the logged-in OS session | Caller-owned Redeven instances, including detached/windowless apps |
| Host reboot / display server destruction / OS cleanup | No survival guarantee | Same; Runtime cgroup cleanup may also end its virtual display |

## Accepted operations and visible state
Quit and force-quit requests are asynchronous. The Host Applications surface must close the confirmation dialog after acceptance and show a per-application pending state until the authoritative running snapshot confirms the target instance is gone.

The first Force quit action only enters that state; only its final confirmation sends the destructive host request.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Linux cannot generically request AppKit-style application quit or reopen, nor adopt an arbitrary process on another display. macOS requires its real logged-in graphical session and explicit capture/input permissions. Neither backend can preserve an application after its OS or display environment has been destroyed.

## Independent execution
Host launches in its own session and process group. The foreground start contract remains: templates must not double-fork, background the application, or retain a permanent wrapper.

This is not a resident service supervisor or another binary.

## Native identity and recovery
The `host:v3` identity binds service ID, launch nonce, PID, and a digest of native facts:

New identities never use formatted dates, timezone, command text, or `kern.boottime`.

An old process's inherited output descriptors cannot be replaced externally; independent output handling takes effect on its next explicit restart.

## Opening and presentation
Host supplies verified native launch identity and executes only the applied authorized hooks through the common [managed opening contract](managed-web-service-opening.md). The driver stores only launch facts and after-start hook completion, never executable snapshots or a second entrance cache. Preparation follows healthy startup and can be retried without stopping the application.

## Mechanism
`localui.Server` is built with an agent, Code App app server, bind spec, runtime-control socket path, Local Environment identity, diagnostics store, and optional access gate.

Local UI bind parsing accepts `localhost`, canonical loopback IP literals, concrete non-loopback unicast IPv4 and IPv6 literals, and the `0.0.0.0` and `::` wildcards.

In-process maps retain only active-session cleanup projections and never authorize a request.

## Concurrent shutdown
Context cancellation and explicit shutdown enter the same serialized close path. Runtime-control and management status serialize start/close and protect endpoint reads, so overlapping shutdown cannot dereference cleared servers or advertise a retired control listener. This uses bounded in-process locks and does not introduce durable lifecycle state.

Opening settings never resizes the app.

A browser advertising H.264 WebCodecs software decoding can receive VideoToolbox hardware video. Hardware encoder unavailability uses JPEG images; a browser decoder failure explicitly renegotiates image transport.

## Waiting and process lifetime
A running process without its first shareable window remains attached indefinitely; there is no first-window termination deadline. Releasing the current client lease during this wait ends that sharing lease normally; missing pixels do not turn a lease release into a launch failure. An unexpected helper exit is a failed sharing session, not evidence that the host application ended.

## Window evidence
The window registry distinguishes present, unknown and confirmed-empty inventories. No first-window deadline is introduced.

## Capture and recovery
Capture availability is independent of lifetime. AX identity survives a capture-surface replacement while the input generation is renewed; retired callbacks cannot update the replacement. Failure to launch and unexpected helper loss remain failures; missing pixels do not change a confirmed process exit into a failed launch.

## Terminal state
Terminal state retains the native end reason: `application_exited` confirms the bound process exited, `windows_closed` confirms its last shared window closed, and `sharing_stopped` confirms detachment. Closing windows and stopping sharing never claim the process has quit. The [lifecycle validation matrix](../operations/host-application-lifecycle.md) separates automated recovery evidence from OS/application compatibility limits.

sections.title: Contract

TemplateSpec 7 accepts exactly one entrance source: a fixed endpoint path, the supported Host opening hook, or `startup_url.line_prefix`. Container and Compose never acquire permission to run Host scripts.

## One preparation owner
`open-session` observes the applied instance, prepares its entrance through one common owner, checks endpoint availability, and revalidates generation, applied identity, Forward and management state before handoff.

List and inspection never prepare an entrance or execute opening hooks.

Changed business scripts and settings still require their normal lifecycle review.

## Browser outcome and recovery
`ready` means the entrance is ready for browser handoff.

Trusted IPC accepts only bounded replies from that same live main frame.

Per-service progress follows [Web Services interface](web-services-interface.md).

`scripts/qualify_managed_web_opening.sh` is the dedicated real-service lane. A failed Electron runtime preflight is an explicit environment failure; qualification cannot alter macOS trust or sign dependencies.

frontmatter.title: Plugin process sessions

concepts.summary:
ReDevPlugin Process Broker is the single platform owner for local processes
requested by plugins. Redeven supplies the authenticated user and environment
scope, permission decision, minimal environment, secret resolver, state root,
audit sink, and diagnostic sink; it does not expose a second process protocol.
The observable outcome is an opaque session handle and bounded binary stdin,
stdout, and stderr operations. The failure boundary is explicit: process
output may be lost after a bounded buffer overflows, and Host shutdown,
disable, uninstall, revocation, or owner teardown terminates owned processes.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Ownership and isolation
Every session binds plugin instance, user scope, environment scope, plugin invocation/session, and client key. Start requests contain an executable and argv array; ReDevPlugin never parses an implicit shell command string.

Secret references are resolved by the Host adapter and values do not cross the UI, error, audit, or diagnostic projections.

## Streams and lifecycle
The first contract supports non-PTY stdin, stdout, and stderr only. Each output stream has an independent cursor and bounded ring buffer.

The platform removes the session after close and prevents access after owner revocation.

concepts.summary:
Redeven owns remote desktop authorization, ephemeral sessions, window placement,
configuration and audit. Published `floe-native-apps` owns current-desktop
selection, OS authorization, native input, capture, codecs, bounded playback and
Linux component acquisition and the privileged physical-desktop service.
A desktop session shares the existing signed-in macOS or Linux desktop. It never
creates an application-private desktop, changes system security policy or grants
access to a lower-permission user. Disconnect releases remote input and media;
host applications and unsaved work survive. Platform unavailability revokes
input and requires a fresh active frame before recovery.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Admission and ownership
`/_redeven_proxy/api/remote-desktop` is independent from application launch. Every session and forward belongs to the authenticated user; renderer-supplied identity never authorizes a route.

The same policy fences new admission under the manager lock, so an HTTP request authorized before revocation cannot recreate the removed desktop.

## Platform boundary
macOS uses the exact remote Swift package in the existing Runtime helper.

The canonical official Alpine source remains the final fallback; every download still checks the expected size and SHA-256 before atomic cache publication, and a failed archive download can move to the next trusted source.

Capability normalization also applies to a retried connection after accepting or declining takeover, so a removed display cannot return through the stored request.

## Media and office interaction
Control and media travel through separate Flowersec native proxy streams bound to the same product attachment. Cancellation retires the selection and releases held keys; lock-screen input cannot use that text path.

Native session and frame authority remain governed by this concept.

sections.title: Boundaries

The [desktop media contract](remote-desktop-media.md) owns low-delay video, encoder selection and Wayland capture/input scheduling.

sections.body:

An authenticated inherited descriptor attaches media; bounded backpressure retires attachment instead of blocking input release. Encoder reset begins a new keyframe chain without discarding transported references.
- Intel AV1 uses publisher-verified pinned amd64 musl media-driver/GMM in the private closure, never the root DRM exporter. Copies are intentional, not zero-copy claims.
- Wayland cursor-free pixels/shapes come from one authorized PipeWire stream. Cursor-only buffers cannot restore a lost baseline. [Wayland evidence](../operations/remote-desktop-wayland-optimization-results.md) distinguishes native/browser from physical latency results.

concepts.summary: Remote control and data artifacts are opaque, single-spend capabilities. Redeven binds each Lease to one digest-global tombstone, persists idempotent bootstrap and top-up request identities, and rejects stale, duplicate, malformed, expired, or cross-environment responses before a connection can consume them. Pool replenishment and relink are terminal state transitions, never silent fallback.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Before any remote data or control artifact can be spent, its Lease callback creates and fsyncs one no-overwrite ledger tombstone keyed only by the artifact's SHA-256 digest. Product channel, generation, sequence, and wrapper labels cannot create a second burn identity for the same opaque artifact.

A legacy local `Direct` config has no matching Portal-side durable sequence authority, so Redeven erases it into a revoked digest tombstone and requires relinking instead of importing it as usable capacity.

Compatibility epoch 35 requires both Desktop and Runtime to understand explicit reasoning `on` alongside the existing default, off, effort, and budget choices. Earlier clients reject `on`; ordinary epoch admission prevents a mixed pair from accepting a Flower or Desktop model-source request it cannot interpret. See the [reasoning selection contract](../ui/flower-reasoning-selection.md) for model capability and control semantics.

Epoch 59 pairs Runtime authorization requests with the shared Desktop and Env App OpenAI account picker. A saved registry requires an account selection or explicit new-registration intent; old Desktop clients must update before Flower access. Registration semantics belong to the [ChatGPT account lifecycle](../ai/chatgpt-account-lifecycle.md).

Epoch 65 requires the model directory's backend-owned default_fetch_source field in provider search policies. See [model web search](../ai/model-web-search.md).

Epoch 67 requires complete changed pin metadata in Flower pin confirmations. New pins append to the endpoint's existing order; Desktop and Runtime must agree on the changed ranks and revisions before a confirmation is accepted. See [sidebar pin ordering](../ui/flower-thread-sidebar.md).

concepts.summary: The Monitor service owns environment CPU, memory, network, and process sampling. Its cached snapshot is the authority for both the Monitoring page and Workbench. The service refreshes system metrics every two seconds and process metrics every ten seconds.

Totals are not a persisted usage ledger and are not reset to zero when Redeven starts.

## Network accounting

Interface topology changes retain the existing aggregate-counter rate behavior rather than introducing a second rate algorithm.

concepts.title: Web Service management recovery
concepts.description: Keep service facts, user goals, resource cleanup, and management archives actionable across failures and Runtime restarts.

frontmatter.description: Keep service facts, user goals, resource cleanup, and management archives actionable across failures and Runtime restarts.
frontmatter.title: Web Service management recovery

concepts.summary:
- Authority: the Registry owns management records and lifecycle transactions; the Manager observes resources and determines actions; the Renderer presents that decision.
- Outcome: every service explains its current situation, the last operation's result, and an available next step in Activity and Workbench.
- Invariants: historical failures never determine current resource state; unavailable inspection never means absence; destructive effects require fresh ownership and explicit cleanup choices.
- Failure boundary: an administrator with a working Registry can detach even when the engine is offline. Detachment preserves resources and never claims that business processes stopped.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Facts and actions
`ServiceFacts` separates presence, ownership, runtime state, inspection completeness, resource references, and check time.

Frontend code never substitutes Retry or Restart for unavailable Start.

A failed Host maintenance hook may be bypassed only through an administrator's reviewed plan, and only for verified resources.

## Review and execution
`GET /managed-web-services/{id}/inspection` requires read permission, is non-cacheable, and uses the same factual backend projection as the list.

Existing unrelated lifecycle transactions cannot be overwritten by recovery.

Instance-scoped allocation and legacy resource boundaries are owned by [Service resource ownership](service-resource-ownership.md).

## Uninstall transaction
Uninstall uses `runtime_manifest_json`, the existing operation coordinator, and the existing event stream.

A resource recreated under the same name cannot acquire the previous deletion authorization.

Detachment remains available while it is unresolved.

## Management archives and access
Registry version 4 adds `active`, `detached`, and `uninstalled`. Only active records participate in template uniqueness and must own an authorized Forward.

Names, ports, or cached reachability never prove ownership.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The contiguous `portforward_registry_v2` 3-to-4 migration preserves bindings, configuration, private-file references, operation history, and existing resource locations. Failed migration rolls back completely; unknown versions and structural drift remain read-only failures. Desktop/Runtime compatibility epoch 15 covers these management contracts.

frontmatter.title: Redeven Service Template format compatibility

concepts.summary:
- Authority: the released `redeven-service-templates/template` package owns schemas, historical data adapters, and current types. Runtime owns authorization and execution.
- Outcome: formally supported old template directories remain usable after a Redeven upgrade, with their original filenames, bytes, modes, digest, and source commit intact.
- Invariants: compatibility operates in memory, feeds one current executor, never persists an adapted execution definition, and never installs, upgrades, or restarts a service by itself.
- Failure boundary: invalid historical shapes, ambiguous entrypoints, incorrect identity, and future formats fail explicitly without altering files. Unsupported formats require a compatible release or author correction.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Identity and version matrix
Current authors use `redeven-service-template.json` with fixed `kind: "redeven.service-template"`, source `schema_version: 4`, author `template_id`, `service_family_id`, positive `revision`, `default_locale`, and `locales`, followed by the full display and execution declaration.

| Entrypoint | Source document | Execution input | Effective execution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `template.json` | 1 | TemplateSpec 3 | TemplateSpec 7 |
| `template.json` | 2 | TemplateSpec 4, 5, or 6 | TemplateSpec 7 |
| `redeven-service-template.json` | 3 | TemplateSpec 6 | TemplateSpec 7 |
| `redeven-service-template.json` | 4 | TemplateSpec 7 | TemplateSpec 7 |

The branded filename requires the branded document.

## Adaptation and execution ownership
The reader strictly decodes the historical document, applies consecutive data transformations, validates current TemplateSpec and passive resources, then returns the current typed definition. Historical syntax never grants extra privileges.

The npm SDK publishes the corresponding types, schemas, and GitHub acquisition contract; it does not execute services or migrate databases.

sections.body:
[Git source ownership](managed-service-git-sources.md) defines original-directory storage and review. Reading an older directory or upgrading Redeven never renames `template.json`, rewrites scripts/locales, changes the stored digest or commit, or creates a normalized template row.

[Database migrations](database-schema-migrations.md) retain their exact lineage, shape checks, rollback, and read-only rejection rules.

concepts.summary:
Tessiven is the Runtime-owned library of immutable service canvases. Each
canvas stores a complete `redeven.io/tessiven/v1.1.0` YAML document and every save
creates a new version. The Runtime is the single owner of canvas data; the
Desktop Welcome surface and the local Env App render that same library. A
failed validation or version conflict leaves the last saved document intact.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- A canvas document contains stable IDs for Runtime nodes, visual groups,   business services, instances, external resources, relations, and evidence. - Every service has at least one instance on an existing node. A missing   placement fails validate/save at the service ID with a source location. - A service kind describes its primary responsibility independently of its   product name, instance role or deployment format. The [DSL versioning contract](tessiven-dsl-versioning.md)   owns version selection, read projections and write upgrades.

The `tessiven_canvas_library` SQLite lineage starts at schema v1. Canvas identities, archive state, immutable YAML versions, and idempotent request results remain intact.

A fresh v2 library and an upgraded v1 library must both reopen successfully.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The local Runtime owns the SQLite canvas library and immutable version documents. Canvas references never authorize resource actions; the [Flower and operations contract](../ai/tessiven-flower-and-operations.md) owns that boundary. Tessiven does not deploy services, discover targets in the background, or synchronize libraries between devices.

data-only `redeven.io/tessiven-presentation/v1` display model. Native clients
render that model using bundled code. A DSL release does not by itself change
the display format or require a client release. Historical YAML, its digest,

An unsupported source retains verified source for viewing and export but does
not invent topology. Integrity failure returns an error without an exportable

Under `/_redeven_proxy/api/tessiven`, `GET /presentation-contract` returns `formats` and `capabilities`. Unknown well-formed capabilities are ignored rather than treated as authority.

The initial optional `group_layouts` capability enables authored group packing; without it automatic layout preserves the same memberships and relationships.

## Compatibility And Authority
The frozen schema is independent of the DSL registry. Existing display meanings must not change in place.

Resource requests continue to read the original version, check exact bindings and enforce current permissions.

Removing a supported display format requires an explicit client compatibility-window decision; a DSL release cannot remove it incidentally.

frontmatter.title: Tessiven DSL versioning

concepts.summary:
The Runtime owns Tessiven DSL schema selection and explicit forward migrations.
New documents use `apiVersion: redeven.io/tessiven/v1.1.0`. Supported legacy
`redeven.io/tessiven/v1` and `v1.0.0` remain readable through the reviewed
`v1 -> v1.0.0 -> v1.1.0` chain. Each edge updates only the version scalar;
new group packing rules are opt-in and older documents retain automatic layout. Reads project current structured data while preserving historical YAML,
digest and revision identity. Authorized edits save a new current snapshot.
Unknown versions, invalid source/target documents or migration failures leave

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Version Identities And Releases
DSL identities use stable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` strings, for example `v1.2.3`.

Paths must be unique, acyclic and complete, with source validation, target validation and semantic checks. Do not introduce a schema-only registry entry without its executable migration and fixtures.

## Read Compatibility
Validation selects the exact source schema, applies the explicit upgrade chain, and validates the current shape and cross-object contracts. Returned `document` is canonical current data.

The [canvas contract](tessiven-canvas-contract.md) owns those semantic rules.

Native rendering uses the independently frozen [canvas presentation contract](tessiven-canvas-presentation.md), not the current DSL identity. Every DSL release must verify its explicit mapping to the oldest supported display contract without rewriting source or granting resource authority.

Ordinary edits valid in the original schema continue to upgrade automatically; no historical YAML is rewritten.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
## New Snapshots And Failure Boundary
Creation, imports, full save and exact edits write the current DSL. Existing history is never bulk-rewritten.

The [canvas storage contract](tessiven-canvas-contract.md) continues to own atomic startup database upgrades independently.

Rows have a 64px minimum, never a fixed height.

Long explanations wrap inside the visible boundary in either theme.

Older or unknown targets retain the stop-first flow and require a second explicit update after stopping; an initially stopped service remains stopped after update.

## Resource intent and route ownership
After starting the selected CodeSpace, Env App submits `mode: browser` and its CodeSpace ID through the same root-frame-only IPC used for built-in editor windows.

Only main can mint an entry from the gateway object.

Runtime and editor traffic never carries the browser cookie; upstream responses cannot set the reserved cookie name.

An OS-open failure closes the newly acquired gateway and route.
