concepts.title: Desktop development sessions and bundles
concepts.description: Own development services, credentials and bundle retention.

frontmatter.description: Own development services, credentials and bundle retention.
frontmatter.title: Desktop development sessions and bundles

concepts.summary:
- Authority: the launcher owns Desktop, local Runtime, saved local Gateways, and bundles.
- Outcome: run current source, stop together, prune obsolete bundles.
- Invariants: preserve user data, identities, unrelated services, and recent, selected or live bundles.
- Failure boundary: preparation errors clean up; incomplete inventory prevents pruning.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Service lifecycle
`scripts/dev_desktop.sh` builds current tracked/non-ignored source and captures HEAD.
Reject concurrent edits. Generated OKF and ignored assets are outputs; protect
OKF sources, builders and Go embeds.

The development launcher owns a profile-local build receipt. Reuse requires
matching HEAD and tracked/non-ignored source bytes (including dirty files),
dependency contents, toolchains, target and build settings, and byte-verified
Desktop output plus immutable Runtime bundle. Missing, altered or incomplete
outputs rebuild; failed preparation never launches a previous bundle. Concurrent
source/input changes fail before launch. A newly installed pinned Rust toolchain
is the only admitted preparation-time toolchain transition.

`--rebuild` forces build preparation; `REDEVEN_AGENT_FORCE_INSTALL=1` reinstalls
all three JavaScript packages once and forces preparation. Package manifests
select pnpm or npm; successful install receipts bind manifests, selected locks
and toolchain identity. Compatibility lockfiles do not select a second installer.
The first launch after this change installs once to establish these receipts.

Development Rust staging may reuse profile-owned Cargo registry/target caches,
while installing the exact locked published crate into fresh staging. Digest,
executable and consumption checks still run and product evidence is regenerated.
After verifying the cached published crate and resolving its locked dependencies
offline, development installs without registry requests. Incomplete caches report
the offline diagnostic and use the configured acquisition policy; corrupt crates
fail, and compiler failures are not retried through a different path.
Release staging always has isolated Cargo directories. Source changes conservatively
rebuild the full product; this is not per-component or watch-mode compilation.
Development overlaps Desktop compilation with Runtime preparation. Within the
Runtime, embedded-assets/Go, verified plugin staging and Computer resources run
independently. Env App, Code App and knowledge assets have distinct outputs;
Env App's no-emit type check overlaps asset bundling under the same checkout lock.
Third-party notice verification runs after all embedded-asset tasks succeed; it
reads installed package metadata and Env App's YAML parser, so it cannot overlap
cold dependency installation in a clean Runtime source copy.
Go compilation waits for every embedded asset. Publication and cache receipts
wait for all builds plus unchanged-source/input checks. Release builds retain
their ordered preparation.

Package dependency byte scans run in three workers alongside toolchain probes;
their digests and ordering match serial verification. Parallel build supervisors
label diagnostics, preserve failures and stop owned process groups (including
nested supervisors) on cancellation or sibling failure.

Saved local Gateways reuse intact compatible installations through the Gateway
service owner. Startup does not force replacement on Desktop source changes;
missing or damaged packages are prepared by that owner, and explicit Update
selects the current build. Verified package archives persist only within a cache
generation bound to the launcher's complete build input key, including dirty
source bytes. Different
inputs discard the previous generation; calls without an input key use a fresh
session cache. Archive verification remains owned by the package cache.

Development launches select gzip level 1 and Brotli quality 4 for embedded assets;
decompression yields the original bytes. Ordinary/release builds default to
maximum compression. The selected profile participates in build identity.
Gateway source copies exclude unrelated agent worktrees and native build caches.

Logs report dependency, input verification, Desktop, Runtime and Gateway timings,
Gateway preparation phases, and total preparation before opening the window.
A warm empty-profile launch is not an end-to-end latency claim for source changes
or saved Gateways. Qualify both rebuilt and unchanged launches with a local
Gateway, checking the current Runtime commit and owned-service cleanup.

Normal exit, startup failure, Ctrl+C and SIGTERM stop owned local services.
The launcher owns coordination; product shutdown semantics remain unchanged.

Shared Electron resolution returns only the path; installer logs use stderr.
Propagate failures and check executability after dependency-changing builds.

## Credentials
Unpackaged development instances use AES-256-GCM with a random profile key
(0600). Keep the key with the profile. It prevents plaintext disclosure, not
same-user process access. Other launches use Electron system storage; codec
construction never probes it.

Legacy Keychain records open a recovery screen without system access or preference
recovery. Only its explicit migration action decrypts and atomically migrates each
file. Failure preserves credentials and permits retry/quit; corrupt keys require
repair. Never reset accounts, Runtime state or Keychain entries.

## Bundle retention
Complete bundles publish under `<development-state-root>/desktop/bundles/<manifest-sha256>`.
Retain the newest three, selected bundle (including reuse), and all live references.
This bounds inactive verified package counts, not bytes; active or unverified
entries can increase usage.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Retention only touches generated packages in the selected profile. Builders own
in-progress directories.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Runtime state identity
Each Runtime state directory owns an immutable Ed25519 seed in `access-identity.key`. Invalid or symlinked existing material fails closed and is never replaced.

Existing TLS, Gateway trust and Runtime authentication remain authoritative.

## Observation and grouping
Main-process observations bind an entry ID to its configured connection and verified identity.

Runtime membership summaries use the Gateway pairing fingerprint: SHA-256 of the canonical, trimmed Ed25519 SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM, encoded as unpadded base64url with `SHA256:`.

Existing registrations, Gateway member and Cloud binding authority remain in their respective stores.

## Explicit default and one-time opening
The existing main Open button uses the saved default. Implicit defaults use stable registration / first-observation order, never probe completion order or a newly rebuilt Gateway catalog timestamp.

[Gateway access sessions](../gateway/gateway-access-sessions.md) owns transport isolation and same-route session reuse.

## Membership discovery and migration
Members are discovered from the signed v5 directory and matched to trusted Runtime membership summaries.

Existing Cloud-only Runtime configurations must rejoin and cannot silently gain the new member delegation. [Gateway Cloud access](../gateway/gateway-cloud-access.md) owns proof-based preservation of a formal environment ID.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
This contract owns display association and route selection. Proof observation never upgrades those permissions.

[Gateway Desktop interactions](../gateway/gateway-desktop-interactions.md) owns the explicit environment connection, invitation and confirmation steps and the independent management, invitation and local consent boundaries; recovery reuses the original Runtime lifecycle owner.

sections.body:
[Interaction continuity](desktop-interaction-continuity.md) owns authority, drafts, visibility and stale completions. Controls stay single-line.

## Window actions
All perspectives use **Open window** for unopened environments and **Show window** to focus an existing session. Labels preserve readiness, authority, lifecycle and session ownership.

Settings, progress, recovery and titles use Environment, environment window or Redeven. Env App is internal, never a label or brand. All shipped catalogs explicitly translate this copy.

## Alignment

## Execution
- Start reuses one verified healthy Runtime. Stop succeeds on empty inventory and verifies termination.

The current binary supplies temporary exact inventory and best-effort stop. Builds, downloads, archive preparation, upload and extraction belong to package progress, never process discovery. Desktop exit/update retires WSL Bridges without stopping WSL Runtime.

A completed probe preserves missing-control diagnostics even when it publishes no Presence. Unknown or unauthenticated status must not become an observed stopped Runtime. Missing diagnostics may guide recovery but never grant live management capability; only current Presence can do so.

Direct lifecycle actions remain available in every diagnosis. Failed nested recovery names the actual operation and retains structured diagnostics; raw stderr appears only in technical details.

[Verified access routes](desktop-environment-access.md) owns association/defaults. Gateway directory presence, membership and application probing are distinct; failure never changes routes or starts Runtime recovery.

[Runtime Flower access](../../desktop/src/shared/runtimeFlowerAccess.ts) checks actual protocol/epoch for commands, subscriptions, frames and attachments. concepts.title: Desktop SSH runtime operations
concepts.description: Direct SSH and SSH-container Runtime lifecycle execution owned by Desktop.

frontmatter.description: Direct SSH and SSH-container Runtime lifecycle execution owned by Desktop.
frontmatter.title: Desktop SSH runtime operations

concepts.summary: Desktop manages SSH-host and SSH-container Runtime only through the saved connection and placement. One process-local lifecycle coordinator, Launcher Operation, transport lease and temporary helper serve Start, Stop, Restart, Update, Refresh, Open recovery and Reinstall. Gateway/Provider credentials never substitute for SSH authority. The target stores no Desktop lifecycle lock or supervisor state.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Transport and authentication
Connection keys include normalized destination/port, authentication, SSH binary and credential scope. Failure retains SSH diagnostics without route substitution or command replay. macOS/Linux reuse ControlMaster; Windows uses native OpenSSH bounded commands and one persistent child per private Bridge, without WSL or ControlMaster. Cancellation/disposal terminate only owned children.

An omitted acquisition password reuses credentials already held privately by that exact transport scope; it is not a request to replace them with an empty password. Explicit credential changes still reject while leases exist, and other scopes never inherit those credentials. Without an available password, use OpenSSH batch authentication with configured keys or its agent even for a password-mode registration; never submit empty-password retries. Explicit management connection attempts allow this authentication; passive status inspection may defer it when no password is saved. Password availability is not management authority.

Start, Restart and Update share transient-password IPC handling. Their executor carries explicit credentials unchanged through restart access/certificate preflight, preparation and readiness verification without saving them. An absent saved password stays omitted so an authenticated transport remains reusable. Observation requests never accept transient passwords.

One normalized Connect Timeout covers connection, probe, inventory and startup-readiness control; startup/package transfer keep their own deadlines. Windows uses the packaged x64 askpass helper: accept password/passphrase prompts, refuse host-key prompts, emit secrets only through private stdout and retain OpenSSH host-key checks. Passwords never enter arguments, files or logs; missing helper fails visibly.

Discovery follows bounded SSH includes and excludes wildcard/negated aliases from selection, while explicit destinations remain allowed. Registrations separate display name from destination and save exact root and container engine/id.

## Preparation
One operation reuses its transport, probes platform once and prepares a lightweight helper only as needed for inventory/stop. Start/Stop never prepare a full package. Update independently verifies its package before modification; build/download/upload remain visible preparation phases. Clean-source builds use published dependencies and install Desktop dependencies before Env App assets; existing `node_modules` is not a prerequisite.

Archives allow 256 MiB compressed and 512 MiB for the complete expanded tar stream, including Runtime, Computer suite and signed plugins. Enforce expansion while decoding, before target modification, and reuse one parsed inventory.

Bulk upload uses bounded writes and a progress deadline; continuous progress may exceed command timeout, stalled writes terminate the owned command, and command completion timeout resumes after the last write. Pipe progress is not remote receipt. Cancellation/loss remains authoritative; administrator credential input never uses this deadline.

All upload/install/container/reinstall paths share private slot metadata: `runtime`, `runtime/managed`, `runtime/managed/bin` and both executables use `0700`; stamp/evidence use `0600`, independent of umask. Normalization failure preserves the live slot; ReDevPlugin owns final executable admission.

## Exact target execution
Host actions use the confirmed remote user/root; container actions inspect the saved exact container. Start/Restart/Update/Reinstall may start it; Stop never does and succeeds on empty Runtime inventory. Signal only verified scope matches and retain typed before/after state. Wipe reinstall treats helper inventory/stop as best effort when direct filesystem access can still isolate the root.

Remote snippets perform one bounded probe, stage, inventory, stop, install, start, verify, isolate or cleanup action. Desktop owns ordering, deadlines, cancellation, progress and retry; there is no remote lock, heartbeat or lifecycle machine.

## Progress and failures
Direct bootstrap uses the generated signed `https://github.com/floegence/redeven/releases/latest/download/redeven-install.sh` with the explicit selected tag; Portal is not another installer. Transfers stay within one Launcher Operation task: uploads count local pipe writes, acquisition counts response bytes with usable content length, and shared cached acquisitions share progress. Direct downloads consume complete installer `Downloading Redeven: N%` records. Installer diagnostics use stderr; stdout carries only the staged path. Companion output cannot reset Runtime progress.

No second download, progress-parser subprocess or SSH polling command is allowed. 100% transfer is not verified installation/readiness; preparation remains active through staged verification. Cancellation/failure freezes measured progress. Acquisition, staging-directory creation, upload and unpacking are preparation; only activation changes the live slot.

The operation exists before its first SSH command. Connection, engine/container, preparation, command and readiness failures remain distinct with technical stderr. Empty successful startup-report reads mean pending until the bounded deadline; nonzero reads mean command failure, valid blocked reports mean Runtime failure, and only nonempty malformed reports are invalid. All lifecycle paths share this interpretation.

sections.body: SSH registrations retain direct lifecycle menus. Gateway/Provider-only entries cannot borrow them. Never signal unrelated processes, substitute similar containers, delete home directories or prune containers globally. Multiple Desktop processes managing one target are unsupported and do not justify target-side coordination.

concepts.summary: Each Desktop placement bridge owns one HTTP/2 session, an immutable-generation recovery snapshot, and one exact registry identity. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Recovery presentation
Recovery uses an unboxed layout within the existing shell, with generous whitespace, semantic theme colors, standard buttons, and fine separators around the authoritative countdown or active phase.

A 30-second stalled-app timeout shows an actionable failure instead of an endless loading surface.

## Mechanism
Each established bridge owns one immutable transport-recovery snapshot with a monotonic `generation` and `revision`, the real `waiting`, `connecting`, `paused`, `ready`, or `failed` phase, completed attempt count, known retry and recovery timestamps, a structured failure, and explicitly allowed actions.

Lifecycle generation fencing cancels matching Opens so a late response cannot recreate the old session.

concepts.title: Desktop WSL runtime operations
concepts.description: Windows-only WSL 2 discovery, registration, Linux Runtime lifecycle, private Bridge, and packaging boundaries.

frontmatter.description: Windows-only WSL 2 discovery, registration, Linux Runtime lifecycle, private Bridge, and packaging boundaries.
frontmatter.title: Desktop WSL runtime operations

concepts.summary: Redeven Desktop for Windows 11 x64 runs only the Electron Desktop process. It provides no native Local Environment, Windows Runtime, or local-container Runtime. A user may register one or more initialized Linux x64 WSL 2 distributions as independent WSL Environments. Desktop manages only the Redeven Linux Runtime inside the exact registered distribution and user; Windows retains authority over WSL installation, distribution state, termination, and removal. Missing WSL, WSL 1, initialization failure, missing Linux commands, a vanished distribution, package damage, or Bridge termination fails visibly and requires an explicit retry or lifecycle action.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Discovery and registration
The main process publishes one immutable platform-capability snapshot. Renderer surfaces consume it and never infer the host operating system.

UI recovery copy may show Microsoft WSL commands for the user to run.

## Linux Runtime lifecycle
WSL and SSH host operations consume the same managed-Linux probe, uploaded install, atomic activation, startup report, inventory, exact stop, and verification scripts.

Runtime installs under the Linux user's home-backed `~/.redeven`, never under `/mnt`, and does not require `systemd`.

Only the Environment Stop action stops it.

## Private Bridge and failure behavior
`desktop-bridge` remains a foreground `wsl.exe` child carrying the shared `redeven-desktop-placement-h2/1` HTTP/2 session over private standard input and output.

Multiple registered distributions have independent target ids, processes, Bridges, update state, and lifecycle coordinator keys.

## Package and update boundary
The Windows Desktop bundle uses `managed_wsl_archive` and contains one verified `redeven_linux_amd64.tar.gz`; it must not contain or execute `redeven.exe`.

Public Windows assets remain forbidden until Authenticode signing, signed NSIS update metadata, signing receipts, and a real signed n-1 to n update are enabled together.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Windows and WSL 2 remain separate authorities. No boundary may be hidden by a native Windows Runtime, SSH-shaped WSL compatibility path, public port, localhost-forwarding dependency, system service, or second lifecycle state machine.

The first-party host-application bootstrap places its controls in one 40-pixel Desktop titlebar, alongside platform-owned traffic lights or caption buttons. Empty header space drags the window when no toolbar popover is open; buttons and popovers explicitly reject dragging.

The control is unavailable until its selected target has decoded pixels.

The bootstrap consumes published Floe `standalone.css`: primitive sizing and fonts, all 26 shell presets, shared floating material and input focus rules. Local CSS owns only viewer layout and maps control states to upstream semantic tokens; it must not maintain a second light/dark palette.

The inline assets add no request or connection wait.

## Backend commands
The shared toolbar and picture-preset presentation do not own backend state. macOS retains native menu, window-generation, frame credit and capture-quality semantics.

It never sends server shutdown or force-kills the application. macOS quit retains its existing application-wide confirmation. These distinct actions must not be collapsed into one destructive command.

concepts.summary: Desktop opens a joined Runtime over its existing outbound Flowersec connection to Gateway. Gateway forwards bytes to the Runtime's fixed application entry; it has no Runtime URL to dial. TLS terminates in Desktop and Runtime. Password, MFA, Host/Origin checks and application authorization remain Runtime-owned. Access artifacts limit initial redemption; no Gateway timer shortens established business sessions.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Reverse application streams
After local consent, Runtime redeems its invitation with its own identity and initiates a persistent Flowersec session to the member TLS endpoint. Gateway opens a reverse ByteStream on that Runtime's connection and relays both streams with bounded buffers and cancellation.

TLS, WebSocket, streaming responses and secure cookies retain their original semantics.

## Application and management separation
A reverse stream enters the original public Runtime handler. It never acquires a trusted Desktop management marker.

The catalog alone does not authorize service or Runtime process operations.

## Limits and revocation
The shared budget admits at most 32 business connections per member and 1,024 in total, including pending opens. One member exceeding a limit cannot consume another member's allocation.

Cloud closure receipts and partition limits are owned by [Gateway Cloud access](gateway-cloud-access.md).

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Gateway owns reverse-stream admission and bounded forwarding only. No path in this contract grants Gateway a Runtime lifecycle command, arbitrary egress, or a second direct-access transport.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Host administration
Local, SSH, local-container and SSH-container connections acquire management only after actually reaching the target Gateway and verifying its private host credential. It never exposes the credential to Renderer, URL connections, Runtime channels or logs.

Removing a Desktop connection does not stop or delete the Gateway service.

## URL enrollment and reconnection
Administrators create client access codes through POST `/gateway/v6/clients/access-codes` or `redeven-gateway clients access-code`. An identical completion retry returns the original result after response loss; other clients cannot consume that code.

A client access code neither enrolls a Runtime nor grants Gateway administration.

## Client visibility and revocation
Host administrators list clients through POST `/gateway/v6/clients/list` or `redeven-gateway clients list`. The display name is a recognition label, never identity evidence.

Revocation survives restart.

## State and compatibility
Trust schema 3 retains Gateway and client keys, preserves previously allowed environment access and removes legacy management grants. A handshake mismatch requests a Gateway/Desktop update, not identity replacement or state reinstallation.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Independent approval and membership
Joining a Gateway establishes local membership only. A directory cannot obtain Runtime credentials.

Namespace authorization, local egress permission and batch-enrollment delegation are separate decisions.

## Required network path
Runtime control registration, independent recovery, data transport and enabled official-platform requests use the explicitly selected route. Gateway outages and denied egress never trigger a direct Internet fallback or global proxy environment variables.

Ownership changes require separate authorization.

## One recovery owner
Registration, heartbeat and credential replenishment share one connection controller and independent credential source.

Unknown results resume that operation.

Each route operation can be queried after an unknown result; cancellation reports a committed operation truthfully.

## Management notifications and closure
Each Gateway has one authenticated HTTPS notification owner. Reconnection starts with an authoritative snapshot.

No short data lease is introduced during ordinary control outages.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Connection and enrollment

Creation offers Not now or After setup, add Gateway access before inspection/startup. Connection precedes verification and consent; prior Env App opening does not prove a live connection.

Creation and every Environment card open one app-owned enrollment session. Cards own no parallel enrollment dialog, recovery dispatch or authentication state. Settings suspends that same session, and closure restores the originating control.

Each dialog opening owns a sender/target-bound bridge lease across all steps. Env App closure cannot release it. Cancellation, renderer navigation/destruction or target authority changes release the lease and reject late requests; admitted writes retain transport until settlement.

Connection first acquires an independent lease on the exact Env App bridge, or attempts the saved management channel with available SSH transport/OpenSSH authentication. A passive `auth_required` diagnosis or absent saved password cannot require password entry before this attempt. Only a current authentication failure shows the inline, focused, Enter-submittable password field; it stops credential-free retries. Rejection stays distinct from Gateway/container-engine failure. Among enrollment commands, only scoped status accepts a temporary password; it overrides saved credentials for that connection without updating preferences. Verification/consent never carry it. Clear the renderer password after connection, failure or closure. Reopening creates a fresh scope and retries available authentication.

When authenticated inspection proves the Runtime or its container is stopped, show an explicit startup action. Start, restart and update use one lifecycle dispatch adapter and the existing lifecycle owner. They first try available authentication; only a typed SSH authentication failure requests a temporary password through the same state and input used for connection. Pass it unchanged through lifecycle execution and access verification, never persist it, and clear it after settlement. Successful recovery invalidates consent before reconnecting; a startup observation cannot interrupt its owning action or race password clearing. Opening or connecting never implicitly starts a Runtime.

Connection loss blocks submission and polling; explicit recovery retains drafts and uses the original lifecycle owner. Lost connection or changed authority requires fresh verification. Observations never cancel pending requests.

Saved-Gateway and manual-entry tabs preserve independent drafts and input nodes. Selection belongs to the enabled saved registration ID across URL, local/SSH host and container kinds, never to an address or observed connectivity. Retain records with no usable endpoints and show inline address setup. Prefer confirmed member_endpoints; a URL registration without catalog endpoints may use its canonical HTTPS origin. Never infer addresses from SSH or listener coordinates. Reject revoked/changed trust, invalid origins, Host-rejected addresses and loopback for remote targets without hiding otherwise eligible registrations. Late inventory cannot replace typed input or focus; removal of a selected usable address revokes verification.

For host-managed Gateways with manage_members permission, the enrollment owner saves a reachable address through update_gateway_endpoints, preserving existing endpoints, listeners and Host restrictions. The IPC response returns the authoritative endpoint list; retain that delivery only until the catalog changes, never resurrect removed endpoints. The user explicitly generates an invitation through invite_gateway_runtime or pastes an existing code. Saving, selection and invitation issuance never enroll a Runtime. URL/access-only connections explain how to obtain an address and code from the administrator. Changed authority, closure and suspension reject late responses; observations preserve pending actions. Runtime verification and explicit consent remain mandatory. Success consumes the code; reopening clears consent and code.

## Welcome task ownership

Preserve the existing Welcome toolbar, horizontal Environment / Redeven Cloud / Gateway navigation, search, filters, full-width cards and bottom status bar. A Gateway name or Manage opens a full page within this shell: Overview, Clients, Runtimes, Network, Redeven Cloud and Service maintenance. There is no separate Desktop connection section. All Gateways restores the list query, position and focus; reopening the selected Gateway retains drafts. Global Welcome navigation suspends the same page and task owners.

Cards expose parallel Connect client / Connect Runtime actions. The shared Floe Dropdown contains only local saved-connection actions: Edit connection, Enable/Disable connection, Remove from list. Connection editing uses a bounded Dialog. Removal confirmation explains local scope; it neither stops the service nor revokes remote clients. Clients and Cloud initialize independently on first visit. URL connections cannot inherit host administration from stale permissions. The source action owner remains mounted independently of filtering or card presentation; no hidden duplicate card owns maintenance.

Creation starts with an explicit existing-service or new-deployment intent. URL pairing and host/container preparation have separate transport choices. A successful save returns the exact saved registration ID and leads to its overview, with observed status and the next supported service action. Saving a connection never claims deployment or connectivity; starting remains explicit through the existing lifecycle executor.

Gateway-side Connect Runtime first distinguishes a Runtime managed by this Desktop from one managed by another administrator. The first choice and environment-side Add Gateway access enter one application-owned enrollment session, preselecting the corresponding object. The second choice opens the existing invitation issuer in a bounded task dialog; missing addresses link to the existing network editor, without creating a second issuer. The picker includes stopped and unopened managed environments. The old member-dialog nested enrollment is removed. Switching from the Runtime-choice dialog to enrollment waits for outgoing modal presence to finish; drafts and return context survive. Hiding enrollment retains its draft and any admitted submission. Reopen it through the existing Environment card Add Gateway access or Gateway Connect Runtime action; no global resume banner or extra Welcome content row is added. Resumption reacquires the management connection and revokes obsolete consent rather than reusing a released lease.

An accepted enrollment shows a result instead of immediately disappearing. Membership and live connectivity remain distinct. An uncertain submission queries the exact Gateway membership; it cannot submit the same invitation again. A positive status completes the result; an authoritative absence clears consumed/uncertain invitation material and returns to verification. Ordinary checks never consume invitations. Done returns to the initiating context.

## Management and presentation

Management uses a quiet Floe content plane, compact sidebar navigation and responsive wrapped navigation below 768 pixels. Only the active section contributes to the Welcome scroll extent; visited sections remain mounted to retain network drafts, codes and progress. Client enrollment, Runtime enrollment, connection editing and service confirmation use the published Dialog, without nested competing overlays. The page remains visible behind tasks. Keyboard dismissal and task transitions restore the initiating control. Ready empty cards show their count without an instructional banner. Semantic tokens, shared controls and explicit locale catalogs follow the published floe-webapp design language.

Readiness follows the observed service and verified Gateway protocol, not equality with the Desktop build. Refresh, pairing and invitation issuance reuse compatible installed Gateways. Package repair must never produce a start-required error. Pairing rejection cannot be reclassified as an update requirement from release or commit differences; [Gateway service](gateway-service.md) owns compatibility and package integrity.

The Runtimes group keeps membership, per-member Cloud overrides, recheck and removal; global Cloud policy belongs to Redeven Cloud. Client enrollment prepares an editable HTTPS address and requires explicit access-code issuance. Opening an entry never creates a code. The delivery exposes the code, expiry and address with separate or combined copying; returning to Clients retains its draft and code. Observational endpoint updates do not overwrite the address. Clients remains the sole owner of listing and confirmed revocation. Member, publication and endpoint choices share the published Dropdown. Refresh failure retains lists/invitations; cancellation cannot reopen dialogs or discard drafts. Settings/client-code import grant no Runtime permission or Namespace approval. [Network settings](gateway-network-settings.md) separates share endpoints, listeners and collapsed Host restrictions and owns validation/restart.

Internal enrollment checks use inline feedback, without status-refreshed toasts. Unknown status never implies rejected credentials; expandable technical details retain the actual diagnosis. Opening Environment settings suspends enrollment, releases its connection and invalidates verification while preserving invitation drafts and the current step. Returning requires a fresh connection before submission.

Use explicit translations and viewport-bounded panels. Saved Gateway and endpoint pickers use the published shared Dropdown with its field-surface marker, keyboard navigation and focus restoration. Focus changes the existing border color without adding an outer frame; native selects and parallel menu behavior do not belong to this enrollment flow. Settings and enrollment address inputs share an explicit HTTPS hostname-and-port example from every locale catalog. Listener and Host examples also belong to every explicit locale catalog. Invitation countdowns use locale plural rules. Member-operation failures show localized recovery text; raw error codes remain in collapsed technical details, including unknown future codes. Policy checks pair localized action names with their technical hook identifiers.

Service maintenance and card actions share the same foreground action owner, admission and progress renderer. A bounded service Dialog overlays the management page; closing it never reopens a card popover or dispatches again. Network restart review uses this same operation surface. Gateway service confirmation presents the action, target and affected sessions without a diagnostic inventory. Its close icon shares the title row. Admission replaces confirmation controls with a pending state until authoritative operation progress arrives; it cannot resubmit the same action.

Service progress prioritizes observed step labels, current-step state and elapsed time. It never invents future steps or a completion percentage. Raw service detail is optional, collapsed diagnostics after the timeline; failures retain their concise recovery summary and separate technical details. Confirmation and progress share a stable card trigger and explicit close control: closing hides the panel, restores trigger focus and leaves the operation running. Reopening retains its steps and timing without dispatching another request. After launcher reconnection, a running service operation takes precedence over a new confirmation: the card adopts that operation's owner and opens its existing progress.

concepts.summary: `redeven-gateway` owns one durable member directory, one-time invitation-code consumption, client access grants, policy and restricted forwarding. Runtime verifies the Gateway address and code, previews the signed enrollment descriptor, then explicitly confirms membership. Gateway never dials a Runtime address, scans a network, or installs, starts, stops, updates or resets a Runtime. LAN access works without Cloud. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Membership authority
An administrator verified through the Gateway host creates a ten-minute, single-use invitation code and shares an administrator-confirmed Gateway address. Gateway never obtains Runtime Cloud credentials from its directory.

Desktop display association uses the trusted Runtime management membership summary and the paired Gateway key; public health proof remains a separate observation and grants no authority.

## Policy and executable hooks
New installations deny Cloud by default.

Programs use an absolute executable and argument array, never a shell. Desktop member management and `redeven-gateway members reevaluate --member ID --version N` check the current member version before applying the same reevaluation.

## Own-process management
The separate Gateway archive and state root contain no Runtime lifecycle data. Saving, refresh, pairing or member management never starts a stopped service implicitly.

Cancellation still stops development startup and exact owned-process cleanup remains required.

## Compatibility and updates

Gateway release tags and source commits are diagnostics, not admission gates. Desktop validates the installed binary against its own installation stamp, then observes service readiness and the actual Gateway wire/authority contract. An unrelated Desktop or Runtime release never forces Gateway replacement. Start/restart reuse an intact installed package; explicit Update validates the staged archive against the selected release and commit before activation. Package corruption, stopped service, pairing failure and protocol incompatibility remain distinct diagnoses; authorization rejection never implies an outdated build.

Gateway v6 owns its authority epoch independently of Runtime Service. The existing value 69 is preserved so deployed services remain compatible; change it only for a reviewed Gateway authority break. Runtime metadata versions do not gate membership. Preserve signed identity, consent, permissions, freshness and current protocol validation; best-effort compatibility does not accept unknown security contracts. A feature failure affects that operation, not unrelated members or Runtime lifecycle authority.

## Address changes and upgrade
[Gateway network settings](gateway-network-settings.md) owns atomic network configuration, next-start listener changes, request Host admission and its persistent migration boundary.

If all fail, the membership stays intact and reports Gateway unavailable.

Optional Cloud publishing remains a separate flow.

The opt-in task qualification calls the selected installed Ollama model through
the production Flower service and published Floret runtime. The model chooses
real tool calls; assertions inspect actual files, terminal processes, canonical
views, and the workspace stream. A failed scenario remains a failure, with no
simulated replacement or automatic rerun. Tests own isolated state and stop only
their own services and tools. Source configuration and credentials stay unchanged.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Run `scripts/check_flower_tasks_ollama.sh` explicitly; `--interleavings` selects
combined operation cases. Every request uses the selected installed model, with
real chosen tools and exact Ollama Chat history. Observe actual effects and canonical
state; retain failure without simulation or automatic reruns.

| Scenario | Required observable result |
| --- | --- |
| Data/file task | Read structured data, compute sum, write/verify, modify in a later turn |
| Stop generation | Prompt acceptance, cancelled terminal state, no failure retry of cancellation, later task accepted |
| Stop terminal | Preserve confirmed initial effect, kill owned process, prevent delayed write, accept later task |
| Queue edits | Optimistic text match, stale edit rejection, reorder/delete and exact execution/user-text order |
| Send now | Cancel active provider request and execute selected queued task |
| Concurrent duplicate input | One retained task; conflicting content for same key rejected across stop/restart/promotion |
| Stop/restart at generation, approval or Ask User | Original stop identity, stale response rejection and exactly-once retained queue promotion |
| Queue edits during approval | Stop/restart before promotion; late approval cannot execute cancelled tool |
| Duplicate approvals | Same answer replays before/after restart, conflicting answer rejects, one actual effect |
| Cancel Ask User | Replacement input runs after restart; stale answer cannot revive task |
| Two interrupted continuations | Concurrent Retry/queued input retain original write exactly once |
| Duplicate send-now | Consumed items reject edits; restart replay does not reexecute |
| Permission/model change | Queued permission changes, active model-change rejection and immutable existing approval snapshot |
| Repeated permission transitions | Readonly/approval, stop/restart, stale/fresh approval, post-effect failure, downgrade/retry and restored full-access effects |

Tests own isolated state, services and tools. Remove temporary stores/files after
each case while retaining reports; source configuration and credentials stay unchanged.

frontmatter.title: Flower request-history CPU qualification

concepts.summary:
Published Floret v7.79.0 reads canonical request facts once per Engine execution
and advances bounded state only after successful writes. Retry/restart reload
facts; historical render-lineage validation remains intact. Redeven stops sidebar
preview work at the latest useful content and retains unchanged sequence groups,
members and observers during streaming. Three real-Service/Electron samples
reduce median backend CPU 80.3%, combined CPU 53.9% and allocations 87.0%, while
preserving complete output, responsive controls, selection and manual reading.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Floret owns canonical request preparation; Redeven consumes the published runtime
without sibling replacements or a second cache. No cadence reduction, dropped output,
history deletion or durable ledger is permitted. [Storage ownership](../ai/flower-storage-ownership-and-migrations.md)
and [streaming interaction](../ui/flower-streaming-stability.md) remain normative.

## Method and reproduction

Real Service/SQLite and production Electron use fake providers, 100 completed turns
(200 requests), 16,384-byte system prompt, mixed Markdown/Unicode/reasoning, tool
boundaries every 40 updates and 40 Hz output. Each fresh fixture warms ten seconds
and measures 120 seconds before exact canonical/rendered prose, reasoning and code
checks. Apple M5 Pro (18 cores/64 GiB), macOS arm64, Go 1.27.3, Node 26.7.0; CPU is
cumulative process time (100% = one core), combined includes all fixture Electron
processes, and allocations are cumulative bytes rather than retained heap.

The historical comparison retains its seed prompt scope. An ordinary fork creates
a new scope and cannot reproduce request-history amplification. Leave that override
unset for concurrency/lifecycle scenarios.

```sh
GOWORK=off go test -c ./internal/ai -o /tmp/flower-cpu-fixture.test
node scripts/qualify_flower_cpu.mjs --build --dist=<isolated-ui-directory>
REDEVEN_CPU_QUALIFICATION=1 REDEVEN_CPU_HISTORY_TURNS=100 \
REDEVEN_CPU_SYSTEM_PROMPT_BYTES=16384 REDEVEN_CPU_TOOL_EVERY=40 \
REDEVEN_CPU_RETAIN_SEED_SCOPE=1 REDEVEN_CPU_STATE=<fresh-empty-directory> \
REDEVEN_CPU_DIST=<isolated-ui-directory> \
/tmp/flower-cpu-fixture.test -test.run '^TestFlowerCPUQualification$' -test.timeout=45m
node scripts/qualify_flower_cpu.mjs --fixture=<state>/fixture.json \
  --seconds=120 --warmup=10 --threads=1 --hz=40 --stop-samples=3 --output=<sample>.json
```

Keep the fixture alive for connection, stop it via its quit operation and verify
owned cleanup. Retain raw samples/failures and binary/UI/source hashes locally;
match reference UI and qualifier revisions because thinking selectors changed in
`7d649a3b6`. Never touch the user's running Flower.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Reference `31e4966a4` uses Floret v7.78.2. Candidate published v7.79.0 also includes
upstream index removal (`2445833`), bounded sequences (`7d649a3b6`) and thread browsing
simplification (`233a46346/41341d417/8cb73c54e`). Product gains measure that combination;
only the Engine benchmark isolates request-history reads. Loopback NDJSON excludes
encrypted network overhead and real model latency. Relative/P95 acceptance does not
satisfy the separate absolute CPU or every-long-task-below-100-ms budgets.

frontmatter.title: Flower persistent-index startup acceptance

concepts.summary:
On the isolated 710,344,704-byte database with 219 threads, complete Redeven
construction plus activation reached a nearest-rank P95 of **9.429 seconds** over
20 sequential process runs. Published Floret v7.52.0 retained at most **261.052 MiB**
of GC-live heap; the entire product retained at most **295.018 MiB**. Both fixture
acceptance targets (P95 <=10 seconds and Floret idle heap <=350 MiB) passed.
These are dataset-specific measurements, not universal startup guarantees.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Method and provenance
The 2026-10-17 measurements used macOS 26.5.2 (25F84) on Apple M5 Pro, Go 1.27.2, and the checksummed published `github.com/floegence/floret@v7.52.0`; no sibling wiring, workspace override or live product store was used. Timings include full canonical and prompt validation and finish before the first query.

Sampled peak heap is a separate metric and must never be reported as idle memory.

## Results
| Scenario | Processes | Median | P95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Migration plus index | 10 | 35.206 s | 39.500 s |
| First index on current canonical data | 10 | 33.956 s | 37.241 s |
| Ordinary Floret reopen | 10 | 6.407 s | 7.582 s |
| Changed binary, unchanged schema | 10 | 6.088 s | 6.425 s |
| Complete product preparation and activation | 20 | 7.852 s | 9.429 s |

Canonical validation still creates substantial temporary allocation; that peak remains a known cost even though idle-memory and ordinary-startup targets pass.

| Operation | Median | P95 | Maximum |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Thread creation | 0.389 ms | 1.004 ms | 3.278 ms |
| Title update | 0.198 ms | 0.285 ms | 0.287 ms |
| Queued-input append | 0.294 ms | 1.019 ms | 33.021 ms |

## Retained timing samples
Durations below are seconds in execution order.

| Sample | Migration | First index | Reopen | Binary upgrade |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 35.595 | 35.624 | 6.857 | 6.205 |
| 2 | 35.124 | 32.561 | 6.814 | 6.260 |
| 3 | 35.396 | 35.387 | 6.145 | 6.043 |
| 4 | 34.905 | 35.027 | 6.211 | 6.153 |
| 5 | 31.666 | 32.692 | 6.289 | 6.002 |
| 6 | 31.692 | 37.241 | 6.142 | 6.040 |
| 7 | 35.742 | 34.094 | 6.124 | 6.002 |

| 9 | 34.870 | 31.350 | 6.525 | 6.132 |
| 10 | 35.287 | 33.818 | 7.582 | 6.039 |

## Validation and delivery
Floret ran its complete Go suite, focused query/persistence/migration/startup race checks, v7.16.2 API compatibility, candidate adoption and actual published module adoption. v7.52.0 contains cbad47d (transactional indexes), acad18a (completed-work progress), and 5be01b8 (cancelled SQLite rollback ownership).

See [readiness ownership](../architecture/ai-readiness-lifecycle.md), [startup interaction](../architecture/flower-startup-presentation.md), and [snapshot recovery](../ai/flower-backup-and-recovery.md).

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Use the same machine, published dependencies, synthetic data and build mode.
Point-read scaling requires ≥70% short-target P95 reduction; warm synchronous P95
is <8 ms and visible feedback precedes commit. Keep raw source identities/results
locally; never commit user databases/credentials or continue real tasks.

Root detail uses Floret window subscriptions. GET/PATCH and root observation share
public projection; send acknowledgments carry exact identities without a current
view. Child reads own an independent bounded interest.
Initial windows and explicit body requests bound transport, excluding metadata and
pending controls. Cold send admission reads bounded current facts but still scans
historical metadata; complete execution preparation follows admission. Explicitly
expanded activities use selected values and bounded field ranges. Backend read and loopback/render timings are
separate measurements, never additive.

```sh
GOWORK=off go test ./internal/ai -count=1 -timeout=15m
GOWORK=off go test ./internal/ai -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkFlowerThreadDetailPointRead -benchtime=1x -count=1 -timeout=10m
python3 scripts/check_flower_storage_compatibility.py
```

Run focused `TestFlowerHistory`, ThreadCache/runtime record tests, history/streaming/
tool-sequence browser suites, both host typechecks and locale validation. Synthetic
and released-writer qualification stays outside ordinary CI/hooks. Private baseline
frames must validate before shared-frame assertions; do not discard arbitrary frames.

Deep-scroll qualification must cross the product HTTP decoder.
`TestServerFlowerHistoryScrollQualification` serves only an owned isolated copy with
execution deferred. `qualify_flower_thread_open.mjs --history-scroll-steps=80` checks
both directions, canonical progress, successful membership requests above 8 KiB,
and idle request stability after each ten gestures. The service-only fixture cannot
qualify HTTP request-size limits. Never commit its raw history or database.

sections.body:
These local sequential diagnostics identify specific costs, not population latency
or smooth-frame guarantees. Cold point reads exclude remote rendering. Retain baseline
failures and report their scope; passing focused suites cannot recertify other known
failing fixtures. Canonical history remains complete.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Source And Published Dependencies
The live capture checks below used Runtime source `5b4e303718adcb5e1b7e244dd306ab8043d2ad9d`, `GOWORK=off`, and no sibling module or package overlays.

The user excluded Redeven push and full integration gates from this local delivery.

## Transport And Authority
Actual Chromium direct checks cover public HTTPS, public HTTP and private numeric-loopback acquisition.

A 4,194,321-byte payload matches byte for byte; a payload larger than 32 MiB closes its stream and never reaches the upstream.

The prepared Xpra 20/21 classes are covered upstream; this phase did not launch a retained Xpra host application on a physical host.

## Linux Live Behavior And Queue Recovery
`server` uses an isolated Runtime and state directory, reached through an owned LAN SSH forward.

Bounded blocking delivery now waits for the consumer and exits on attachment shutdown. The queue was not enlarged and the failure evidence is retained.

## Connection Launcher Refinement
The launcher now names the actual Desktop connection or reported local hostname, keeps optional view/grant-reuse settings collapsed, omits a single-display selector, and separates status checking from connecting.

This verifies the launcher and locked-host boundary; the unlocked macOS limits above still apply.

## macOS Boundary And Outstanding Work
The Apple Silicon helper reports authorized screen and input access but a locked host.

Prior desktop acceptance results are not substituted for this transport build.

Go proxy and checksum database readback verified the release.

The opt-in `TestInstalledClientInputViewer` uses a task-owned state directory, private display, port and application.

The real macOS disposable application fixture passed pixels, click, Unicode, shortcut, menu, reconnect, stale input, resize, window replacement and close checks.

The current records do not qualify physical system-pointer appearance in shipped Electron, Chrome, Safari or Firefox, page zoom 80/100/125/150/200 percent, or monitor changes.

These limitations do not alter the earlier real IME/soft-keyboard acceptance assigned to the user in the [input validation record](host-application-validation.md).

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Release identity and evidence layers
The retained qualification below consumed published `github.com/floegence/floe-native-apps` v0.21.0 at `a7f3b76a2a9dd64ba13b303c24d7bed645b33441`, with module checksum `h1:E1Wgl8aRB/h53ejCCDkUwlrj3uC2zx+SGcAODZZ5nWg=`.

| Architecture | Combined component digest |
| --- | --- |
| amd64 | `f8f29cf383166c4e7c6728b6c1f696ab015391875dc2a370f283d4d4ca457a90` |
| arm64 | `93a0210e630a54d176f9b8f6ff3fc21605a348d6f97c7c5c8127fa6cd7a484be` |

## Package, desktop and graphics coverage
| Case | Evidence and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Strict Snap Firefox | Real user-systemd scope, private graphics/bus, native confirmed text and saved document in upstream qualification; Redeven browser adds click-to-type, repeat, field selection, copy/paste and toolbar receipts |
| Flatpak GTK/Qt | GNOME Text Editor and KWrite use real sandboxes, package metadata, remote official file dialogs and document grants upstream; Redeven verifies native first frame, repeated Unicode, selection replacement, text/Enter order and actual Ctrl+S bytes |
| Native DEB/RPM | Native GTK/Qt/browser and GNOME Text Editor receipts; retained Fedora 44 RPM Firefox 156.0.1 and Text Editor 50.1 evidence keeps SELinux Enforcing and original signed packages |
| AppImage/classic Snap | Retained original mounted Notepad Next v0.15 and classic Snap Emacs 31.1 input/save/reconnect/exit evidence; Redeven additionally verifies mounted AppImage click-to-type, Unicode, replacement and exact Ctrl+S bytes; no extraction or sandbox bypass |
| Desktop coexistence | Actual GNOME Xorg/Wayland, KDE Wayland and Xfce X11 shells in disposable native KVM qualification, with unrelated applications retained; these virtual-display tests do not certify physical GPUs |
| No full desktop | Native application preparation and private software rendering without a monitor or complete desktop; sandbox package requirements remain separate |
| Wayland/Xwayland | Pure GTK/Qt/Chromium Wayland and mixed native window families, menus, oversized dialogs, generation-bound input and reconnect; retained Xpra remains an explicit distinct backend |

## Product acceptance
The retained v0.21.0 qualification repeats production-viewer native input on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit and actual Chrome/Firefox stream acceptance on udesk26. The [performance guide](host-application-performance.md) owns picture modes, bandwidth, latency, bounded decode work and explicit claim limits.

Test harnesses consume current session state rather than fabricating perpetual `running` status.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Released capabilities
The current integration consumes Floe Native Apps v0.22.19 and Floe webapp core 0.86.0 with `GOWORK=off`.

The native Linux adapter maps physical keys to the published seat, uses confirmed text when the client layout cannot be represented by that keymap, and sends clipboard publication before paste through the upstream scheduler. It must not paste the old selection, replay text or release composition when scrolling ends.

## Actual application receipts
On a task-owned Linux installation, set `REDEVEN_TEST_DESKTOP_COMPONENT_STATE` to the released combined component root.

The application must report the received string before further checks.

Minimal test images may lack CJK/emoji fonts: exact string receipts remain valid input evidence, but missing glyphs are not visual font acceptance.

## Lifecycle and retained resources
`TestInstalledDesktopApplicationTransport` verifies real pointer/text/key input, exact saved bytes, invalid clipboard rejection and cancellation of dependent input, then recreates the Runtime manager and saves again through the same helper.

Unknown records fail read-only. Elapsed time alone cannot end a live application awaiting its first window; the installed timeout regression observes the old 40-second boundary without ending sharing or the process.

The native Mac helper remains the platform authority. Shared canvas extraction requires macOS viewer/input, first-frame, toolbar, reconnect and stale-target regression tests as well as actual fixture input.

Browser composition and touch event injection prove transport and application behavior only.

frontmatter.title: Host application lifecycle acceptance

concepts.summary:
This matrix records observable lifecycle acceptance for Host Applications. The
[shared authorization contract](../architecture/host-applications.md) and
[macOS window lifecycle owner](../architecture/macos-application-window-lifecycle.md) remain normative.
A live process, an available window, a decoded frame and an authenticated viewer
are separate facts. Only explicit closure evidence ends the physical viewer.
A missing or inaccessible surface must preserve the app and provide an accurate
recovery path; it must never silently select an unrelated process or inject stale
input. This matrix is not a certification of every installed application.

See the [cross-platform behavior contract](../architecture/host-application-behavior.md)
for aligned operations and unavoidable OS differences.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
| Scenario | Required result and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Existing single-instance Mac app | Reuse exact process; lease release preserves it (native fixture) |
| First window after 40 seconds | Keep waiting, then reveal without relaunch (48-second fixture and Go watchdog) |
| Multiple windows | Counted picker with literal titles, retained selection/focus and direct switching (viewer/browser tests) |
| Close cancelled | Retain process/session and viewer (native cancellation fixture) |
| Unreadable/replaced surface | Uncertainty never expires into closure (Swift inventory/presence tests) |
| Linux dialog-only app | Reveal decoded dialog at native dimensions (Xpra adapter) |
| Final window actually closes | Close established physical viewer (native/viewer tests) |
| Last lease released | End sharing, retain newly launched app and all windows (multi-window fixture) |
| One stale quit selection | Reject whole selection before termination (native quit fixture) |
| App cancels quit | Keep process, pixels and sharing; permit another explicit request (cancellation/reconnect fixture) |
| Unknown quit result | Keep confirmation error; never infer exit or auto-retry (Env App test) |
| Read-only caller | May list running apps, never quit/detach (API/UI tests) |
| Network loss/reload | Keep app; suspend capture/input, reclaim buffers, reconnect same session/current credential (WebSocket/native/viewer tests) |
| Second viewer | Revoke previous input, release held keys, suspend old capture before successor resumes (WebSocket/native tests) |
| Permission loss/console lock | Invalidate capture/input and expose distinct recovery (Swift/viewer tests) |
| Helper exit | Sharing failure is not app exit; reclaim route, credential, buffers and helper before terminal state (Go/viewer tests) |
| Late callback/unknown terminal reason | Ignore stale results; retain terminal page without automatic physical closure (macOS/Xpra viewer tests) |
| Unproven foreground/window ownership | Nonblocking input failure, no replay into another app (native/viewer tests) |
| Missing video decoder | Negotiate same-process image transport (picture/viewer acceptance) |

Toolbar checks cover content resize below its fixed bar, bounded popovers at
320/390/1000 px, native-menu keyboard access, distinct window close/confirmed quit,
late menu dismissal and no replay of unconfirmed quit. Native quit tests cover
catalog/session controls, visible/windowless apps, cancellation and stale generations.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Screen-recording and accessibility are explicit macOS grants. Save-dialog cancellation
never permits forced exit. [Distribution evidence](host-application-validation.md)
names tested targets; [platform behavior](../architecture/host-application-behavior.md)
owns OS differences.

concepts.summary:
The [display contract](../architecture/host-application-display.md) owns picture
behavior. Floe Native Apps owns capture, encoding and region decoding; Redeven owns

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Reproducible measurements
Compare baseline and candidate on the same host, browser version, source size and workload.

An SSH tunnel changes transport overhead and must be recorded.

| Metric | Definition and controlled viewer acceptance budget |
| --- | --- |
| Input to presented pixels | DOM key event through remote application to changed canvas pixels on the next animation frame; nearest-rank P95 of 20 samples below 150 ms in every mode |
| Input during motion | The same 20-sample measurement while document scroll continues; P95 below 250 ms, including Save data cadence |
| Presented FPS | At most one changed-canvas presentation per animation frame; Motion first at least 25 FPS during document scroll |
| Received payload | All incoming WebSocket data bytes, including JSON; excludes WebSocket/TLS/SSH framing and network retransmissions |
| Idle bandwidth | Below 0.25 Mb/s after settling; a fully unchanged document should send zero image bytes |
| Document-motion bandwidth | Below 5 Mb/s for Automatic/Clarity/Save data and 15 Mb/s for Motion first at the recorded source size |
| Decode work | No more than two current-target frames plus one retired decode; no reconnect on a picture change |
| First frame | Navigation to first decoded canvas presentation; excludes browser-process launch before the viewer attaches |

A sandboxed Chrome 153 client on Ubuntu passed all v0.21.0 viewer budgets over loopback, isolating capture, forwarding, decoding and presentation from networking:

| Chrome | 2.14 | 27.0 | 46–65 ms | 129–237 ms |
| Firefox | 4.37 | 37.4 | 65–81 ms | 99–231 ms |

## Retained Xpra distribution validation
The historical Xpra matrix below covers userspace installations without a desktop environment or monitor. Container checks cannot certify a distribution's boot, kernel, SELinux/AppArmor, GPU, or login policies.

| Environment | Installed stack | Evidence scope |

| Ubuntu 22.04, orange host | Xpra 6.5.3, HTML5 v20 | Native host application acceptance, browser/Desktop window controls, input and reconnect |
| Debian 13 | Upstream Xpra 6.5.3 packages with explicit `xpra-x11`, HTML5 v21 | GIO checks; X11 launch/resume/stop; browser display, input, reconnect and application-exit closure |
| Fedora 43 | Distribution Xpra 6.5.3, separately installed HTML5 v20 | Same installed-stack and GIO checks |
| openSUSE Tumbleweed | Distribution Xpra 6.5.3, separately installed HTML5 v20 | Same installed-stack and GIO checks |
| Alpine 3.23 ARM64 | Distribution Xpra 6.2.2, upstream HTML5 v20, static GNU Redeven Runtime | GIO; launch/resume/stop; complete Runtime and native terminal; browser display, input, reconnect and application-exit closure |
| Arch Linux x86_64 | Distribution Xpra 6.4.4, upstream HTML5 v20 | GIO and isolated X11 launch/resume/stop in the prepared userspace; complete Runtime and browser flow under the translation constraints below |

## macOS validation
The native adapter was exercised on macOS 26.5.2 ARM64 in a logged-in graphical session with capture and accessibility permission. The disposable AppKit fixture verifies real bundle metadata/icons, direct launch, captured pixels, pointer input, Unicode text, native shortcuts, actual menu invocation, real AX resize, reconnect without a new process, stale input rejection, and application-window closure.

This covers the idle-helper replayd contention that single-application startup tests cannot detect; the [capture ownership contract](../architecture/macos-application-capture-owner.md) defines the required process and channel boundaries.

## Implementation And Distribution
Upstream commit `ec0d9cc8e64fd3e9e2020da017bec57a56ce0f94` replaces full-frame Python allocation and copying with a bounded Gst buffer pool.

These results certify the tested host-desktop component, not the whole optional application distribution.

## Correctness
Thirty-six focused Python tests pass, including existing damage, sequence, mapping and cursor rules.

- BGRA, BGRx, RGBA and RGBx; packed, padded and non-aligned source rows. - Separate cursor updates and embedded composition without corrupting retained clean pixels. - Bounded pool capacity, final-frame recovery, parent lease retention and interruptible shutdown. - Retained frame bytes after pool deactivation and idempotent capture close.

These checks retain the cursor, mode, reconnect and permission contracts; neither a debug workspace nor sibling source overlay is used.

## Performance Of The Final Implementation
The same udesk24 VM ran alternating old/new/old/new tests at 2560 by 1440 with software x264. The real private PipeWire producer emits a moving rectangle through MemFd at 60 FPS and never reads the user desktop.

| New B2 | 59.90 | 2.64 ms | 8.68 / 9.99 ms |

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Deployment And Host Identity
On 2026-10-11 the task Desktop used card **Actions → Update** for udesk26, then the real Env App administrator-authorized service deployment.

Cleanup removes task fixtures, channels and local processes while retaining installed host Runtimes and services.

## Real Functional Evidence
| Interaction | Observed host or Viewer outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Picture | Physical GNOME panel and Clash Verge, then the fullscreen task GTK fixture, appear in the real Viewer. |
| Mouse | A real Viewer click increments the fixture's visible button counter and host event log. |
| Keyboard | Physical `a` press/release reaches GTK; twenty later presses add exactly twenty `a` characters to the host document. |
| Unicode and Enter | In **Use local input method**, CUA sets the real keyboard textarea once to submit an input event; GTK and Viewer show exact `abC中文😀$`, then physical Enter and `second` produce `abC中文😀$\nsecond`. This is assisted commit, not human IME composition acceptance. |
| Lock | Viewer **Lock host** locks GNOME; ordinary controls, clipboard and the editable keyboard surface become disabled. A later observation shows actual lock pixels; the initial black interval has no measured duration or established cause. |
| Physical unlock | **Start unlocking** and physical Enter expose the GNOME password box. One wrong submission keeps the host locked; the authorized correct physical password restores the desktop and `LockedHint=no`. A subsequent click and `x` change the fixture, proving restored input. |
| Shortcut | The first Alt+Tab submission lacked host-effect evidence. A later real shortcut switches from the GTK fixture to Clash Verge and back. Only the latter observations qualify window switching. |
| Fullscreen | The real Viewer enters Electron fullscreen; Escape restores native window controls while retaining the remote picture. |
| Explicit disconnect | Picture is removed, input and shortcut controls are disabled, and **Desktop disconnected** instructs the user to close and reconnect. Closing and reopening from Env App previously restored the picture. |

### Missing-text diagnosis

No feedback percentile or production defect owner was established.

A bounded layered check of configured orange (`192.168.31.134:22`) finds route en0, the expected ARP MAC, three ICMP replies at 153.169 / 767.083 / 47.908 ms, and an OpenSSH banner after a 160 ms TCP connection.

Orange's native AFBC and lock/input evidence is preserved.

concepts.summary:
The controlled physical-seat and X11 comparisons qualify their tested local
configurations. The v0.22.29 physical-seat candidate reduced host-local input
receipt latency and CPU use; the v0.22.10 X11 candidate reduced client-window
response latency with working NVIDIA encoding and one local host-shaped cursor.

Session authority remains owned by the
[desktop contract](../architecture/remote-desktop.md). These measurements establish
the tested configuration, not physical input-to-photon latency, universal GPU
performance, zero-copy capture or WAN behavior. Capture/encoder failures still
revoke media authority and require fresh current-generation paint.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Physical-seat measurements
The v0.22.29 physical-seat candidate was measured on the task-owned `udesk26` DRM output (i915, DP-3, 1920x1280) and `orange` (1920x1080). These are host-local Unix/DRM observations, not physical input-to-photon measurements or Desktop SSH/browser end-to-end latency.

## Configuration and measurement
The physical server uses Ubuntu X11, i7-14700KF, RTX 4090 D, NVIDIA 550.90.07 and 1920x1080 at 60 Hz.

The earlier NoMachine comparison is context only and must not be presented as this candidate's same-path benchmark.

There is no optical sensor or high-speed-camera evidence.

## Observed results
Values are milliseconds, median / nearest-rank P95.

| Endpoint | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Light click to client window | 67.5 / 84.8 | 56.0 / 71.7 |
| Scrolling click to client window | 69.9 / 88.3 | 57.8 / 75.2 |
| Light source timecode to client window | 60.4 / 73.4 | 49.9 / 68.8 |
| Scrolling source timecode to client window | 60.1 / 78.7 | 54.5 / 71.6 |
| Light receive to decoded | 1.0 / 1.4 | 1.0 / 1.3 |
| Light decoded to completed canvas draw | 7.9 / 15.3 | 4.8 / 8.3 |
| Scrolling decoded to completed canvas draw | 5.4 / 14.9 | 4.5 / 8.5 |

The server GPU encodes; the local Mac decodes.

## Failure and recovery evidence
The initial NVENC prototype omitted explicit SPS bitstream restrictions.

Unit/browser coverage rejects invalid cursor metadata and prevents cursor shape messages from granting painted-frame authority.

X11 readback, scaling, raw IPC and GPU upload remain CPU-visible. Adaptive bitrate, cancellable refinement transport and a new real-time carrier require separate measured justification. macOS and Wayland retain their embedded-cursor contracts; this result qualifies X11 local shapes.

## Current Product Deployment
The task Desktop uses state `/tmp/redeven-orange-viewer-desktop` and a bundle built from Redeven `bb6683b5ce18`, consuming published native `v0.22.37` with `GOWORK=off`. Only bounded task fixtures receive qualification input.

The [SSH deployment owner](../architecture/remote-desktop-ssh-deployment.md) defines update and admission; deployment identity differs from recipe identity.

## Release And Regression Evidence
Redeven `b7d994aff911` fixes Node 26 linked-entrypoint identity after Desktop exit 71 exposed skipped release verification; all 31 affected checks pass.

Redeven setup nevertheless fails before installation because the Go module omits nested MPP assets; the old service remains usable.

Test tabs and the isolated HTTP server close afterward.

## Real Viewer Acceptance
Explicit local paste previously depended on host clipboard synchronization, which DRM does not advertise. The product adapter now uses existing bounded client text, fences delayed reads after mode/authority changes and reports denied clipboard access.

Credentials never enter evidence, command arguments, environment or diagnostics.

## RustDesk Comparison Status
The [physical desktop comparison](remote-desktop-rustdesk-comparison-results.md) owns its method, measurements and unresolved acceptance boundaries. Orange results remain evidence for Orange only; no hardware-wide parity claim is supported.

## Diagnosis and changes
Released `text_input` separates local composition from clipboard synchronization.

The earlier results do not qualify that new setup; no permanent display policy was changed.

## Native input comparison
Each of three rounds uses 100 pointer moves at 1920 maximum dimension, 15 FPS and original pixels. udesk26 is amd64/1920x1280; orange is arm64/1920x1080.

| Host and version | Input receipt | Matching DRM feedback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| udesk26 v0.22.32 | 3.699 / 4.194 / 3.696 | 17.659 / 17.692 / 18.118 |
| udesk26 v0.22.33 | 7.655 / 7.191 / 10.015 | 16.946 / 17.094 / 17.039 |
| orange v0.22.32 | 5.060 / 6.750 / 5.678 | 5.498 / 6.523 / 6.035 |
| orange v0.22.33 | 11.566 / 12.063 / 14.842 | 8.907 / 7.869 / 11.809 |

## Physical-host qualification
Both hosts previously passed native attachment, current-frame admission, retired-generation rejection, teardown, ASCII/Chinese/emoji text and Enter.

Subsequent source inspection and real pixels proved that canonical AB24 import succeeds with a bounded component-order normalization.

Explicit OS authorization retains its user-driven lifecycle.

## Client and idle CPU observations
Real CUA drags with one controlling udesk26 Viewer produced cursor-feedback P95 44.0 / 41.2 / 47.6 ms, with only 6 / 8 / 6 matched observations. Input-result timing is excluded because the Runtime assigns native command IDs independently; naïve client-ID correlation is not authoritative.

No same-configuration baseline was captured in that round, so this does not establish a 70% reduction.

## Idle desktop response
At 60 FPS/original pixels, a GTK fixture toggles black/white on Space.

| Host and version | Round 1 | Round 2 | Round 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| udesk26 v0.22.32 | 86.283 / 193.823 | 76.856 / 192.253 | 73.528 / 98.269 |
| udesk26 v0.22.33 | 73.765 / 94.790 | 62.772 / 84.435 | 50.607 / 89.433 |
| orange v0.22.32 | 241.530 / 267.476 | 255.642 / 282.653 | 246.081 / 257.422 |
| orange v0.22.33 | 96.195 / 265.283 | 100.704 / 274.402 | 103.856 / 224.087 |

## Lock input and regression boundaries
Released `physical-only` mode fixes orange's earlier lock-screen IME leak. Chromium/WebKit/Firefox upstream tests cover IME, empty codes, stale composition and release without weakening ordinary text input. udesk26 verified physical unlock. Orange's subsequent native invalid/valid unlock and successor-generation round is recorded in the AFBC qualification; its complete Desktop SSH Viewer acceptance remains a separate requirement.

## Published Dependency And Conditions
Both product binaries use clean source `6caee6df1da1eabdd5d9f4670d6eedcb578de1a3` and published `floe-native-apps` v0.22.6 (`dec4e3f48dba9445704b08cf2ff78c683c0c679a`).

Its glibc CUDA library cannot load into the isolated musl stack, which selects x264.

This is alternative scanout, not native 1440p60.

## Current Product Results
### macOS v0.22.6

| Capture | Minimum FPS | Maximum interval P95 | Maximum refinement | Bandwidth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1920x1080 | 57.582 | 23ms | 329.5ms | 14.71-14.82Mbps |
| 2560x1440 | 57.657 | 24.7ms | 351.1ms | 26.21-26.33Mbps |

Doubling acquisition from about 115 to 224 reads/s improved changed/encoded FPS only from 56.0 to 56.5; that higher-cost change was not adopted.

It had at most one pending handoff and zero at completion.

## Release And Lifecycle Evidence
v0.22.6 source CI, CodeQL, both native architectures, private applications, host-desktop media and Swift checks passed.

Authenticated Xvfb checks passed pixels, resource lifetime, protocol isolation, cursor, input and recovery. macOS uses a bounded latest-sample mailbox to separate comparison from encoding; callback wait P95 fell from about 8.6ms to 0.02ms.

Final focused desktop/appserver race tests were repeated against the published dependency and passed.

Earlier Mac results retain 38.323 FPS, 33.3ms interval P95 and 82.2ms input P95 failures, plus `KEYFRAME_REQUIRED` despite verified foreground.

Neither host is qualified for remote unlock.

The implementation and subsequent records were fast-forwarded into local `main` through `2945183a90e46f382410fa7ae23d4b35d8b63998`, preserving existing unpublished commits.

Its performance is outside this delivery's acceptance scope by explicit user instruction; no 55 FPS Wayland claim is made. - Any broader release claim requires its own host qualification; source integration alone is not release acceptance.

concepts.summary:
This guide defines acceptance for the [desktop contract](../architecture/remote-desktop.md).
Use published dependencies with `GOWORK=off`, preserve failed measurements and
resolve unmet thresholds for the agreed performance hosts before declaring
remote-desktop acceptance. Source integration does not substitute for this
qualification. A connected picture, native input
admission or a synthetic fixture does not certify real desktop performance.
The [acceptance record](remote-desktop-results.md) owns measured results and
remaining qualification.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Performance
At both 1920x1080 and 2560x1440, measure scrolling and task-owned window motion for at least 60 seconds, three times each, on a documented low-latency connection.

Refinement must finish within 500ms and match a lossless text reference at the same dimensions after host motion stops. 4K does not substitute for either required resolution.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
## Real-Host Qualification
For this delivery, the user explicitly designated `udesk24` as a functional-only GNOME Wayland environment on 2026-10-02 after its graphics limitations were measured.

Before each physical-input sample, wait for current paint authority and focus; record recovery transitions and never replay a key whose delivery is unknown.

Credentials and raw captures remain outside the repository and audit payloads.

## Focused Verification
Run affected `GOWORK=off go test -race` checks for `internal/remotedesktop`, `internal/codeapp/appserver`, `internal/hostapps`, `internal/config` and Local UI access lifetime, plus Swift `HostApplicationHostTests`.

These contract checks cannot replace real-host or performance evidence. This proves generation-scoped playback delivery, not acoustic output.
