sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Reproduction And Repair
The ordinary Desktop connection to `udesk24`, using its normal saved portal grant, progressed from authorization to active generation 1, then immediately suspended with `CAPTURE_LAYOUT_UNSUPPORTED` in generation 2.

The native repair maps only a readable MemFd with validated file size, aligned mapping offset and bounded pixel range. The old published component remains identifiable and is never modified in place.

## Verification
### Regression And Installed Libraries

Nineteen focused Python checks cover metadata, damage continuity, padded pixels, non-page-aligned MemFd offsets, read-only access, mapping reuse/removal, changed buffer identity, invalid/truncated backing files and idempotent stream cleanup.

The complete release gate remains failed, so these results do not certify the full release qualification matrix.

designated this host for functional validation only on 2026-10-02; its graphics
performance does not block delivery. It still fails the
[performance contract](remote-desktop-validation.md): current 1080p/1440p
scrolling reaches 27.46/23.46 FPS despite authorized virtual graphics provisioning.
Preserve the failures; X11 or synthetic results cannot replace Wayland evidence.
The [overall record](remote-desktop-results.md) owns delivery and the other hosts.

sections.body:
## Verified Deployment And Desktop
The earlier accepted v0.22.6 build used clean source `6caee6df1da1` and native Floeterm. An initial older-v0.22.2 deployment failed before text input and was replaced only in the task Runtime; retain that failure with its original version.

No independent virtual desktop was substituted.

## Product Interaction
The task uses an isolated Runtime on port 24864, private state and an authenticated SSH forward.

This qualifies physical playback for that Linux-to-Mac path; destination-clock progress alone is not acoustic proof or a calibrated latency measurement.

## Desktop Launcher Admission Regression
On 2026-10-03, the real Desktop launcher exposed a product contract bug: desktop session `target_url` included `/_redeven_desktop/`, while Desktop window admission requires the registered loopback origin.

The fix returns the port-forward service's canonical origin, retains Desktop's strict validation, preserves IPC rejection diagnostics and removes misleading host-confirmation guidance after a failed launch.

The already-running user Runtime and Desktop were not restarted or replaced.

## Performance And Diagnostics
Each reported product scroll cell ran at least 60 seconds. The first cell failed the unchanged FPS threshold, so the matrix stopped and retained its failure; three passing repetitions and window-motion qualification were not obtained.

| Captured size | Actual painted FPS | Interval P95 | Refinement | Bandwidth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1920x1080 | 36.539 | 31.6ms | 234.4ms | 3.257Mbps |
| 1920x1440 | 39.647 | 33.5ms | 253.9ms | 3.611Mbps |

An unconstrained direct-caps diagnostic first failed with `target not found` and zero frames; the constrained diagnostic and failure are retained separately.

## Authorized Virtual Graphics Comparison
The user explicitly approved provisioning the hypervisor's GL/EGL/Mesa userspace dependencies and normally shutting down and starting only VM 106.

| Capture | Painted FPS | Interval P95 | Refinement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1920x1080 | 26.430 | 51.4ms | 387.5ms |
| 2560x1440 | 22.139 | 58.7ms | 334.9ms |

Raw 1080p capture without conversion or encoding was 32.26 FPS with the console open and 32.91 FPS after the user closed noVNC.

Direct DMA_DRM and linear BGRx DMA-BUF diagnostics failed format negotiation and produced no frames; no production fallback was added.

## Published v0.22.7 Follow-up
Clean Redeven source `69cd04988970c8b456f751838523e61625531d3c` uses the official v0.22.7 module and Linux component digest `09bfc6f9061997c43166ff7810092bf5e79ffaac0112d14a0a0711808e1709bc`.

Preserve the failure; the passing retry alone does not establish its cause.

| Capture | Painted FPS | Interval P95 | Refinement |

| 2560x1440 | 23.458 | 57.1ms | 335.1ms |

frontmatter.title: CI and release gates

concepts.summary:
Redeven runs focused development checks, a fast staged pre-commit gate and one
bounded integration gate for the exact main tip being pushed. Published
dependencies, generated assets, localization, compatibility and OKF must agree.
Full browser, Desktop, Docker, performance and native qualification run explicitly;
release packaging additionally requires same-commit historical conversation
evidence and authenticated target-specific artifacts. Windows remains an internal
certification target and cannot enter the formal release inventory.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Validation and exact-tip ownership

[AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) owns Git discipline and concise working rules; domain
contracts belong in OKF. `quick_ci_policy.test.mjs` enforces its 100-line limit,
index entrypoint and linked contracts.

| Level | Required scope |
| --- | --- |
| Development | Focused checks for changed behavior, source contracts and conflict resolution |
| Pre-commit | Staged diff, README localization, open-source hygiene and affected notices/viewer assets |
| Ordinary push/PR | One bounded source-only Actions job |
| Main pre-push | Clean, exact rebased base/tip; source, dependency, release, runtime and hygiene groups in `check_final_integration.sh` |
| Explicit qualification | Browser/UI, real Electron, Docker, native, stress and performance suites appropriate to the change |
| Release | Published artifact gates and successful historical conversation workflow evidence for the exact release commit |

Pre-push requires the checked-out local main tip to equal the pushed tip, verifies
fast-forward ancestry against the remote handshake and rejects unpublished merge
commits. Earlier or pre-rebase evidence cannot certify another tip. Local gate
fingerprints cover executables and inputs, excluding `MANPATH` because macOS hook
shells can change it without changing execution. Real-hook tests guard evidence
reuse. Generators must leave the tree unchanged; Go formatting reports all offending
tracked paths before expensive stages.

Staged notices use a temporary Git-index snapshot, including partial staging,
installed metadata and the exact cached staged Go toolchain with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`.
Proxy, SumDB and VCS downloads are disabled. Missing prerequisites or stale output
stop commit; cleanup cannot rewrite the index or working files. Viewer assets verify
staged sources and locked installed dependencies without installation or generation.
Their sole generator is `internal/envapp/ui_src/scripts/buildHostApplicationAppearance.mjs`.

Daily/manual CodeQL is separate from push/PR. Unchanged main since the latest
successful scheduled analysis skips the language matrix; lookup failure scans.
Resolve findings against current source and every maintained lockfile. Dismissal
requires specific authorization/input-boundary evidence; unavailable scanning is
not clean. External Actions, including certificate import, use reviewed commit pins.
Their supported Node 24 runtime is independent of the product toolchain.

## Toolchains and generated assets

`go.mod` owns the exact Go patch; Actions use `go-version-file` and local gates
select the same version. `.node-version` owns first-party Node; helpers and package
engines reject other majors. Public README prerequisites and badges match these
sources. Desktop pnpm permits lifecycle scripts only for `electron` and `esbuild`,
ignoring `electron-winstaller` because internal Windows packaging uses NSIS.
Dependency changes regenerate and check `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

README translations preserve canonical structure, links, code literals, protected
terms and synchronization hashes in `assets/readme/locales.json`. Reviewer identity
or approval counts are not synchronization metadata. OKF matches active contracts;
its bundle, manifest and checksum are generated and committed together. Build embedded
UI assets before Go tests importing their embed packages.

Env App `pnpm build` owns a checkout-local `flock` across cleanup, TypeScript, Vite,
budget checks and compression. The inherited descriptor releases when build processes
exit. Same-checkout builds wait; worktrees remain independent. `build_assets.sh`
cannot compress after lock release or silently skip missing assets.

Shipped Runtime uses cgo plus `floeterm_native`, native Linux/Darwin amd64/arm64
runners and published terminal-go. Untagged live attachment fails closed. Source
contracts cover release, Desktop, SSH and carrier commands, including macOS Bash 3.2
strict-mode arguments. Main runs build contracts; full native execution is qualification.

## Qualification and security boundaries

`flower-history-qualification.yml` opens copied immutable released-writer databases,
explicitly continues through the product and repeats after restart. Release-ref
requires successful same-commit Actions evidence. Ordinary CI and main run source-only
fixture verification, not this full qualification. The [historical upgrade contract](../ai/flower-upgrade-compatibility.md)
owns preservation, failure and restore requirements.

Explicit UI/renderer gates use canonical headless browser/carrier runners and fresh
exact-source assets. Ignored prior `dist` output and headed diagnostics cannot establish
that evidence. [Upstream web dependencies](../architecture/env-app-upstream-web-dependencies.md)
own browser modes. Renderer-only Floe tests use client Vitest/browser resolution and
a DOM; mocks retain real utilities unless testing that boundary. Headless fixtures
retain scrollbars and explicit space-consuming geometry, and await focus restoration
after unmount paint. PDF drag fixtures remove only runner preview scaling and restore
it after interaction, preserving the product canvas projection.

[Desktop qualification lifecycle](../desktop/desktop-test-lifecycle.md) owns processes
and cleanup. Preload tests verify temporary working and separate utility/session
user-data paths inside Electron. Cleanup targets only the spawned POSIX group or
addressable Windows tree and waits for drain; external SIGKILL remains failure.
Preflight resolves and executes the exact pinned npm Electron binary inside Desktop
`node_modules`. Signal/AMFI rejection is an environment failure; tests never sign
Electron, change host trust or mutate dependencies to bypass it.

Manual Windows WSL certification requires exact `origin/main`, a matching Linux amd64
Runtime and two isolated WSL 2 distributions. It covers install, Start, private Bridge,
external shutdown, explicit Retry, Update and exact Stop before an unsigned internal
NSIS build. Only workflow cleanup may unregister its temporary distributions.

Security-sensitive inspection, hashing and consumption use one no-follow descriptor
for signed native manifests, Runtime log tails, source identity, installer pins,
Sparkle keys and qualification credentials. Source capture also matches the enumerated
inode; replacement tests guard these boundaries. Computer qualification proxies accept
only the fixed Responses POST route. Terminal carrier TLS exceptions require that
run's isolated device CA authentication. AI diagnostics are bounded single-line text.
Explicit report paths, synthetic credentials and POSIX-quoted SSH fixture data grant
no product file/network authority. Secret scanning excludes downloaded SwiftPM/npm
caches while retaining product native sources and other build output.

## Release handoff

[ReDevPlugin artifact gates](redevplugin-release-gates.md) own publication, native
evidence and closed inventories; [plugin integration](plugin-integration-gates.md)
owns Host, market and renderer behavior. Each artifact-consuming runner installs
pinned Cosign itself. Desktop jobs enable Corepack and install frozen Env App packages
to stage Playwright/QuickJS helpers, without installing browsers or running browser
qualification. Bundle exit traps capture the exact staging path and preserve original
failure status under Bash 3.2 and Linux Bash.

Protected `redeven-release` supplies signing, notarization, Sparkle and Team ID secrets.
Desktop exposes only a credential-free HTTPS feed and public updater key. Native macOS
verification binds App, framework, bridge and DMG to architecture, Team ID, hardened
runtime and notarization. The final DMG must receive Apple's Accepted result and be
stapled/validated before receipts or feeds. The App's stapled ticket and native
`syspolicy_check distribution` must pass.

Stable releases sign two non-delta Sparkle appcasts and release notes, verify their
signatures and remove temporary keys. Prereleases omit stable feeds; the collector
rejects them. Linux publishes architecture-matching `latest-linux.yml`. Installers,
feeds and notes join aggregate checksums and remote readback before publication.
[Self-contained installation](self-contained-installer.md) owns bootstrap pins,
suite activation and separate guarded default-version promotion.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Published source and trust

Consume the coordinated ReDevPlugin release pinned in the product manifest
(currently `v3.0.36`). The boundary guard rejects sibling wiring, Go workspaces/
replacements, npm links, copied runtimes/contracts, Rust path overrides and duplicate
platform-core trees. Scans exclude generated dependencies/output and fail closed on
scanner errors. The product commits neither plugin packages nor a separate catalog
manifest: a validated latest-only market snapshot selects immutable transport, which
ReDevPlugin retrieves and verifies. Market metadata is not trust.

Upstream GitHub Release must contain exactly one `platform-release-manifest.json`.
Bind tag, source commit, release workflow and attestation, then independently verify
Go module/go.mod h1 via proxy and SumDB; both npm integrities/provenance SHA-512;
runtime/worker SDK crates.io checksums and Cargo VCS identity; and manifest version,
closed coordinate order and contract-set hash. Extra assets, partial publication,
mutable/local identity or any registry mismatch fail before construction.

Manifest transfer requires HTTPS including redirects and certificate verification.
It permits an initial attempt plus three network retries, including handshake errors,
with 15-second connect, 60-second transfer and 120-second retry-start limits. The final
transfer may finish afterward. Exhaustion cleans partial files and stops before Rust
preparation with release-specific diagnostics. Validation errors never retry.
`--manifest-file` applies the same checks offline from the transfer step. The Node
contract CLI must validate and emit requested evidence from canonical or symlinked
checkout paths; exit success without work is not evidence.

## Native construction and admission

Build every Linux/Darwin amd64/arm64 target from the exact published runtime crate,
packaged lockfile and Rust 1.88.0. Metadata cannot resolve another first-party path
dependency. Rust preparation verifies local toolchain/target first; warm caches do
not contact servers. Missing components retry only classified transient network
failures (three attempts by default, at most five); checksum, signature and manifest
failures stop. `REDEVEN_RUSTUP_OFFLINE=1` is cache-only Rustup preparation, not an
override for manifest/Cargo acquisition. Honor standard Cargo/Rustup/proxy settings,
disable probe auto-install, retain TLS, recheck successful installs and return the
exact Cargo path. Download timeout is 120 seconds; default waits are 2/4 seconds,
capped at 60. Cancellation ends retries and cleans diagnostics.

Linux must be static PIE without ELF interpreter or dynamic dependencies; Darwin
must be target-exact 64-bit Mach-O built natively. Sign Darwin release bytes with
Developer ID, hardened runtime and timestamp before computing evidence; development
uses ad hoc signing. Emit binary, SPDX SBOM, resolved-package provenance, notices
and signature/certificate. Release Sigstore identity binds the exact Redeven tag
workflow; fresh ephemeral local Ed25519 profiles fail `--require-release`. Cosign 3
explicitly retains detached format with `--new-bundle-format=false` and
`--use-signing-config=false`; verification keeps workflow, OIDC and transparency checks.

The deterministic `redeven.redevplugin_runtime_build.v1` marker binds upstream
publication, all product files, target, toolchain, Redeven source, workflow and signer.
Consumption rechecks descriptors, binary target, evidence profile and signature.
Host startup trusts this marker's expected digest, never a digest computed from the
field binary as its own trust anchor. Runtime archives contain exactly Redeven,
ReDevPlugin runtime, six evidence files, license and product notices.

## Desktop packages and collector

Before replacing `.bundle/<target>`, validate archive name, closed flat inventory,
Go target and native policy. Gateway is separate and cannot enter Desktop. Packages
include complete evidence beside Redeven. The macOS signing exclusion is a regex
anchored to the independently signed runtime executable; its bytes/evidence cannot
change. Redeven, Computer helper, Sparkle and bridge remain signable. Copy the whole
Computer resource tree after Electron assembly, preserving nested packages/licenses.
Run startup validation before signing and again after refreshing only signer-visited
Runtime/Computer descriptors immediately before the enclosing resource seal.

Native builders inspect final DEB/RPM/read-only DMG bytes and emit v2 receipts binding
the runtime and six evidence files to installer bytes. Upload only installers,
receipts and `latest-linux*.yml`; diagnostics/unrelated macOS YAML are excluded. macOS
inspection uses system text and Apple tools without requiring ripgrep; complete
pipeline output is consumed under `pipefail`. Team ID, signature, hardened runtime,
updater key, stapling and distribution policy remain mandatory. Sparkle `lipo` passes
the final binary before `-verify_arch`. Separate relink gates validate Linux source/
object archives; consumption must not mistake them for runtime archives. Compatibility
tests derive epoch/window expectations from the current reviewed contract. Normalize
Linux feeds to exact published installer names before signing the inventory.

DEB admits POSIX ustar/GNU regular files and directories, bounded GNU long names and
metadata-only root. RPM disables optional build-id symlink indexes. Bounded no-follow
snapshots reject noncanonical/duplicate paths, links/devices, privileged modes,
sparse/PAX metadata, malformed trailers, trailing data and oversized payloads.

The collector accepts exactly four package and four Desktop artifact directories:
four Redeven and four Gateway archives, two DEBs, two RPMs, two DMGs, six target-bound
receipts and identical shared metadata. Each source is opened once no-follow, hashed
and copied through that descriptor, checked for inode/metadata changes, fsynced and
linked without replacement. Failure removes partial output.

Windows `managed_wsl_archive` admits one verified Linux amd64 archive bound to version,
commit, size and digest and rejects `redeven.exe`. It is internal certification only.
The formal collector rejects every Windows artifact directory until signing and
signed-update certification exists; Windows is not an optional fifth target.

The final job requires release-only consumption, signed checksums and
`safe_extract_tar.py`, then compares the complete draft asset names, sizes and hashes
before publication. [The installer contract](self-contained-installer.md) owns
verify-before-execute, complete immutable suite activation and retention.

concepts.summary:
Release packaging builds `redeven-installer_<os>_<arch>` for macOS and Linux,
AMD64 and ARM64, with CGO disabled. It renders `redeven-install.sh` from the
actual four binary digests and signs both the binaries and entry through

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Trust and failure boundaries

The original HTTPS script is the initial trust boundary. A reviewed fixed
installer digest authenticates the executable before it runs. The executable
uses the upstream Cosign Blob API, authenticated TUF roots, certificate
transparency and Rekor evidence to verify the exact repository workflow, OIDC
issuer and requested tag. It accepts detached `.sig` plus PEM or base64 PEM;
it does not guess a bundle format, accept mutable trust overrides, disable
verification, or fabricate upstream verification markers.

TUF requests preserve cancellation, use bounded HTTP timeouts and do not write
the user's trust cache. Log responses are bounded before SDK parsing and admit
only the detached X.509 `hashedrekord/0.0.1` contract. Other log types, including
legacy OpenPGP-capable formats, fail before the general upstream parser.
The bytes passed to the SDK are unchanged; the SDK owns cryptographic checks.
Signature or digest failure never executes the downloaded Runtime.

Public installation discovers GitHub's latest release unless an exact Runtime
version is supplied. The explicit managed channel selects the public version
manifest and GitHub-first artifact sources; it does not affect the public
default. The existing Runtime self-upgrade environment contract is retained.
Automatic resolution cannot downgrade a known installed version. Explicit
versions can request a rollback.

## Installation transaction

A no-follow, nonblocking lock serializes an activation root. Product-selected
regular archive members are closed and bounded; links, duplicates, traversal,
unexpected files, missing components, invalid trailers and changed bytes fail.
Published artifact-cache code owns acquisition and digest-checked storage.

Complete suites live in `.redeven-runtime-suites/<archive-sha256>`. Staging,
file synchronization, inventory/digest/version readback and pinned ripgrep
preparation precede the atomic `redeven` symlink switch. Ripgrep 15.2.0 uses
musl archives on both Linux targets; every new or reused authenticated executable
must run and report the exact required version before its link or Runtime is
activated. A missing loader, execution failure, wrong version, oversized output
or deadline failure leaves the previous Runtime activation unchanged. Activation detects
concurrent changes, retains every published suite, and restores and
checks the prior entry when post-switch verification fails. Errors distinguish
an unchanged activation from a committed but unconfirmed change.

Unselected suites and legacy flat-layout resource files are not automatically
removed: a still-running older Runtime can need its original resources after
one or multiple newer installations. The installer
does not own process lifetime and cannot prove those suites unused. Disk usage
therefore grows with distinct installed archives; removal requires a separate
explicit decision after confirming no process or rollback still needs them.

Fresh installs use a writable per-user directory without implicit sudo.
PATH updates use idempotent managed bash, zsh or fish blocks; the current shell
still needs the printed command. Unknown shells receive a direct executable
path. Upgrade mode does not edit shell profiles, start services or restart
Runtime; Runtime owns maintenance and re-exec after installer success.

## Publication and entry selection

From `v0.13.13`, the authenticated `redeven-installer-contract.json` declares
the minimum installer, closed targets and Runtime archive contract. Older
installers must stop before acquiring a new incompatible payload.

One bootstrap template is rendered from the four actual installer build
hashes. Release signing covers both `redeven-install.sh` (GitHub channel) and
`redeven-install-portal.sh` (Portal channel with the official mirror fallback).
There is no separately maintained shell installation implementation.

Release publication is separate from default-version promotion: assets are
published with `--latest=false`. Before promotion, `check-distribution`
authenticates the candidate inventory and contract, verifies each bootstrap's
whole-file digest, own release tag, channel and four installer pins. This
immutable candidate check does not depend on the current default pointer.
After promotion, `--check-active-entry` additionally reads back the public
entry: GitHub must match the authenticated candidate bytes; Portal authenticates
the active bootstrap against its own signed release and checks the candidate
Runtime's minimum installer version, allowing an older recommended Runtime.
GitHub's default
pointer is read back separately.

Runtime README commands select the generated GitHub release bootstrap. Portal's
Console and Install Worker redirect to the generated Portal bootstrap, using
one Portal-owned channel contract. That redirect is routing, not signature
verification. Bootstrap hashes are derived only from real release builds; no
placeholder pins or absent assets may be publicly activated. Public deployment
is an explicit operation, not a side effect of delivering source changes.
Rollback selects another compatible immutable signed release; it never restores
an obsolete external-tool installer or a duplicated rollback shell source.
Installation, historical upgrade, native execution and page integration are
independent feature/release acceptance, not additional ordinary push gates.

sections.body:
Verification is online; transparency or trust-service outages fail closed.
The bootstrap cannot defend against compromise of its original HTTPS script.
Cross-compilation alone does not certify execution on every target OS.

The dependency audit fixes the reviewed gRPC findings by selecting released
`v1.83.1`. The general SDK still imports the deprecated OpenPGP implementation
reported by `GO-2026-5932`; symbol scanning can continue to report it. The
installer rejects those input formats before SDK parsing. Do not describe a
nonzero scanner result as a clean audit, add a blanket suppression, or remove
this boundary without reviewing the upstream replacement and genuine fixtures.

The template repository owns recommendation discovery and immutable catalog releases.
Redeven's daily and manually dispatched watcher owns adoption of the published Go

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Upstream publication
The template repository's configured release sources select the official npm `latest` dist-tag and reviewed canonical OCI tags. The catalog is published with a new immutable module tag after isolated generation, Registry preflight, generated-contract verification, SDK acquisition tests, and all upstream Go tests, including the complete frozen historical-format fixtures.

## Published dependency adoption
Redeven queries only `github.com/floegence/redeven-service-templates` through `https://proxy.golang.org` and `sum.golang.org`. The chosen module and go.mod hashes must match the exact go.sum entries.

Maintained knowledge describes stable boundaries and does not need a prose rewrite for each version number.

## Main integration and recovery
Immediately before integration the watcher fetches remote main and compares it with the recorded base.

A failed gate can leave a candidate on the ephemeral runner's local main, but it is never published. Each run removes only its own temporary worktree and private branch.

The [Managed Service release contract](../architecture/managed-service-release-discovery.md) owns installed release identity and user-selected upgrades; catalog adoption does not rebuild, restart, or upgrade installed instances.

frontmatter.title: Local UI certificates

concepts.summary: Runtime owns the saved HTTPS identity and validates it before serving. Desktop exposes explicit certificate creation, import, regeneration, and removal only through the registered management channel. Certificate validity, client trust, and the latest operation result are independent. No operation silently replaces an identity or installs trust. Invalid imports preserve the saved pair; changes affect the next HTTPS start while the running identity and sessions remain intact. HTTP remains the default and requires no certificate.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Identity and trust
The user explicitly creates a device CA with `local-authority device-ca generate` and inspects it with `status`. Runtime startup never generates, replaces, or repairs certificate material.

Public export contains certificate material only, never the key.

## Explicit certificate changes
`import`, `regenerate`, and `remove` require `--confirm`. Reject malformed or extraneous PEM blocks, trailing text, encrypted/mismatched keys, invalid dates, invalid chains, missing SANs, and certificates unsuitable for server authentication.

This supports process-interruption recovery; it does not promise an OS trust rollback or filesystem power-loss durability.

## Coverage during network changes
[Local UI network exposure](local-ui-network-exposure.md) owns the two-second interface refresh and atomic public snapshot.

A signing failure retains only current addresses covered by the previous valid leaf and reports `certificate_refresh_failed`; retries recover automatically. Startup and explicit saved-identity preflight retain their strict validation boundary.

## Desktop interaction and private input
The compact HTTPS panel presents certificate validity, expiry, and system trust separately. Public path, fingerprint, and bounded selectable diagnostics live in the expandable details section.

Saving next-start HTTPS settings remains possible with an unusable certificate, with an explicit startup warning.

sections.body: Runtime owns saved identity validation and replacement; Desktop owns explicit management presentation and private file acquisition. Certificate operations cannot silently restart Runtime, install system-wide trust, or expose private material to the renderer.

frontmatter.description: Local UI separates network scope, password authentication, explicit HTTP or HTTPS, and private Desktop access.
frontmatter.title: Local UI network exposure

concepts.summary: Runtime owns a public client endpoint independently of the Desktop that starts it. New environments explicitly use HTTP on `localhost:23998`; HTTP needs no certificate. Network exposure retains local browser access and adds reachable network addresses; it requires a fixed port and an effective environment password. HTTPS is an independent explicit choice, with strict certificate validation and client trust. Pages and Flowersec WS/WSS share one public port. A TLS failure never downgrades to HTTP, and the authenticated private Desktop bridge never becomes a public fallback.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## HTTPS certificate ownership
[Local UI certificates](local-ui-certificates.md) owns creation, import, replacement, removal, validation, and client trust. It never creates or repairs certificate material, installs trust, or falls back to HTTP. Certificate replacement affects the next start; the running TLS identity and sessions remain intact.

## Listener and origin boundary
The public listener accepts only canonical authorities derived from its actual bound addresses.

Its isolated `flowersec-private-loopback/1` profile is unchanged and cannot authorize public clients.

## Native Desktop default-port recovery
Only native Desktop launches with saved default `localhost:23998` and no explicit one-start bind override opt in through `--local-ui-default-port-fallback`. Other errors, custom ports, numeric loopback overrides, network binds, and wildcard binds never silently select another port.

External bookmarks containing the old fixed port cannot follow the temporary address.

## Network changes and current reports
While network exposure is enabled, Runtime enumerates eligible interfaces every two seconds. Its public list is explicit, including `[]`; private bridge endpoints cannot supply missing public addresses.

Address failures affect public availability and never assert that the Runtime process has stopped or expose private management URLs.

## Admission and lifecycle
A network listener starts only for a concrete non-loopback IP or wildcard with a fixed nonzero port and an effective password.

Occupied explicit ports fail with a startup error instead of silently selecting another port.

Flowersec owns admission, session establishment, liveness, handler dispatch, close, and lease release; Redeven does not copy those loops.

## Server-owned access configuration
[Runtime two-factor authentication](runtime-two-factor-authentication.md) owns the persistent credential authority, one-time bcrypt verifier migration, TOTP enrollment, recovery, replay protection, and ordinary-session revocation. Explicit password changes remain next-start settings when MFA is disabled; MFA-enabled settings cannot clear/replace that password or downgrade HTTPS.

Failed catalog saves roll back verifier initialization as well as replacement and clearing.

sections.body: Installing trust in each HTTPS client is an explicit user action outside Runtime startup. Browser capabilities requiring a secure context remain unavailable with feature-specific guidance; browser security is never disabled. The private Desktop profile still requires exact preload provenance and numeric loopback, independently of explicit public HTTP support.

The local permission policy is a three-bit read/write/execute cap.

frontmatter.title: Plugin platform integration security

concepts.summary:
Redeven supplies authenticated host facts and source policy to ReDevPlugin; it
does not accept plugin ownership, authority, provenance, or trust from browser
payloads. Every HTTP route passes explicit authentication, origin, CSRF, and
closed-action authorization, and direct Host calls pass the same owner/action/
resource policy. External package source, signature, execution approval, update
eligibility, and permission are independent facts. Integrity failures, invalid
runtime identity, and capability scope mismatches fail closed.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Local process boundary
The `process.local` permission is an explicit high-risk grant and method-level Process Broker access is checked again for every Worker invocation. The Host does not inherit the complete Redeven environment and never injects session cookies, plugin tokens, or Host credentials.

See [Plugin process sessions](../architecture/plugin-process-sessions.md) for the lifecycle contract.

## Authenticated session boundary
The session resolver accepts only a Redeven channel id whose stored metadata has exact non-empty channel, user, and environment identities.

The bounded session cache is keyed by owner-session hash and accepts a hit only when all four hashes match.

Guessed owner sweeps and local teardown registries are prohibited.

## HTTP and direct authorization
The canonical route is `/_redevplugin/api/plugins`.

Method effect is resolved before local policy clamps it, while shared runtime management remains admin-only.

## Permission management projection
Plugin Center reads active grants and explicit plugin security policies through released ReDevPlugin APIs. It never writes registry tables, invents a default grant for a catalog plugin, or treats catalog identity as permission.

Its actual trust badge remains unchanged; only verified catalog trust may receive the `Official` trust badge.

## Package admission and trust
The retained release install/update path accepts only the exact source policy, revocation evidence, publisher, plugin, version, signed release metadata, package hashes, and Host requirement. Browser-supplied trust state, arbitrary package bytes, rollback, unknown publishers, invalid or revoked signatures, and invented fetch provenance are denied.

Redeven does not add a new authorization workflow; the existing official release-ref verification remains unchanged.

## Capability confirmation plans
ReDevPlugin validates a capability preflight result against the Host-known capability response schema before it becomes a confirmation plan. Values in the reserved `redevplugin.capability.risk_plan.*` namespace must match the strict v1 risk-plan contract; an unknown or malformed reserved version fails closed instead of falling back to a generic object.

Replacing or replaying any of those values requires a new confirmation.

## Runtime trust
Runtime descriptors bind version, target, IPC, WASM ABI, and artifact hash. Darwin release bytes receive their Developer ID signature before the product digest and Sigstore evidence, and later Desktop signing must preserve that exact nested executable. Startup must not hash the field binary and accept that value as its own trust anchor.

## Business adapter and observability boundary
Plugin business adapters are invoked only after ReDevPlugin resolves lifecycle, permission, confirmation, lease, quota, revocation, and audit context. Product code cannot bypass that chain.

Raw adapter errors, tokens, secrets, cookies, query strings, absolute paths, and complete URLs are not copied into public or durable diagnostic detail.

Desktop runtime-control tokens, direct-session artifacts, Gateway credentials, RCPP credentials, and Flower grants are not plugin ambient authority.

Redeven security adapters may narrow authority; they may not mint platform tokens, weaken route policy, edit opaque state, or replace released brokers.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Session authority and lifetime
The gate alone decides channel authorization when registering the channel and its lifetime cancellation callback under one lock. Callers supply verified private-management identity or an ordinary login session ID, never an `unlocked` assertion.

Runtime restart clears in-memory sessions and incomplete operations; it preserves committed authentication state.

## Browser Cookie scope and continuity
Local UI alone issues, reads and clears `redeven_local_access_<http|https>_<port>`. Forwarded headers cannot select the scope.

Only an incorrect password or factor produces input validation feedback; transport failures and cooldowns retain their own messages.

## Desktop consumption and forwarding
Desktop Flower retains the complete Runtime-issued access-cookie `name=value` pair and returns it unchanged. It never derives the name from a bridge or forwarded client port.

No upstream platform capability changes are required for this product authentication policy.

frontmatter.title: Runtime two-factor authentication

concepts.summary: Runtime `accessgate` owns environment authentication independently of Redeven Cloud. Enabling two-factor authentication requires the environment password followed by a TOTP or single-use recovery code for ordinary browser, direct URL, and Cloud data sessions. A password-only challenge grants no file, terminal, editor, plugin, or forwarding access. Authenticated native/SSH management retains its separate private host authority; loopback addresses, Cloud administrator claims, and forwarded headers do not establish that authority. Missing or damaged committed authentication state fails closed. Host recovery locks ordinary access until a new password and authenticator are committed.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Enrollment and management
Desktop Environment Settings / Access presents one two-factor row. If a different environment password has been saved for the next start, restart before configuring MFA; the old running verifier cannot overwrite the newer saved authority.

These commands do not alter SSH keys, sshd policy, PAM, host passwords, or execution identity.

## Session authority
[Runtime access sessions](runtime-access-sessions.md) owns ordinary session deadlines, browser Cookie scope and refresh continuity, challenge binding, native editor delegation, and revocation. MFA management changes revoke ordinary authority through that single gate; they do not create a second browser or Desktop authentication lifecycle.

## Persistence, replay and recovery
`access-auth.sqlite` is a versioned, private SQLite authority, separate from the transport authorization database. The committed database and initialized key become the sole authority; deletion, malformed data, unsafe modes, symlinks, unknown schema, or key loss cannot fall back to the retired verifier.

Authentication state and secrets are not diagnostic export inputs.

## Dynamic Activity pages
Only plugin instance, plugin, and surface identifiers are persisted. Execution plans, admission credentials, temporary URLs, and management revisions are resolved through the current plugin opening flow and never saved in navigation.

Loading and cache authority follow [Env App resource snapshots](env-resource-cache.md).

concepts.summary:
Redeven chooses interaction mode through released Floe layout configuration.
Native Desktop always uses desktop interaction. Browser mobile interaction
requires all three conditions: width below 768 CSS pixels, a coarse primary
pointer, and no primary hover capability. Narrow mouse windows retain Activity
and Workbench. Floe owns media-query observation, local space measurement, and

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## One interaction mode
Desktop Welcome and Desktop-hosted Env App configure `mobileQuery: 'not all'`; the Env App recognizes its native host through the existing Desktop bridge.

Resizing a desktop browser cannot rewrite its saved Activity/Workbench choice or activate mobile terminal input.

A hidden toolbar action must retain an explicit reachable entry.

## Temporary desktop navigation
Shell, Flower conversations, Files/Git navigation, and Terminal sessions measure their own shared navigation/content region. When that region cannot fit the current sidebar width plus 480 CSS pixels of main content, the sidebar becomes a transient left side drawer.

Files/Git navigation begins with its mode switch, without a separate Files title row or reserved header space. The switch uses the published field height, including its border and padding, so the sidebar and single-row file toolbar dividers align at every interface scale. The mobile close action shares that row; desktop drawers retain their accessible dialog title and dismissal. Sidebar resizing and local tree scrolling remain available.

Mobile navigation retains its product-specific bottom/side panel behavior under the [mobile Shell](mobile-shell-navigation.md) and [Flower](flower-mobile-navigation.md) contracts.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
## Flower welcome
Desktop Flower retains its mark, title, introduction, working directory, four complete starter suggestions, and keyboard hints even when the chat region is 767 CSS pixels or narrower. Container queries adjust spacing and the suggestion grid; they cannot hide content or switch interaction mode.

Narrow layouts may ellipsize selection titles; explanations remain normal prose and mobile suggestion cards retain their compact presentation.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Persistence and authentication
The Runtime opens apps/filesystem/directory-favorites.sqlite through sqliteutil before service readiness and closes it with Code App. Schema v1 is initialized transactionally; existing tables, objects and records are verified and unsupported or future schemas fail before a writable open.

There is no ten-item cap, automatic deletion, move tracking, grouping or custom naming.

## Client ownership and interaction
One in-memory client per authenticated environment supplies every mounted entry.

Initial load failure offers retry; refresh failure retains displayed paths.

No separate title card, second path line or persistent favorite star occupies the sidebar.

## Compatibility
Runtime compatibility epoch 69 requires this exact authenticated resource and Desktop route allowlist. Floret APIs, domain schema, conversation lifecycle, file-operation authorization and Runtime Service protocol version remain unchanged.

Published Floe owns visible-viewport constraints and drag geometry; Redeven persists settled geometry and preserves reachable controls, local scrolling and destination interaction.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Drag-region synchronization
Desktop projects iframe-relative native drag regions. A settled snapshot must not schedule another frame by rebuilding itself; native pointer/geometry ownership remains upstream.

## Global bands
Ordinary windows use 1000–1099; expanded Flower 2000; its context previews 2100–2199; plugin Panel 3000 and plugin context menu 3100; product modals 4000; command palette 5000. Local menus, tooltips and recovery UI stay within their surface's global band.

## Dialog placement
Mobile plugin/tools navigation belongs to Shell content, not a global Launcher. Backdrop clicks close only the Dialog without reaching Activity beneath it; titlebar controls remain no-drag.

## Visible viewport boundaries
Published Floe owns visible viewport/safe areas, Safari fixed-origin conversion and projected-surface intersection. Do not bypass it with fixed positions, uncapped viewport heights or transforms. Temporary constraints preserve preferred size.

Upstream elastic dragging resists boundary overflow, retains a reachable header and returns the window inside safe bounds on release/interruption. Dragging a maximized header restores preferred size at the grab point and continues the gesture; controls, double-click and mounted body remain independent. Redeven supplies safe-area insets and persists only settled geometry.

## Movable window order
A Shell-lifetime provider registers stable IDs, retains multiply registered IDs until all owners unregister, and assigns bounded MRU order within each window band. Minimized Debug Console is a base-band launcher, not an open window.

## Flower dismissal
Expanded Flower sits above ordinary windows; owned previews sit above Flower and below plugin Panels. Dismissal never restores composer focus, which would expand it again. Host pointer/focus and trusted plugin bridge activation/focus/action events collapse Flower without consuming destination interaction, including cross-origin iframe interaction.

concepts.summary:
The published Floe resource cache owns disposable snapshot restoration, request
coalescing, response fencing, persistence, and capacity eviction. Redeven owns
identity confirmation and explicit presentation projections. Host Applications,
Containers, Web Services, and Codespaces show their most recent successful inventory while

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Identity and authority
The Shell requests `GET /_redeven_proxy/api/ui-cache-scope` as soon as an authenticated connection is available, in parallel with current-session read permission confirmation. The value is not a credential and cannot select request authority.

Container projections follow that same owner instead of clearing their inventory on connection changes.

## Persistence and presentation
Browser clients use Floe's asynchronous IndexedDB adapter. Cache files never enter synchronous UI preferences.

Activating a Codespaces view refreshes its shared inventory; no new polling or connection recovery loop is introduced.

## Actions and recovery
A stale application is resolved through current inventory before launch.

Cached restoration never installs components, requests permissions, launches processes, or starts lifecycle operations.

Rapid reopen uses the same presence owner, and an older presentation release cannot clear a currently open or retained preview.

## Responsiveness
Retention stores only a constant-size presentation token and existing references.

Pixel sampling of a bright HTML page fading onto a dark background must show no brightness rebound. These measurements qualify the tested browser fixture; they do not substitute for packaged Desktop release qualification.

concepts.summary:
Redeven owns file classification, authorized reads, edit state, and preview
placement. Published Floe owns HTML document construction and isolation policy.
Opening an HTML file displays its page by default; source editing requires an
explicit action and write permission. The document cannot access the trusted
shell or authenticated resources. Oversized, truncated, or unreadable content
never executes and retains the existing localized preview error surface.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Page rendering
Files ending in `.html`, `.htm`, or `.xhtml`, regardless of case, open as rendered pages in floating windows, mobile previews, Workbench, and attachment snapshot previews.

It renders an opaque `allow-scripts`, no-referrer iframe; it never inserts file HTML into the trusted shell or navigates to an authenticated file endpoint.

The current Activity file preview and Workbench same-file reuse rules still own placement.

## Placement and interaction
The page fills the reading area and scrolls internally. An unselected Workbench iframe is inert and cannot intercept pointer, keyboard, or wheel input. Unrelated shell updates preserve the live document.

## Source editing and snapshots
Edit opens the existing HTML source editor only when write permission permits. Attachment snapshots remain read-only and show the attached bytes rather than re-reading the live file.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Window boundary
[Floating layers](env-app-floating-layer-order.md) own placement/clamps; title, close and toolbar remain reachable while documents scroll locally.

## Reading area and zoom
Fit uses local CSS pixels excluding padding/scrollbars, unaffected by ancestor/Workbench transforms. Initial fit may enlarge; resize recomputes automatic fit while preserving manual zoom. Attachments retain native PDF controls/contained images and shrinkable containers.

## Rendering ownership
Lazy published `@floegence/floe-webapp-core/pdf` owns PDF layers with scoped CSS. Each PDF/PPTX page has one renderer; stale work cannot replace current resources. Image callbacks match displayed identity. Cancellation is neutral; failures are local/retryable.

## HTML pages
[HTML preview](file-preview-html.md) owns page-first opening, explicit source editing, bounds/isolation and refusal to execute incomplete HTML.

## Markdown enhancements
Mermaid skips theme/sandbox work without diagrams, caches themes and fences stale results. Floating Contents starts closed in the published right-drawer Dialog, preserving width/nodes/scroll. Dismissal affects only Contents; heading activation scrolls Markdown then closes. File changes reset it; headingless files disable it. Main previews retain their sidebar.

Floe roles color headings/links as interaction/info, lower headings/quotes as tip, emphasis as note and code with its dedicated foreground. Raised dark headings retain hue with a lightness floor; tables/metadata use subtle tints and GFM alerts keep semantic roles. Text/inset titles require 4.5:1 contrast across presets/materials, including floating windows. Links retain underline/focus; selection is readable and forced colors use system roles. Theme changes preserve geometry, DOM, selection, focus and scroll.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Close and reopen
Explicit close clears the controller request immediately so the browser is no longer active and focus restoration can proceed.

The same FloatingWindow owner cancels a pending exit; an earlier close completion must not retire the reopened surface.

Closing must not leave an independent timeout or detached browser alive after the window disappears.

## Responsiveness and resource lifetime
Closing must accept subsequent page actions without waiting for exit motion. The focused browser fixture exercises 1,000 directory entries and five cycles, checks synchronous close and frame intervals below 50ms, and verifies that controller close, opener focus, and an underlying action remain responsive.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Companion ownership
Published `BottomBarCompanion` owns geometry, viewport/safe-area clamps, motion, outside dismissal, Escape and mount handling. Its Portal uses the explicit Activity overlay host, never `document.body`. The collapsed field is centered; bounded detail grows upward without changing body geometry. Running work cannot prevent collapse or destination interaction.

## Activity Terminal footer
Desktop Activity Terminal supplies a 24-pixel anchor in its 28-pixel footer, centered in the terminal column with a shrinkable 360-pixel maximum width. Workbench/mobile terminals supply none. Placement does not create another Flower instance, alter transport or route Flower input through the terminal.

## Stable Flower placement
After first access readiness, one retained `EnvAIPage`/`FlowerSurface` moves among explicit hosts. Visibility drives `hidden`, `aria-hidden` and `inert` together. Available unfiltered Workbench placement survives deselection; canvas selection governs input/focus only. [Settings](flower-setup-and-settings.md#retained-panels) own retained panels/forms.

## Contextual Ask Flower
New companion conversations may capture the desktop Activity origin using its read-only page reader. [Turn launcher](flower-turn-launcher.md) owns sending/context actions.

## Presence and summary
[Presence](flower-companion-presence.md) owns collapsed priority, live tails, completion feedback, composer precedence and workspace observation.

## Dismissal, focus, and reads
Outside capture includes shell, anchor and classified Flower-owned Portals. Trusted cross-origin plugin bridge events join host pointer/focus dismissal without consuming the destination. Shared SSE summaries are activity-only; initial/reconnect read baselines and later read envelopes are scoped to the same `UserPublicID`.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
The Workbench Flower widget retains its existing window, canvas, and focus contracts while contributing only a placement host for the Env App-owned Flower product.

The companion never auto-expands for completion, failure, approval, or user input. Showing an available, unfiltered Workbench Flower widget moves the retained product tree into that widget without starting a second list load or live stream, and later canvas deselection does not move it away.

concepts.summary:
Shared Flower UI uses canonical Floret facts and one transcript viewport owner.

Desktop and Env App share this contract.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Stable disclosure and safe content
Activity identity is thread, run, turn and canonical item ID. [Tool sequences](flower-tool-sequences.md) own grouping and bounded thinking; individual details remain available.

Field summaries preserve collapsed labels and result shape without transferring hidden payloads. Disclosure reads selected values; long text uses 16 KiB ranges and a 128 KiB reading window, with explicit selection pins. Closing, hiding or navigating cancels obsolete demand. Markdown reads exact UTF-8 chunks and yields between batches: whitespace cannot be sampled or silently removed because it affects parsing and copied code. A selected Markdown document remains a complete working set rather than a fixed-memory preview.

## Thread query and read details
`Thread Query:` and `Thread Read:` are fixed technical labels; their suffix retains model-authored intent in the user's language. [Thread queries](../ai/flower-thread-queries.md) own lookup, privacy, bounds and failure behavior.

## Web search details
Use one localized action title for visible and accessible labels. Expanded details show actual per-call results/errors, including URL-only sources, without repeating header query, URL, pattern or status.

## Semantic tool icons
Shared Desktop/Env App rows retain compact geometry and explicit glyphs for registered tools, hosted web search, sources, MCP and unknown extensions.

## Intent, inputs and results
Collapsed titles describe invocation intent, never substituted outcomes. Presentation cannot supply execution input or authorization.

## Viewport and gesture ownership
One viewport controller owns transcript position. Layout, focus, animation and growth cannot resume paused reading. [Sequence reading](flower-tool-sequences.md#disclosure-and-reading) owns native nested scrolling; hidden controls are neither focusable nor hit-testable. [SubAgent details](flower-subagent-detail.md) have an independent viewport.

## Thinking duration
Floret's canonical first/last output-chunk receipt times survive hydration, reconnect, restart and Fork. They replace page observations; native continuation reopens the interval and completion ends at the last chunk. Tooltips distinguish received output from provider compute time. Show <1ms below one millisecond and localized Not recorded when absent; never infer timing from neighboring events or turn totals. Legacy page observations remain memory-only.

## Visual motion
Confirmed live thinking fills five petals clockwise, then its center, holds and fades over 2.4 seconds. Sealed, cancelled and disconnected rows are static. Theme tokens, reduced motion, high contrast and forced colors own accessible variants; CSS needs no separate lifecycle. Disclosure uses one reversible Web Animation (180 ms open, 140 ms close); stale completions cannot change presence.

Fresh tool, argument-preview and thinking titles reveal once over 168–360 ms, at most 32 width-adapted steps. Full text, geometry, accessible names and actions exist immediately. After sequence placement, viewport owners make room over 220 ms before reveal; growth retargets without extending the deadline. User scrolling interrupts; paused reading stays paused; reduced motion skips animation. Delivery, results and controls never wait. Concurrent arrivals remain independent; running glyph shimmer starts after reveal without typography changes.

Execution-scoped arrival claims exclude history, navigation, reconnect baselines, hidden disclosures and mounts delayed beyond 450 ms. Claims observe sequence closure before lazy mount and survive preview promotion, disclosure remount, snapshot replacement and completion. A final snapshot may reveal new tools from the previously active execution. Automatic folding waits for admitted title animations and then applies reading protection; manual folding and final replies remain immediate. The title node survives trigger changes; call identity transfers remaining animation time. Failure/approval actions are immediate. Navigation, disposal, hidden documents and reduced motion clear clipping. No character timers, per-frame reactive state or persisted animation facts.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Published Floe Markdown parsing owns GFM syntax with CJK-aware emphasis boundaries for completed and streamed text. Display parsing never writes back to canonical messages or provider cache input. New messages preserve complete sources; old records lacking sources remain readable without rewriting historical data.

## Inline-code references
Inline Markdown code derives from the published Floe `--inline-code-foreground` and `--inline-code-background` pair.

Fenced code, copy behavior and canonical content remain independent.

## Status and live output
Canonical priority is running, queued, attention, unread failure, unread cancellation, unread completion, unavailable, idle. Reduced motion disables flow/tracking/arrival effects while retaining semantic text/color. Live tails use matching current-run facts without exposing raw thinking.

## Completion acknowledgement

Exclude history, queued-only work, failures, cancellation, attention, expired/mismatched runs and completion while other running/queued work remains. Feedback is ephemeral, not canonical presence.

1. Current-thread pending decision, regardless of question type or draft.
2. Ordinary editor for draft, attachment, reference, focus or IME; inspection if editing unavailable.

4. Ordinary editor or read-only/unavailable inspection.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Ownership and persistence
`ai_conversation_preferences` belongs to product schema v11. Transactional v10→v11 validates source/target shapes, preserves data and never infers preferences from old threads. Missing stable scope cannot read another user's defaults.

## Selection events
Patch only the chosen field. Existing-thread edits must succeed before saving memory; memory failure cannot roll back confirmed thread state. Explicit Default differs from absent memory; Default/budget and Off/budget semantics remain.

## Drafts and admission
Draft overrides remain distinct from effective model/directory admission values; old selection cannot seed a new draft. Without explicit/remembered reasoning, root launch freezes explicit Default so retries cannot acquire later memory. Server [canonicalization](../ai/model-reasoning-runtime.md) owns model capability. Existing busy/queued/unresolved-input edit restrictions apply.

## Concurrency and failure
Adapters serialize captured patches and load latest revision; the store atomically merges with compare-and-set. Stale writes return 409 without auto-retry. Captured target/model identity fences late responses against navigation or retargeting.

The originating surface consumes its authoritative response/settings revision without reloading shared model resources; other surfaces refresh persisted preferences. Catalog refresh is reserved for configuration changes, preventing model/reasoning selection from replacing the composer with loading UI.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: This is Redeven product preference policy using already published Floret capabilities, not a generic upstream settings framework. Runtime catalogs, filesystem scope, canonical Thread settings, and immutable Turn execution remain authoritative. Model and directory recovery use existing controls and host notifications, not new switches, save buttons, or confirmation dialogs.

Floret owns canonical history, identity and versions. Redeven authorizes public
projection; one workspace stream delivers it to ThreadCache. Text growth changes

Window loss refreshes that reading interest; transport loss uses the existing

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Ownership and initialization
`ThreadFactsSource.SubscribeFacts` serves account watches, workload/Computer cleanup and workspace observation without bodies or a viewer. Root/child have independent authorized `ThreadWindowSource` interests. One worker coalesces up to 64 dirty parents without blocking the facts pump; see [adapter ownership](../ai/floret-redeven-adapter-and-projection.md).

Register observation before freezing authorized roots in navigation order. Budget/release IDs and backing arrays as pages drain. Ready publishes observer identity, then canonical summaries in drained pages of at most 25; only the last has `baseline_complete`, followed by private read states. Accepted reading updates bypass sidebar preparation; ordinary facts wait for its baseline. Close/cancellation releases subscribers and queued bytes without requiring Next; canonical failure invalidates observation. No arbitrary sidebar timeout or pin-induced skipped roots.

Merge pages immediately; prune only at completion, preserving selection/local creations. First page, confirmed empty inventory or accepted selected detail admits the initial surface; partial empty Ready does not. Explicit HTTP refresh uses cancellable 25-row pages with ten seconds per progressing page and preserves delivered pages on failure. Desktop also cancels history/item POST reads. [Startup](../architecture/flower-startup-presentation.md) owns display.

## Reading, bodies and delivery
Foreground history waits for the current live observer. Ready installs its baseline before releasing navigation into the shared loader. A covered response coalesces later baseline demand; explicit command confirmation remains forced. Navigation, disposal and transport changes cancel obsolete waiters. Reconnect binds a fresh read to the new observer while retaining accepted content, scroll state and unsent drafts.

Root/child slots have independent monotonic revisions. Baseline and deltas share a subscription; replacing a page replaces its interest and fences older revisions. First reads select up to 50 items with 1 KiB text previews and Activity field summaries, subject to the window byte budget. Explicit earlier/newer reads select at most 150 items within 512 KiB; receipts refresh the accepted interval, never replace historical reading with Latest.

Collapsed patch rows use Activity summary display name/change type for one mutation, or localized mutation count for multiple files, without detail reads or invented diff rows/targets. Expansion retains titles, patch totals and each file's statistics.

Root/child window POSTs allow 64 KiB JSON / 150 identities; item/body locators allow 8 KiB. Exact membership budgets 448 KiB canonical preview metadata, excluding hydrated bodies. Selection charges the larger of transmitted size and the original canonical window_bytes carried by compact tool summaries. Network interest stays bounded independently of the reading document. Visited sealed items retain reactive owners and bodies on the confirmed path; eviction removes whole inactive documents. Visible/focused/selected live islands stay mounted. Gap refills stop at the missing interval; prefetch advances only ahead of the reading edge. One coalesced scroll demand owns each handoff; HTTP/layout completion cannot traverse collapsed history recursively. Stationary edge input can request the next page. Failed navigation retains content/drafts and offers localized Retry.

Publish the bounded reading window without completing the surrounding turns for statistics. A sequence shows exact counts only when its loaded boundaries and intervening items/parent events are known; otherwise its sole summary is the localized “Consecutive tool calls” label. Running groups can already have complete counts. Normal scrolling can supply missing evidence, but count presentation never starts history requests, receipt backfill or body reads. Receipt alignment reads at most one preview page per displayed span; missing intervals remain ordinary scroll demand.

The foreground reader owns publication; live baselines wait in its handoff queue. Retention uses one prefix check: sealed ID, kind, turn/run, ordinal and canonical ordinal must match. Reuse only the preceding confirmed cached prefix without inferring a new end from the old window. Pagination preserves manual sequence disclosure through anchor changes and subsequent navigation, and moving canonical rows preserves focus and selected text.

Collapsed Activity summaries carry exact shape, counts, scalars and small display values without per-field body locators. Explicit Activity structure/value reads acquire authorized frozen sources; storage, indexes and migrations stay unchanged.

Only unseen text uses skeletons. Accepted prose, attachments/references, anchors and chosen follow state survive growth, refresh and completion. One observer admits demand within 160 pixels; text/open tools share two slots and a fifteen-second deadline. Visible live text and interactive disclosure precede ordinary visible history reads, then background work; aging every eight admissions prevents starvation. Offscreen/navigation cancellation removes demand and aborts reads; failures offer local Retry.

ThreadCache alone retains expanded bodies by item/turn/run/source identity. Freshly authorized ThreadItemTextReader.ReadItemText reads return at most 16 KiB from the accepted UTF-8 offset. One source task coalesces extents, accepts earlier in-flight prefixes and yields between chunks. No polling, full-prefix/history downloads or duplicate transcript store. A changed source, including live-to-canonical sealing, restarts at its canonical preview byte offset; live and sealed text need not share a suffix or extent. Retain visible prose while bounded chunks assemble the new source, then publish the complete replacement once. Same-source refreshes retain read progress; late old-source chunks cannot overwrite it. Exhausted or terminal body failures expose an explicit localized Retry without replaying execution.

Schema v3 has one decoder. Fragments carry identity, zero-based index/count, total bytes and Base64. Only matching revision/thread/item/turn/run, contiguous version and UTF-8 offset can merge appends inside a 32 KiB fragment. Growth sends locators, not prefixes. Same-source extents coalesce server-side/per browser frame with constant storage, original base version and preserved semantic boundaries. Limits: 16 pending batches, 32 MiB per envelope/subscriber and 32 MiB global retained references. Started frames are immutable; byte-accounted covered versions suppress represented deltas. Summary, private read state and child inventory use independent mailboxes.

Pending controls do not depend on page membership. Server-only authorized 64-item pages collect Computer safety facts only from pending turns, stopping at their user boundaries. Leaf/version confirmation rejects mixed snapshots; oversized safety collections use individual member reads. No full View or historical bodies cross this path. Missing authority or a broken sequence invalidates observation.

Measured offscreen sections retain DOM and intrinsic height while skipping layout. Returning to inspected content preserves disclosure state and nested offsets; report choices belong to the displayed thread, so a Fork does not inherit its source thread's manual disclosure; unchanged sections and unrelated message projections retain identity. One scroll controller owns writes and corrects the visible reading anchor before paint, including stationary edge input and replacement of a summary or placeholder. Readiness notifications remain scheduled independently of before-paint correction.

Cold sealed bodies stage all bounded chunks inside their existing item record and keep the loading presentation until complete, including across reconnect. Complete Markdown publishes atomically with no entrance height animation or partial table/code/list formatting. Existing readable prose remains visible during source replacement; live sources still grow incrementally. Root and child navigation suppress arrival scrolling until the destination is positioned and revealed at its final geometry. Cache accounting traverses each raw object once without recursively unwrapping reactive subtrees or subscribing to their fields.

Compaction decorations accompany visible anchors and the active run's latest operation. Paging restores historical decorations; canonical context remains complete.

ThreadCache evicts inactive detail at twelve threads or 32 MiB estimated detail bytes; lightweight navigation summaries survive eviction. Selected, retained and in-flight owners are protected until release. Append logs retain at most 256 chunks / 256 KiB, with absolute cursors and exact-source catch-up for a paused Markdown consumer. These are cache budgets, not a cap on an explicitly active document or selected text.

History loading and terminal catch-up share the floating notice below. Catch-up reuses the 200 ms feedback deadline: fast completion mounts nothing, data publication remains immediate, and overlapping reads never duplicate notices.

## Immediate send feedback
[Command/composer ownership](flower-turn-launcher.md) shows captured input immediately, retains request-key DOM identity through admission, and separates SendAck from authorized windows without a second lifecycle.

## Recovery and interaction
The coalesced detail loader owns recovery under one fifteen-second deadline: retry the entire baseline/preparation after 200, 600 and 1200 ms, at most four attempts. New revisions discard unpublished pages and obsolete envelopes. Leaf changes are recoverable; foreign threads and malformed ordering are terminal. Navigation, disposal and connection changes cancel reads/backoff. Success adds no timer or read. Accepted DOM, drafts and scroll remain; exhausted refresh offers Retry with interrupted-sync wording, while first-load failure keeps its own title. Recovery never replays commands or execution.

Revision-fenced `history_invalidated` permits one automatic bounded read per selection/manual action; repeated loss offers Retry. Failed reads preserve content/anchors. `history-release` cancels installed/pending interest without waiting for slow reads; child close releases only its slot. One-shot windows cannot reuse old subscription membership.

Transport loss, handshake deadlines and sequence gaps use the existing bounded backoff owner. Final disposal aborts transport without publishing reactive state or cache boundaries into a component tree being torn down; reconnect continues to publish its boundary. Activity visibility observers attach after DOM adoption and disconnect with their row. Authorization, capacity, incompatible versions and malformed contracts are terminal. Classify fetch/bridge errors before mapping; mapper exceptions are not retried. Diagnostics expose category, HTTP status and epoch, never bodies or arbitrary server messages. SSE sync loss is 503, baseline timeout 504, invalid request 400, capacity 429. Unknown command results retain request keys; disconnect cannot replay effects.

One floating stack owns connection/unconfirmed status, settings reads, initial/detail/history failures, parent-report recovery and return-to-parent navigation. Main, embedded and child notices consume no transcript height; collapsed-companion notices float above its editor. Loading uses the sidebar's four wave bars, localized text, live status and reduced-motion support. Errors retain explanations and recovery actions; terminal connection failure offers Resync. Notices stack without overlap and alone accept pointer input. The composer omits duplicate recovery and keeps its progress slot height. Canonical cancellation/activity owns Stopping. Publications read one canonical summary; Viewer/current-only updates cannot invent loaded coverage. [Approvals/input](flower-approval-context.md), [read state](flower-read-state.md) and [process disclosure](flower-turn-process-disclosure.md) own their policies.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Transcript reading scale
Assistant/user text uses `0.875rem` and unitless `1.75` line height. Composer controls retain published control scale.

## Assistant reading roles
Body/headings retain the chat foreground. Presentation does not rewrite Markdown or infer metadata from authored bold text, dates, identifiers or citations. [Citations](flower-citations.md) own destinations/copy.

## Filled messages and content
Sent text/answered-question receipts use `selection-bg`/`selection-fg`. Text, placeholders and actions share the right edge; the full-row history wrapper makes the 78% desktop bubble limit relative to the transcript. Short text fits intrinsically; narrow views retain the full-column limit. Error/code insets use readable foreground and selection roles over their own backgrounds.

## User media and resources
Order is image thumbnails, wrapping resource cards, text bubble, then timestamp/copy. Resource/image-only messages omit empty bubbles. Canonical previews use exact thread/turn/reference identity; queued actions retain their separate authority/click guard.

## Native text selection
Filled text, including transparent table headers, uses contrasting `selection-on-primary` roles. Selection never changes parsing, copying or transport. Browser checks require 4.5:1 ordinary/selected text across all presets/materials. [Highlighting](flower-code-highlighting.md) retains its own stable-content contract.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
The composer always keeps its model label visible without an availability spinner or busy status.

Runtime status distinguishes no Desktop provider (`not_configured`), configured but unavailable keys or catalog (`missing_keys` or `empty`), and actual connection or protocol errors.

## Model identity and recovery
Thread snapshots, list items, and patches carry `model_id` and `reasoning_selection` as thread defaults. The last is a disabled, ungrouped display of a thread's missing model; Flower never silently replaces it.

See [reasoning selection ownership](flower-reasoning-selection.md) for loading, draft, and submission rules.

## Web search presentation
Model choices display the shared search badge from the server's readonly `web_search` projection. A provider brand or frontend model name never enables search. See [model directory ownership](../ai/model-directory-and-selection.md).

## Permission and navigation
Below the 768px viewport breakpoint, the composer keeps permission status and selection in its own More panel, alongside any other overflow controls.

Saving disables only the permission control, prevents duplicate requests, merges the authoritative settings response, and restores the confirmed value on failure.

Warm sessions switch without provider or transcript remount and stale loads cannot replace the current thread.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Flower does not treat the global model or permission as an existing-Thread launch override. After creation, its `model_id`, `reasoning_selection`, and `permission_type` are authoritative; Thread changes write to its settings, while new-thread overrides stay connection-local and never update environment defaults.

The header switcher is only a product-specific compact presentation; it does not create a second selected-thread owner or change the requested, committed, and content-presented ordering.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Model request
Each logical request and attempt has its own start, first-output time, last semantic-progress time and estimated received output tokens. Local tools, approvals and user input never use this model-pause presentation.

Only phase text is a live region; numerical updates are readable without repeated automatic announcements.

## Progress symbol
The shared Flower mark retains its five-petal geometry.

The symbol is decorative beside the existing localized status text and does not create another live announcement or execution state.

## Edit arguments
The frozen tool definition supplies one optional argument preview parser per call. Their input budget is 1 MiB per call, with bounded JSON depth and field counts.

[Confirmed file Activity](flower-file-activity.md) remains the durable outcome.

## Connection setup
OpenAI offers API keys or verified local ChatGPT accounts. Registration and model selection stay independent; endpoints stay flat and permissions unchanged.

## Kimi
One Kimi choice offers API or Kimi Code. Drafts isolate keys, endpoints and models; close clears them. Switching rejects stale discovery. Saved methods stay fixed; add another connection to change service. Cards label methods; IDs, aliases, selections and history stay unchanged.

Use short names and access labels. Explain keys, quotas and saved methods in the access tooltip; model limits in the model tooltip. Icon links open official guidance. Code keeps regional endpoints and reviewed IDs; billing never falls back.

## Search and secrets
Provider and model search switches must both be on; preferences remain editable when provider search is off. Backend policies own availability. See [failure recovery](flower-failure-recovery.md). Stored keys use fixed dot placeholders. Null removes a key; omitted/blank patches preserve it. Catalog refresh never selects new models.
