sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Flower read state is a Redeven-owned per-user activity watermark. A separate loaded-content revision prevents metadata or private confirmations from qualifying stale body content as current.

No storage format or historical watermark is reset.

Neither a detail response nor a hidden measuring transcript qualifies as
presentation. Selection telemetry and read acknowledgement wait until the
[destination presentation boundary](flower-thread-selection.md) releases its
prepared viewport, then retain the existing visible-document and content-revision

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## First-time setup
Welcome setup requires no selected thread, configured provider or usable model, and absent/`not_configured`/`empty` Desktop source. Desktop `local_host` opens the current surface's settings, never another Welcome window or a remote destination. Artwork has no glow or continuous animation.

## Starter tasks
Four editable drafts cover current-folder understanding, connected computer, installed applications and folder organization. Names/dates alone never justify deletion. The [companion](flower-activity-companion.md) omits the grid.

## Settings composition
Settings edit the environment profile even with a Desktop model source. Flat sections preserve identity/drafts. Immediate switches block duplicate edits and roll back on failure.

## Provider configuration
[Provider configuration](flower-provider-configuration.md) owns authentication, layout and connection-before-model sequencing.

## Retained panels
FlowerSurface retains chat/extensions and a lazily loaded settings form in a bounded scrollable modal. Covered chat/navigation remain inert through close and do not acknowledge reads. Settings interactions belong to the companion: dialog close keeps it expanded; host collapse closes both while retaining form/progress/errors.

## Saving and ownership
Independent adapter operations save permission, model profile and default model. Permission uses a serialized 700 ms coalescing controller, fences older responses and restores the last confirmed value on failure. Computer-use failures restore the confirmed switch and expose errors.

concepts.title: Flower streaming stability
concepts.description: Incremental Markdown and local record updates preserve interactive identity.

frontmatter.description: Incremental Markdown and local record updates preserve interactive identity.
frontmatter.title: Flower streaming stability

concepts.summary: Flower renders actor-native changes through the indexed ThreadCache and the published Floe incremental Markdown parser. Ordinary growth changes the affected text/DOM region only. Stable history, code colors, copy controls, focus, selection and disclosure choices remain intact. A semantic change must remain visible; malformed updates recover through the single [live-state boundary](flower-live-timeline.md), never by omitting output or substituting a second lifecycle.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Local data and rendering
Snapshots initialize indexed item/message records. Text/body extent growth retains history-window, turn and decoration identity; only membership, replacement, turn or context changes recompute their relevant metadata. Growing argument previews update their existing reactive block without revisiting completed tools; the same canonical validation still rejects invalid counters and retires withdrawn/stale attempts. Actual removal moves focus to an adjacent action or composer unless navigation already moved it. Regression fixtures retain 100 and 10,000 archived items and require zero historical ordinal reads for twenty text appends.

## One Markdown parser
Released Floe `createIncrementalMarkdownParser` owns Marked/CJK/GFM: reset sets a complete source baseline, append returns changed regions, finish authoritatively parses/corrects all content. Changed snapshots reset the complete baseline because tokens can move offsets and identities; reuse exact tokens at unchanged offsets and retire other old regions. Identical-source metadata retains regions. Completion, process collapse and replacement preserve all authored blocks. See [highlighting](flower-code-highlighting.md) and [media](flower-inline-media.md).

## Soft live text reveal
Added prose ranges fade to theme color over 320 ms through CSS custom highlights, without splitting nodes, delaying delivery, moving lines or replaying read content. History/corrections render immediately; links, code, media and controls keep their colors and behavior. Twenty fixed CSS phases use originating `currentColor`, avoiding stylesheet mutation, computed-style reads or per-frame inline writes.

Each owner has at most 32 transient groups; diff inspection is bounded at 8,192 characters/128 text nodes per region. Larger changes remain immediately readable. Completion lets valid effects settle; reset, unmount, hidden documents, reduced motion and forced colors clear them. Historical owners schedule no frames/listeners; unsupported highlight APIs use immediate text.

## Disclosure and layout
Cold historical text remains a loading presentation until all canonical chunks arrive. A reconnect retains both read offset and unpublished staging. Complete bodies enter at final geometry without height animation; browser acceptance samples table, code, list and text geometry from the first exposed frame. Existing readable text and live output retain their separate incremental behavior.

Composer/approval font measurements use releasable completion/error listeners, never retaining detached surfaces through `FontFaceSet.ready`. Companion reads only the newest relevant record and a bounded normalized Unicode tail.

## Interaction cadence and resources
One bounded frame queue applies every envelope in order, including semantic boundaries. Transport callbacks enqueue; each envelope commits atomically inside its host reactive batch. A four-millisecond cooperative budget includes reactive work and yields between envelopes through a timer task. It cannot preempt an individual expensive envelope. Apply failures are captured inside the reactive batch, allowing recovery notifications to commit before the error is rethrown to the connection owner. Ready waits for the queue to drain before admitting navigation; other reads pause at sixteen pending frames or one MiB. Disposal, failure and epoch changes release waiting readers and fence obsolete callbacks.

Coalesce only contiguous single-item appends with matching thread, item, turn, run and reading revision. Facts must match except timestamps and monotonic progress in the same request attempt. Preserve semantic boundaries and component clears. Join chunks once, preserving UTF-8 offsets and versions. A detected pending gap invalidates that batch and reports one synchronization error to the connection owner; no partially accepted batch is published.

Growth limits remain 64 frames, four MiB encoded bytes and a 250 ms presentation deadline; drag/resize cadence is 75 ms. Semantic work replaces a stalled animation-frame schedule with an immediate timer without overtaking earlier growth. One supported atomic wire envelope can use the existing 32 MiB allowance plus the growth reserve, while backpressure blocks further reads. Diagnostics expose bytes, age, count and application duration without transcript content. Copy feedback starts only on success, lasts 1.6 seconds, and never reports clipboard failure as success.

The opt-in real-Service qualifier freezes history/provider cadence, builds production UI and measures runtime, all Electron process CPU, frame/input/click/output latency, allocations and wire bytes. After timing it opens exact turn/nested-sequence controls and compares every assistant/thinking item with canonical content. Task-specific thresholds are hard gates, separate from bounded CI/main integration.

The synthetic qualifier measures task/script CPU, sampled allocations, retained heap, decoded envelopes and queue metrics; state-mutating probes run after timing. Decoded payload is not encrypted traffic, sampled allocation is not peak heap, and synthetic results do not qualify production providers/transports.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Terminal facts
Floret owns the nested `ActivityItem.presentation` contract and merges results with their stable call presentation. Labels and descriptions are authoritative; the typed operation supplies localized fallback text.

The five-line independently scrolling output viewport retains its existing owner.

An omitted output field is pending content, never an empty canonical frame with a nonzero first sequence. Wait for small-field hydration before polling or installing its sequence; large fields use source-bound ranges, then acknowledge their watermark before adding process deltas. Existing output and selection survive handoff.

Inactive output caches have 200-entry / 8 MiB estimated-byte limits. Mounted outputs remain retained until release; frame metadata coalesces after 128 records without changing sequence checks. These cache limits do not truncate an active process output or its canonical history.

## Interaction boundary
[Activity disclosure interaction](flower-activity-interaction.md) owns stable triggers, manual choices, animation, transcript following, and floating controls across all renderers. Approval state is never a row badge, chip, metadata line, title suffix, tooltip, detail, or ordinary activity ARIA label. Completing a decision removes that dock without inserting an approval outcome into history.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Selection and navigation
Rail feedback precedes visible commit by two animation callbacks and a task; hidden documents do not wait for frames. Latest intent supersedes earlier work; summary effects cannot bypass foreground coordination.

Reveal only after accepted detail, measurable layout and visible historical text settle. The scroll owner also prepares the latest active tool sequence after row placement, so both outer and inner tails are positioned before reveal. Restored activity details settle without opening animation; explicit group folds survive and retain a current activity label. Initial positioning has no smooth scrolling or time-based fallback. One cancellable 200 ms deadline spans detail/body/layout loading feedback; ready content/errors appear immediately. Selection, New chat and disposal cancel old feedback; frame, composer/navigation remain stable and failed body reads remain local and retry with renewed viewport demand or reconnect.

Cached destinations flush render effects; visible rows pass `checkVisibility({ contentVisibilityAuto: true })`. ResizeObserver adjusts above-viewport growth before paint, while reveal/body work stays in rAF; visibility events reuse this pass. Navigation clears arrival motion. No positioning polls or per-row observers. Explicit wheel/touch/scrollbar/keyboard input can interrupt preparation; scroll events alone cannot.

Two read slots prioritize visible text/margin and cancel obsolete demand. ThreadCache retains immutable bodies. Growth/refresh/completion never restart selection or remove accepted prose; [live delivery](flower-live-timeline.md) owns validation/retry. Selection opens Latest; reading restoration is separate. Ordinary threads sort by descending creation time, then ascending ThreadID.

## Continuous history and concurrent activity

Users browse earlier and newer history by scrolling. Viewport demand reads
canonical windows automatically; no load-earlier or load-newer action is part
of normal navigation. Retained windows preserve visible, selected and focused
rows while gaps are filled in either direction. Stable item identities preserve
expanded details and scroll anchors during live appends and replacements.
When a collapsed tail is shorter than the viewport, prepending history retains
the visible trailing room required by its reading anchor. The scroll owner
reclaims that room only as it leaves view or content fills it; loading must not
push existing messages down to fill the viewport. Viewport resizing preserves
the anchor, and destination preparation clears the temporary geometry. The
transcript content observer attaches after DOM mounting and corrects growth
before paint. This adds no history reads, persisted state or disclosure changes.
The floating Latest action stays available above the composer while reading
away from latest, including at the bottom of a historical window. It is hidden
during destination preparation and keeps pointer-gesture protection. If the
latest window is already installed, the action scrolls smoothly and retires
retained trailing room at arrival. Otherwise it cancels obsolete reading demand,
installs one bounded tail interest and reveals the prepared latest destination;
it never walks intervening pages. Main and child views share these semantics.
The accepted history baseline belongs to the live observer and reading revision;
superseded navigation cannot replace a newer selection.

Collapsed tools and parent reports retain presentation previews. Full activity
bodies and report text are requested when disclosed, under fresh authorization.
Collapse, navigation and disposal cancel unused demand; reconnect restores active
consumers. Retry is local to an actual read failure. Released empty activity
sources use Floret's canonical default presentation in source order.

Field-only activity presentation remains disabled for ordinary product history
until complete renderer parity is qualified. Complete body expansion is retained;
computer evidence and target hydration can still require full canonical reads.
This release does not promise a fixed opening latency or globally bounded memory
for all expanded terminal output.

## Detail read ownership
Floret supplies canonical summaries, source-bound windows and exact body reads; ThreadCache owns selection/detail with twelve entries. The bounded coordinator shares navigation, confirmation and reference-preflight demand. Cancellation never reconnects the workspace stream.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Resizing
One 220–380 CSS-pixel preference owns desktop sidebar width. Inline resizing updates only its grid track, at most once per frame; drawer width applies only in overlay mode. Mobile, companion and embedded layouts keep their sizing.

One primary-pointer gesture retains the latest sample and settles on release, cancellation, lost capture, blur, layout change or unmount. Release listeners, frames and cursor/selection shielding; persist once per gesture or immediately for keyboard changes. Storage failure cannot interrupt interaction. Width changes cannot reparse Markdown or invalidate the full transcript.

## Rename from the conversation header
The header pencil edits the existing ThreadID, including during execution/loading, with canonical title prefilled and selected. Header/sidebar share one save owner and thread cache.

## Selection and detail reads
[Selection](flower-thread-selection.md) owns deferred commitment, bounded reads, cancellation and recovery. ThreadCache owns committed selection/detail; sidebar intent reserves feedback only.

## Reference action
Right-click, More and Shift+F10 share the ThreadID-owned menu. [References](flower-thread-references.md) own deduplication, preview, admission and recovery.

## Pending replies and approvals
Localized reply/approval labels appear beside the title with bounded status/progress width. Background updates use the workspace stream without selection.

## Pin ordering
The stable `.flower-thread-rows` owner contains inline size for real/skeleton rows; movable cards cannot be size containers. Keyboard order matches visible search/pin-overlay order. Failed pin operations undo only their own presentation and reconcile via the existing summary stream or one explicit command read.

## Stable presentation and convergence
Key rows by ThreadID and group labels separately. ThreadCache owns summaries; each batch publishes once under existing title/revision rules, preserving menus, focus and running-wave continuity.

concepts.title: Flower consecutive tool sequences
concepts.description: Compact tools and bounded thinking without hiding dialogue or taking over active reading.

frontmatter.description: Compact tools and bounded thinking without hiding dialogue or taking over active reading.
frontmatter.title: Flower consecutive tool sequences

concepts.summary:
Flower groups consecutive tools in Desktop and Env App.
Adjacent thinking becomes an inline node in that sequence, including leading and final thoughts. Active sequences default open. Settled sequences fold when following assistant output completes or the canonical turn ends; temporary gaps between calls and unfinished prose do not trigger a fold. Explicit choices and active inspection survive those boundaries.
When an answered input falls between work segments in a settled turn, each
settled tool sequence remains independently collapsed, including the newest
sequence. Active tools retain their existing disclosure behavior.
This is product presentation over existing published Floret facts; it introduces
no upstream contract, canonical summary or backend migration.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Boundaries and identity
A sequence contains at least two nodes in one thread/turn/run, including a tool; one call plus following thinking qualifies. Calls, failures and argument previews qualify. Adjacent leading and trailing thinking joins the group; thinking alone stays standalone. Complete counts report calls, thinking, failures and subtask updates without synthesizing summaries. A newer single-call segment can settle an older sequence without changing its explicit disclosure choice.

Prose, user messages, interactions, compaction, Goal updates, approvals and non-tool errors break groups. SubAgent tools and canonically scoped report/completion events join the sequence; unresolvable parent-event ownership remains a boundary. Returned uncertain tool errors stay in their exact thread/turn/run sequence and show a localized unconfirmed-result count when coverage is complete, including when collapsed; invalid success-with-uncertainty facts and uncertain parent lifecycle events remain boundaries. Goal calls and Web Search remain tools; running attention and SubAgent waits remain in the sequence; other waiting states and approvals break it. Empty live assistant placeholders are transparent; text whose body remains unknown is not evidence of continuity. An answered input splits work in a settled turn: sequences on both sides default closed, including the newest, while explicit choices and active calls retain disclosure policy. Whole-turn disclosure remains independent.

Canonical call identity retains row lifetime; the first loaded node anchors a group and thinking moves in place. Pagination retains an existing anchor while the canonical first node becomes the DOM owner; both share the same disclosure choice for subsequent navigation. Preserve source order, final output, actions and errors. Adjacent icons connect with theme-owned active/completed/failure states.

## Count completeness
A group needs both known boundaries and no missing items or parent events inside its interval. A partial history window can contain complete groups; a running turn can already have complete counts. Unknown coverage shows only the localized “Consecutive tool calls” label, including its accessible name. Do not show partial totals, running counts, latest-tool previews or count-loading messages. Known failures retain attention styling and their original detail behavior. Normal pagination may reveal exact statistics in place, preserving disclosure, focus and selection. Statistics never request additional history, whole turns, receipt pages or unopened bodies.

## Disclosure and reading
Session-local choices are keyed by runtime, thread and tool. Defaults settle on first observation and once when an open active group becomes eligible for automatic collapse. Explicit choices survive completion, consecutive calls, updates, reconnects and navigation until refresh; later observations cannot reopen closed groups. Focus, selection, gestures, open details/thinking and reading away from the tail protect expansion.
Each choice owns its reactive subscription; changing one group cannot notify every historical group. Inspection can retain an already open group but cannot reopen a closed one. Only a direct disclosure or explicit navigation action can reveal it.

Closed groups initially mount only row shells and summary. Details mount on first expansion and remain mounted but inert after folding; new members of manually closed groups wait. Whole-turn closure likewise retains previously inspected bodies after motion. Existing row owners lend DOM to the first node's viewport and restore it on disposal, preserving focus, selection and nested detail state. Unchanged groups/members retain identity during content growth; membership, status, disclosure and order changes replace only affected immutable projections.

Historical thinking reads observe the displayed thinking node, which moves with its sequence, rather than the vacated message shell. Pending sealed thinking registers visibility demand only while explicitly expanded; nested viewport clipping still gates reads. Visible live thinking retains its existing read policy. One shared two-slot queue owns reads, cancellation and retries; explicit thinking demand receives interactive priority. Folding, leaving the viewport and navigation cancel obsolete demand. Completed text stays reusable, and loading status reflects an actual queued/in-flight request. Closed tools never acquire body reads or mount their detail content.

Desktop sequence rows are 1.75rem tall and the viewport fits ten compact rows, capped at 65% of transcript height on short windows. Coarse-pointer rows retain 2.75rem targets. Expanded details share this bounded viewport; short content retains natural height without canonical truncation. Thinking uses 20rem, 45% of the window and the transcript limit. Both expose thin scrollbars, keyboard focus, localized names and reachable summary controls.

Thinking, sequences and read-only terminal/file/diff/excerpt/code details use native ancestor scroll chaining. Inner regions consume only input they can scroll; short regions and outward edge input reach the next ancestor. The transcript controller uses the same wheel/touch/keyboard chain: upward input reaching it pauses following; an actual return to bottom resumes it. Explicit CSS containment, cancelled events and zoom remain local. Interactive terminals/editors retain their input owners.

Inner active content and the transcript use the same input-aware scroll controller. Explicit wheel, touch, keyboard or scrollbar reading pauses following; geometry changes, programmatic scroll events, image loading and row placement cannot create reading intent. Each open sequence observes its mounted children through that owner, preserving native nested input chaining and reading anchors. Every explicit opening positions the latest tool before paint, including reopening after calls arrived while closed. Navigation waits for row placement and the latest active sequence destination as well as the transcript. Restored activity details settle without opening motion during preparation. Manually folded groups remain folded and, when counts are complete, show the latest canonical tool label beside their counts; this preview never requests unopened bodies. Manual collapse focuses the group button. Thinking remains in the user-selected state on completion and restores its saved inner offset on reopening. [Activity motion](flower-activity-interaction.md#visual-motion) coordinates placement and bounded arrival scrolling with both viewport owners.

Controls expose viewport IDs and localized counts; hidden nodes leave no gaps. Shared narrow-layout, pointer, focus, reduced-motion and forced-color rules apply in both product catalogs.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Core commands reject missing, duplicate, invalid or conflicting IDs; only the legacy RPC adapter may fill a missing one. [Goals](../ai/flower-goals.md) share the outbox. Empty-thread creation retains text/reference/attachment authority; first Send binds staged resources to the authorized canonical thread. Unknown effect outcomes are terminal with safe explanation and no replay action.

## Immediate send feedback
The immutable transport outbox owns submitted text, references and attachment
metadata before IndexedDB or HTTP completes. Ordinary sends render a pending
user row immediately and consume only the captured draft; newer edits stay in
the composer. Request-key message and section identities survive canonical
admission, including receipt/live ordering and prepended history. Images reserve
the same thumbnail geometry and use the authorized staged preview until admitted.
Failed and unknown outcomes retain the frozen request for explicit recovery;
server 5xx responses never prove rejection or authorize a fresh request identity.

Product admission uses published SendAck and narrow canonical summaries. HTTP
and RPC return admission identity without a post-commit history read; authorized
window observation supplies presentation separately. Agent preparation binds the
already persisted execution authority to the admitted turn. No duplicate
post-admission authority write or second conversation lifecycle is introduced.
Full model history remains an engine execution requirement, not a prerequisite
for painting the submitted message.

## Restored data and preserved inputs
New submissions capture storage generation immediately, even behind paused dispatch. Rejected input stays copyable/restorable; running it requires explicit new submission, never resumed old approvals/effects.

## Context preview presentation
One Env App `FlowerContextPreviewWindow` uses existing preview/text components for launcher and draft/canonical snapshots. Launcher owns attachment IO, sequencing and URL cleanup; Flower owns validity. Related-surface markers preserve input ownership; Escape dismisses preview before companion.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Canonical facts and eligibility
Validated ThreadView/HistoryPage turn facts include exact TurnID/RunID, optional control kind, start/end, outcome, elapsed/wait/work durations, ordered intermediate/final item IDs and complete-final boundary. Summaries cannot author them or trigger collapse; unknown output remains visible.

A single thinking-only process keeps its existing thinking disclosure and timing; it never gains a redundant work-duration summary or divider on completion. Eligibility follows typed process structure, not prompt text or elapsed-time heuristics. Other process summaries show at most two nonzero time units with subsecond copy. Interleaved answers use a static overview counting calls, failures and answered inputs, never a whole-turn toggle. [Sequences](flower-tool-sequences.md) independently fold settled work on each side.

## Reading and interface state
Running/preparing/retrying/finalizing/waiting turns stay expanded without a toggle. After a canonical outcome and end time, confirmed intermediate/typed process rows fold automatically, including the latest failed/cancelled/interrupted turn. Final and trailing partial output remain visible. Focus, selection, gestures, open details/thinking and reading away from the tail retain inspected work; observation cannot later undo that protection. Capture an unaffected visible anchor only when a real automatic collapse starts, and correct geometry through the existing scroll owner. Open/closed choices survive pagination, reconnects and regrouping. A newly classified row under inspection remains visible until the next explicit group toggle, without reopening other folded rows. Only an explicit disclosure or navigation action can open a closed group. Inspected bodies stay mounted and inert when folded, preserving nested choices and offsets. Main, embedded and child views share rendering with separate scroll owners.

## Layout and accessibility
Automatic turn/sequence folding settles summary insertion and process removal in one layout update before paint. Explicit manual open/close keeps the existing motion and reduced-motion preference; the disclosure owner retains the interaction choice. Canonical Path order, never timestamps, positions messages/receipts. Dialogue, final segments and secret-answer redaction remain intact.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
[Directory selection](filesystem-picker-navigation.md) owns validation; this contract owns entry points and destinations.

## Header and new-conversation entry points
The full-page header has a borderless folder/name browse button; new-conversation welcome selects the draft directory without persistent full-path secondary text. Only picker confirmation remembers a validated real directory. Browsing, cancellation, suggestions and destination navigation never write it; created-thread directories remain immutable.

## Directory and menu ownership
Right-click captures its row's thread/directory without loading, selecting or acknowledging it. Updates cannot retarget actions; handled child events cannot open outer menus. Copy/cancel restores valid triggers without scrolling.

## Destination behavior
Activity Files reuses its singleton window/geometry; Terminal creates a new session. Workbench creates the matching widget. Request IDs, lazy loading, terminal admission and layout persistence retain ownership. Created-thread browsing includes ThreadID; menu/terminal actions require it.

## Availability and recovery
Browsing and Terminal availability are separate. Disabled reasons/errors are explicit; rejected terminal paths cannot silently fall back to Home. Existing transport, process, authorization and persistence owners remain; Flower adds no queue, lifecycle mirror or retry owner.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Capability and generation
Use workspace-v1 only after the exact client confirms revision, path-status, directory-scope and stash-section capabilities. Client replacement discards old capability/generation state and late responses. Files never falls back to unbounded legacy workspace reads. Moving from Files into Workspace opens a fresh generation before applying section/scope.

## Loading and recovery
Git shell/navigation stay mounted; each panel owns initial loading/errors without a second curtain. Diff requests and nested file references must satisfy the JSON-only transport contract.

## Invalidation
One protocol-level `GitWorkspaceInvalidationBus` advances monotonically. Every dispatched effect invalidates in `finally` for success, application failure or unknown transport result; preview/validation does not.

## Files decoration
Filesystem navigation never waits for Git. Detection uses the committed path and repository identity; prior directories cannot leak repo facts. Replacement generations are bounded and preserve committed decoration. Section identity disambiguates staged/unstaged/untracked/conflicted and stash rows.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Workspace revisions provide read consistency, not mutation authorization. UI cancellation is an ownership optimization, not proof that a dispatched effect did not run; invalidation remains mandatory for unknown outcomes.

Non-Git Flowersec outbound allocation is outside this feature's transport budget and must not be presented as fixed by UI batching.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Type roles and boundaries
Env App/Desktop bundle Inter Variable with shared script fallbacks. Guidance, errors, labels/dialogs use published roles, not fixed 13–14px or generic utilities. sections.title: Contract

Activity Bar Plugins opens a Shell-root Launcher without changing the normal surface. Search intersects category with NFKC/locale-case-folded display names, canonical keywords and explicit locale aliases. Tablet/desktop details overlay the grid without reflow and restore originating-row focus.

## Session recovery
An authenticated session-ready transition invokes idempotent Host `recoverEnabled` without a stability timer. All placements consume Host `action_state`; trust, grants, policy or recovery flags cannot derive `can_open`.

## Installation and package review
[Installation progress](plugin-installation-progress.md) owns durable Execution observation and approved setup; [package review](plugin-package-review.md) owns external packages. Failures preserve placement rather than delete components.

Plugin Center joins inventory, grants, Host requirements and policy. Method effects cannot rename granted capabilities. Failure reloads authority and requires a new confirmation.

## Activity windows and pinned pages
Each window creates one fresh `PluginSurfaceSlot` through `openSurfaceInSlot`. Opening/bridge failures replace the iframe with local recovery; timeouts explain delay and offer Retry. Restart restores shortcuts but starts on a built-in page, never automatically opens third-party content.

## Workbench widgets and placement
[Layout continuity](plugin-layout-continuity.md) owns saved bindings, atomic placement, exact removal and recovery. Status overlays cannot forward input, guess focus or create a second bridge. Unpin removes only the shortcut.

## Confirmation and teardown
One abort-aware FIFO dialog decides requests independently with initial Cancel focus. Hidden, retired or revoked surfaces cannot approve queued work. Retired surfaces cannot download; Shell neither uploads nor retains exported bytes.

sections.body:
## Catalog and Session assignment
Redeven owns `apps/terminal/groups.sqlite` as a versioned product database. Future versions, wrong kinds, and schema drift fail closed without replacing the file.

Reorder persists one complete non-Default order in a single database transaction and revision; Default remains protected at order zero.

## Activity, Workbench, and view-local state
One Terminal Session Catalog Provider owns the browser projection, the live in-memory Session display order, and the Redeven-specific `session_id -> group_id` membership map for the Environment. List requests carry membership and lifecycle fences, so an older response cannot overwrite a local move or newer notification.

Search matches Group name, Group path, and Session presentation; a matching folded child is revealed temporarily without changing that saved preference.

## Interaction and asynchronous lifecycle
The sidebar renders Group headers with explicit expand/collapse and scoped create-Session actions.

Header decoration must not offset that geometry on desktop or under Workbench scaling.

Individual failures are returned as explicit Session IDs; those Sessions remain hidden, no success is fabricated, and no silent retry loop is introduced.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Group membership is not Workbench placement, shell working directory, controller ownership, attachment identity, or persistent Session recovery. No Activity or Workbench component may maintain a second membership map, infer membership from paths, or repair an unknown Group by changing a Session to Default. Group disclosure and metadata updates remain renderer-neutral UI state and must not remount `TerminalSessionRuntime`.

business services run. Solid Runtime node cards sit inside tinted dashed visual
groups; external dependencies use a separate card treatment. Default connections
show root-level overview; hover and focus show only the current group or host's

Browsers retain popup-blocking feedback, and native refusal or failure remains visible through localized command feedback without starting another opening path.

Separate responsibilities   include cloud controllers, node agents, container runtimes, network plugins,   service meshes, ingress, operators, registries, observability, identity, secret   and certificate services, streaming, and metadata; repeated instances of the   same responsibility keep the same icon.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Layout and routing
Automatic layout and library thumbnails use the same published Floe layout engine, direction, layers, and visibility projection. Saved positions guide ordering within a layer and never override its rank. Positioned objects without relationships still contribute their actual world bounds, so fitting a newly mapped or isolated node keeps it inside the viewport.

## Connection scopes
Default browsing shows one directed overview connector per root endpoint pair. Group-internal relationships remain in the canonical pool overview and never create a group self-loop.

The interactive overview and library thumbnails always paint the root overview, even while the main canvas shows a focused host's detailed paths.

## Controls and rendering
- Canvas controls expand or collapse all logical groups in one compact reflow. They preserve the selected visible object, or its enclosing group when hidden,   and never create a document version. Large-graph   qualification measures actual host counts, including groups of ten   so a thousand-host fixture never silently measures only aggregate cards.

sections.title: Contract

## Reading surface
The window uses the theme's main reading surface continuously across its titlebar, transcript and composer surroundings. A subtle border and shadow frame compact readable message spacing; canvas nodes must not bleed through reply text.

End padding keeps the final choice fully readable when scrolled to the bottom; the action controls remain outside the fade.

## Actions and continuity
Less frequent actions live in the More menu: new conversation, settings, subagents, available Computer actions and opening the full conversation.

Messages, tool disclosures, questions, approvals and errors remain canonical.

Existing canvases open the combined window directly.

concepts.summary: Heavy navigation acknowledges selection synchronously, commits target visibility after that intent can paint, then performs focus, resize, scroll or measurement after content paint. Published Floe separates visual from committed values; Redeven applies this ordering across Activity, Workbench, terminal, Flower, Files/Git and heavy panels without duplicating business state.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
Initialization, persisted restoration, permission correction, automatic open and recovery use synchronous canonical commitment such as `commitNow()`. Genuinely blocking operations keep their dedicated presentation.

## Activity and retained content
Activity uses Shell UI-first mode and after-paint activation. Files preserves hidden virtual-grid measurements, usable width/range/scroll. Flower keeps the previous transcript during cold selection and replaces it only when the latest destination is ready.

## Measurement
Debug Console groups presentation events by surface/source. User interactions must avoid renderer tasks/frame gaps of 50 ms or more. Instrumentation flags intent at 32 ms and content at 100 ms; focused performance/browser gates enforce distributions and long-task limits.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
UI-first scheduling is not permission to duplicate canonical state or create a second business model.

Explicit environment replacement, permission-root replacement, connection recovery, resource-pressure policy already owned by the relevant subsystem, and user-requested closure may establish separate lifecycle boundaries; a navigation click alone may not.

frontmatter.title: Workbench terminal interaction

concepts.summary: Floeterm terminal-go owns PTY, native VT, geometry, controller epoch, semantic history and atomic Presentation. Released terminal-web renders one canvas per view and collects local input. Authority/renderer violations fail closed; auxiliary history or search errors stay local and retryable without disconnecting live output.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## One terminal owner and one view renderer
One `SessionActor` owns each session; sequence and geometry generation only advance. Every view receives the same authoritative Presentation with canonical dimensions. Paint complete backgrounds before cells, graphics, selection and cursor to avoid stale edges during resize, activation or theme changes.

## Multi-view geometry and controller ownership
Published Floeterm owns attachment arbitration and geometry. Browser views never parse output bytes, own history or create hidden renderers.

## Product footer placement
[Activity companion](flower-activity-companion.md#activity-terminal-footer) owns the Activity-only measured footer entry. Workbench supplies none. Layout cannot attach a view, request control or intercept terminal input.

## Input, links, selection, and mobile interaction
`TerminalInputBridge` sends confirmed Unicode once, structured key intents to the native encoder and clipboard paste through its bounded interaction. Script/malformed URLs, stale capabilities and remote paths fail closed.

## Clear, history, refresh, and lifecycle
Clear is the actor's semantic reset, never canvas erasure, Ctrl-L, recreation or detach; stale generations have no effect. Close/delete removes catalog, attachments and capabilities; stale notifications cannot resurrect sessions.

## Product lifecycle and performance
Dormant sessions remain metadata-only and the catalog renderer-free. Ask Flower captures selection or bounded visible semantic text; working directory requires current local-path capability.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Redeven may adapt Flowersec streams, product permissions, local-path capability, responsive placement, notifications, and Desktop URL/file actions. It must not recreate terminal parsing, key encoding, history ownership, attachment arbitration, canonical geometry, semantic frame encoding, cursor state, graphics state, or renderer internals. Local sibling dependencies, raw-byte fallbacks, hidden renderers, automatic reattach on ordinary resize, error swallowing, and sequence rollback are prohibited.

## Activity presentation
The existing canonical active/running/idle state and the persisted activity indicator preference remain authoritative. Opaque widget bodies and neutral static shadows do not change during activation, dragging, or resizing.
